Zann frowned. "Everything sounds too dangerous to you," he snapped.
"Especially when it's my parents who are missing instead of yours!"
Gliss gasped, and tears came to her eyes. "I—I have to go," she mumbled.
Snapping her fingers, she zapped out of sight.
"Zann!" Perda scowled at him. "That was mean!"
"Gliss was just worried about you," Darb added. He glanced at Perda.
"Will you take me to check on her?"
"Sure." Perda grabbed Darb's hand. "Zap!"
They disappeared, leaving Zann alone with Zing.
Zann felt guilty for hurting Gliss' feelings.
But he did his best to shake off his guilt.
In a few days he would be stuck at school.
This could be his last chance to come up with a plan to find his parents.
If his friends didn't want to help, he would do it on his own.
Two days later Zann was no closer to a plan.
He'd researched the locations of all the known wormholes in Magica, but they were all far away from Swamp Bottom.
Zapping to any of those wormholes would use up all his energy, leaving little or no energy to navigate through the vortex.
He would have to rest for at least a day first.
That would give Boz enough time to notice Zann was missing, figure out what was going on, and stop Zann from leaving Magica.
The day before school was due to start, Zann zapped to the swamp to meet Darb.
Darb had stopped by earlier to set up a time and place to meet.
But when Zann reached their meeting spot, nobody was there.
That was surprising. Darb was almost always on time. Zann sat down to wait.
A moment later Gliss zapped into view. "Hi, Zann," she said.
Zann jumped to his feet. "What are you doing here?"
"I asked Darb to arrange to meet you so I could talk to you alone," Gliss said.
"You mean you asked him to help you trick me." Zann frowned.
"I'm sorry!" Gliss exclaimed. "But I've been trying to apologize, and you won't—"
Suddenly Perda zapped into view. "Zann!" she cried, her eyes wide and excited.
"I've been looking for you! I need to talk to you—now!"
"No problem," said Zann before Perda had a chance to notice Gliss standing behind her. Grabbing Perda's hand, he said, "Zap!"
They landed in another part of the swamp.
Perda looked confused. "Why did you zap us away?"
"Never mind," Zann said. "What did you want to talk about?"
"Oh!" Perda smiled. "Right. Listen to this—I just found a new wormhole.
And it's right here in Swamp Bottom!"
"You found a wormhole?" Zann exclaimed. "In Swamp Bottom?"
"Uh-huh." Perda looked pleased with herself.
"See, I've been practicing some spells since we got home.
Mostly Seeking spells and a few others." She shrugged.
"I've been thinking I might want to be an explorer someday, so I want to be ready."
Zann was surprised. Since when did Perda want to be an explorer?
But he didn't have time to think about that right now.
"So what happened?" he asked. "How did you find the wormhole?"
"I was using the Seeking spell to find the strongest sources of magic in Swamp Bottom," Perda said.
"Mostly the spell pointed me to the spots I expected—City Hall, your house, the spellstone quarry, places like that.
But there was one source I couldn't identify.
I went and checked it out, and that's when I found the wormhole."
"Wow!" Zann was impressed. Seeking spells were advanced magic—he didn't have any idea how to perform one himself.
"And you're sure it's a wormhole?" he added.
"Of course I'm sure! It's small and kind of unstable-looking.
It's probably brand-new, which is why nobody else has noticed it yet."
Zann's head spun. This changed everything!
"You have to show me," he said.
"I will." Perda smiled. "But only if you'll let me come with you."
"Come with me? You mean, through the wormhole?"
"Yes." Perda's eyes shone with excitement.
"I want to see what the vortex is like.
I want to help you search all those other worlds."
Zann shook his head. "I can't let you come. It's too dangerous!"
Perda folded her arms. "I don't care if it's dangerous.
That's my deal. Take it or leave it."
Zann bit his lip. For a second he was tempted to agree to her deal.
Perda was smart and brave and good at magic.
It could be helpful to have her along.
Then Zann remembered all the adventures they'd been through together lately.
No, he couldn't put Perda in that kind of danger again.
This was his quest, and he should be the only one to take the risks.
Still, he couldn't pass up this chance to find a wormhole close to home.
"It's a deal," he said, trying to sound sincere. "You can come along."
"Cool!" Perda grinned.
Zann forced a smile, though he already felt guilty. He hated lying to Perda.
And he knew she was going to be furious when she figured out that he'd tricked her.
But what other choice did he have?
He just had to hope that she would forgive him someday.
"Let's go check out the wormhole," he said.
"Right now?" She sounded surprised. "Shouldn't we gather some supplies first?
Professor Huli says some other worlds don't have the same kind of magic we do.
So we can't count on just creating anything we need, like food or extra clothes."
"Oh, we aren't going right now." Zann thought fast.
"We should go tomorrow after school. That will give us plenty of time to gather supplies."
"Tomorrow?" Perda frowned. "Why not later today?"
"Um, well, it might take some time to find the supplies we need. We don't want to rush."
Perda didn't say anything for a second. Zann held his breath.
He needed her to think they were really going tomorrow.
That would give him plenty of time to sneak back to the wormhole later today.
"Okay, I guess that makes sense," she said at last. "We'll go tomorrow."
"Great. Now where is it?"
"It's this way." Perda zapped them both out of the swamp.
They landed on the street a few blocks from Zann's house.
From there they walked to a wooded area at the edge of town.
In the middle of a small clearing was a ripple of magic energy.
When Zann and Perda stepped closer, it opened into a wormhole!
"Wow," Zann said, staring at it.
It was small, just as Perda had said—much smaller than the ones in First City.
The edges sparked and swirled wildly, and the opening changed size and shape every few seconds.
Zann jumped back as the wormhole let out a small burst of magic energy, sucking in some fallen leaves.
Perda took a step closer. "Are you sure you don't want to go today?"
"I'm sure," Zann said quickly. "Let's each pack a bag to take with us, and then hide the bags in the swamp.
We can meet there after school tomorrow."
"Zann! Come here, please!" Boz called.
Zann was in his room stuffing things into a backpack.
He shoved it under his bed and hurried out of the room.
Boz was standing near the front door.
"What is it?" Zann tried to sound normal even though he was nervous.
Could Boz have figured out what was going on?
But Boz looked distracted, as usual lately.
"I have a meeting with the mayor," he said. "But I'll be home for dinner."
"Okay," Zann said. "I'll see you then."
"Good." Boz smiled at him. "We've both been so busy since returning from the capital that I feel I've hardly seen you.
Perhaps we can finally have that talk this evening."
Boz zapped out of sight, and Zann slumped with relief.
This could be his chance to go back to that wormhole.
He just had one thing to do first.
"Come on, boy." Zann whistled for Zing. "Let's go see Darb."
Zing stared at him and let out a puff of smoke.
But the dragon stayed where he was.
"What's wrong with you?" Zann said impatiently, grabbing Zing. "Let's go!"
Zann snapped his fingers and zapped out of the house.
Once Zing was safe with Darb, there would be nothing standing in Zann's way.
When Zann arrived at the swamp, Darb was waiting. So was Gliss.
Zann was still mad at Gliss. But he tried not to let those feelings show.
After today he might not see his friends for a long time.
In fact, he might never see them again.
He didn't want to leave on bad terms.
Gliss smiled uncertainly. "Hi, Zann."
"Hi, Gliss." Zann smiled back briefly. Then he turned toward Darb.
"I need a favor. Can you watch Zing for a few hours?"
"Sure," Darb said. "Why? What's up?"
"Right before the trouble with Morb started, I told Professor Nurt I'd do some extra credit work for Food and Drink Creation class," Zann said.
"I need to finish it before school starts tomorrow."
Gliss looked surprised. "I doubt Professor Nurt will care about that," she said.
"Everyone knows you've been kind of busy."
Zann forced a laugh. "I know. But I still want to do it."
"Wow." Darb grinned. "Saving Magica must have changed you, Zann.
You never cared that much about schoolwork before."
"Ha-ha, very funny." Zann was nervous. Were his friends suspicious?
Maybe he should have thought of a different cover story.
"Anyway, it will be easier to create puffberry soufflés without Zing there trying to eat them."
"No problem." Darb gave Zing a pat. "We'll have fun. Right, buddy?"
Usually Zing loved spending time with Darb.
But today he ignored him, staying pressed against Zann's leg.
"What's wrong with him?" Gliss wondered.
"Nothing." Zann gave Zing a nudge. "Go with Darb, boy."
The dragon whined and emitted a puff of smoke.
Zing refused to leave Zann's side even when Darb called him.
Finally Zann snapped his fingers and created a dragon harness.
He slipped it onto Zing's scaly body and then handed the leash to Darb.
"I'm sure he'll be fine once I'm gone.
He's just annoyed because he knows he'll be missing all those soufflés."
Darb chuckled. "You're probably right." But he looked concerned as he glanced at Zing.
Zann didn't want to give his friends the chance to ask any more questions.
"Thanks," he said. "See you in a few hours." He zapped home.
Soon he was stepping out of his room with his backpack strapped onto his shoulders.
He reached into his pocket to make sure the message stone was there.
As he touched its cool, hard surface, he shivered. What was he getting himself into?
But he couldn't lose his nerve now.
After taking one last look around the house, Zann hurried outside.
He'd already decided to walk to the wormhole instead of zapping there.
It wasn't far, and he would need all his energy for navigating the vortex.
Just as he reached the clearing, the wormhole let out a magical burp that rattled the branches of nearby trees and made Zann jump.
Could he really do this?
"Yes," he whispered. "I have to do it."
Taking a deep breath, Zann stepped toward the wormhole.
Its ragged mouth opened wider, and its chaotic energy reached out and began to suck him in.
"Zann!" someone shouted. It was Perda, and she sounded angry.
"You didn't think you really tricked me with that pathetic story, did you?"
Zann tried to pull away from the wormhole. But its pull was too strong.
"Perda, no! You have to get back!"
"No way." Perda rubbed her fingers together with one hand while she grabbed Zann's wrist with the other.
A second later a glowing band of energy appeared, linking their wrists together.
"A Shackle spell?" Zann blurted out. "Where'd you learn to do that?"
"I'm full of surprises." She smirked, tugging at the magical shackles to test them. "Now you can't leave me behind!"
Zann gritted his teeth, trying again to escape the wormhole's pull.
But it was no use. It was all he could do to stay where he was.
He had to convince Perda to back off before she got sucked in too!
"Listen," he said. "I didn't want to lie to you, but—"
"Then why did you?" she shot back.
"Perda, I—" Before he could go on, Gliss burst into view.
"Oh no!" she cried as she saw the wormhole.
"What are you two doing? Are you crazy?"
Zann glared at Perda. "Did you tell everyone I was here?"
"I didn't tell anyone," Perda said. "I don't know what she's doing here."
"I zapped to your house, Zann." Gliss took a step closer while keeping a wary eye on the wormhole.
"I wanted to talk to you. I saw you rushing off down the street, so I followed.
Now I'm glad I did. You can't do this—it's way too dangerous!"
"Too late," Perda said. "We're going, and you can't stop us!"
Gliss frowned. "Oh yeah?" She stepped forward and grabbed Perda's free arm, trying to drag her back. "Don't be stupid!"
"Get back!" Zann was still struggling to hold his position.
"The wormhole's energy is too strong. You'll get sucked in with us!"
Just then he heard a familiar whistle. Zing!
The dragon flew at Zann with a blast of irritated flame. His harness was trailing behind him.
"Zing, no!" Perda exclaimed, ducking her head to avoid the fire.
"Zing! Where are you going?" Darb called, rushing into sight.
He gasped when he saw what was happening.
"Hurry!" Gliss called to Darb. "Help me pull Zann and Perda out!"
Darb jumped forward, grabbing onto Gliss. At the same time, Zing latched onto Zann's backpack with his claws.
Zann felt the wormhole's hold on him loosen slightly.
"Fine, I give up!" Zann called. "Everyone pull back together, and—"
Whoosh! Energy suddenly expanded and contracted, sucking the whole group into the wormhole's gaping mouth.
"Zann! Is that really you?"
Zann turned. A teenage girl he'd never seen before was rushing toward him, grinning widely.
"Uh-oh," Perda whispered. "It's another fan!"
"Perda!" the girl exclaimed. She noticed Zann's pet dragon sniffing at a beetle nearby.
"And Zing! Oh wow—it's an honor to meet you all!"
The girl rubbed her hands together. Flowers rained down on the street all around them.
"They're beautiful," Perda said politely, catching one of the blossoms. "Thank you."
The girl beamed. "No, thank you! You guys saved Magica!"
A few passing pedestrians stopped to see what was going on.
"Look, son," a man told a little boy. "It's Zann and Perda. They're heroes!"
Zann forced a smile as the little boy stared up at him.
It had been less than two days since the grand ceremony celebrating Morb's defeat.
But Zann and his friends were already getting used to attracting attention everywhere they went.
Still, Zann felt a little uncomfortable whenever someone called him a hero.
"We just did what we had to do," he mumbled.
Several people chuckled or clapped their hands to create puffs of colorful magic energy or pretty sparkles.
Zann wondered what his fans would think if they knew he sometimes still thought about Morb's offer.
Zann knew he'd done the right thing by refusing the offer—if he hadn't, Morb would now control Magica.
But Zann still couldn't help wondering . . . Did Morb really know where Zann's parents were?
By now a small crowd had gathered around Zann and Perda.
Thinking about Morb's offer had reminded Zann of today's errand.
"Excuse us," he said. "We have to get going."
"Of course, of course." An older woman beamed at him.
"I'm sure heroes like you have lots of important things to do."
Zann smiled weakly and then hurried off. Perda and Zing followed.
"Slow down!" Perda complained as they raced around a corner.
"Otherwise I'll have to use an Acceleration spell to keep up!"
"Sorry." Zann slowed his pace slightly. "But there's no time to waste.
Who knows how much longer we'll get to stay in First City?"
Perda made a face at the mention of leaving.
"We're lucky the king and queen asked Boz and Gliss' parents to stay for a few days.
Otherwise we'd already be back to our regular lives in boring old Swamp Bottom."
"Yeah." Zann was a little surprised by Perda's words.
Before their adventures had started, Perda seemed content to live in Swamp Bottom.
Zann was the one who had always complained about how boring the town was.
They passed a wall on which someone had scribbled "Voids are Magicians too!" in large letters.
Perda glanced at the graffiti. "Looks like the Void Rights group has been here," she commented.
"At least their messages are polite. Some of the ones from the new anti-Red groups are pretty rude."
Zann nodded, but he wasn't really listening. They'd just reached the university.
"My parents' old lab is this way," he told Perda.
A young woman looked up when they entered the building.
A nameplate on her desk said "Elbi."
"Oh! It's two of the young heroes!" she exclaimed.
Zing spurted out a small blast of flame.
Elbi yanked a potted melody plant out of the way just in time to keep it from getting singed.
"And the dragon." Elbi narrowed her eyes at Zing and frowned.
"Hi," Zann said. "My parents used to run this lab.
Their names are Nax and Asta. Did you know them?"
"Sorry, no." Elbi shrugged. "I've heard of them, of course, but I only started working here two years ago."
"Oh. Well, is Olpa around?"
"No. Olpa and the other senior researchers are all at some big meeting at the palace.
I'm not sure when they'll be back. Should I tell Olpa you were here?"
Zann was disappointed. "Are you sure there's nobody here who knew my parents?"
Elbi looked sympathetic. "Sorry. But listen, I have an idea.
Would you like to see their storage shelf?" She stood up.
"When your parents disappeared, someone put their things there for safekeeping."
"That would be great!" Zann felt a surge of hope.
Could there be clues to his parents' whereabouts on that shelf?
Elbi led the way through the lab.
Being back there after so long felt strange to Zann.
Many things looked the same, but others looked very different. Only a few people were in the main room.
A couple of university students were reading near the bookshelves.
A Void was cleaning a nibbler's cage.
A young researcher was studying a bubbling beaker and scribbling notes.
"Wow, this place is cool!" Perda whispered to Zann, looking around with wide eyes.
"It must be amazing to work here!"
"Yeah, I guess," said Zann, distracted.
He followed Elbi as she opened a closet door.
"It's the middle shelf in the back," Elbi said, rubbing her fingers together to create a light.
As soon as Zann saw the shelf, he was flooded with memories.
There was his mother's favorite hair clip. His father's lab coat.
Even a dragon-shaped paperweight that Zann had given his parents as a gift.
"What's this?" Perda picked up a large metal sculpture.
It was so blackened by fire that the edges were crumbling away.
"I don't know," Zann said. "I've never seen it before."
"It looks kind of like Teplo's pet sniffer goose, doesn't it?" Perda said.
Before Zann could answer, there was an enormous explosion from somewhere in the city.
The building shook, causing some books to fall from the bookshelf. Everyone shouted in surprise.
Zann froze, immediately thinking of Morb and the evil Void's final words: Magica hasn't seen the last of me!
"Hello?" someone shouted from outside. "Come and look!"
The Skellians headed for the door of the hut.
"What are we going to do?" Gliss whispered.
"We can't get back to Magica without a wormhole!"
"We'll figure something out," Zann said, trying to sound confident.
Zann and his friends joined the Skellians at the doorway. Everyone was staring at the beach.
"What's going on?" Perda asked Ello.
"It's the gulpers." Ello pointed. "They're clustering along the shore!
It's weird—they don't usually do that."
Zann squinted through the rain. Several gulpers were splashing around in the shallows.
A few Skellians climbed down the rope ladder for a better look.
"Isn't it dangerous to get too close to those things?" Gliss asked.
"It's okay," Ello replied. "The gulpers can't come onto land. Let's take a look!"
Following Ello, Zann and his friends climbed down to the beach.
That seemed to make the gulpers even more excited.
They churned up the water so much that part of the beach was flooded.
"It's because of our visitors," a woman said, staring at Zann and the others.
"They must give off enough magic energy to attract the gulpers."
"Good thing they can't come on land." Gliss sounded nervous.
"Be careful, Darb! Don't get too close!"
Zann smiled. "Darb is always curious about new creatures," he told Ello.
"I think that's the same gulper that bumped our raft."
Darb pointed to one of the creatures.
"See? I recognize its color and the shape of its eye."
"If you say so," Perda said dubiously. "They all look the same to me."
"I can't see anything in all this rain," Gliss complained.
Snapping her fingers, she conjured up an umbrella.
That caused the gulpers to go into a frenzy.
One even flopped onto the beach, splashing everyone.
"Wow," Zann said. "They definitely noticed that magic you just did, Gliss."
"Yeah." Perda stared at the gulpers with amazement.
"It's almost like we're having our magic tracked by Morb again!"
Until that moment the Skellians had been laughing and pointing at the gulpers, seeming to enjoy the unusual spectacle.
But at Perda's comment, they all became silent.
"What did you say?" one of the women asked Perda.
Perda looked confused. "What? You mean about Morb?
He's just this guy from Magica. It's a long story, but I guess we could tell you . . ."
The Skellians traded serious glances. "I'm sorry," an older man said.
"I'm afraid we cannot welcome you into our village after all. You'll have to leave."
"What?" Perda exclaimed. "Where are we supposed to go?
You just told us there's hardly any land here!"
The man shrugged. "I'm sorry," he said again, though Zann didn't think he sounded very sorry.
Ello looked dismayed. "Rellu, no! You can't turn them away."
"You don't understand, Ello." The man's voice was stern. "Come, let's get inside."
Most of the Skellians turned to leave. But Ello grabbed his mother.
"We can't do this," he said. "I'm sure they're not—"
"Hush, son." His mother shot a nervous look at the visitors.
"What's wrong?" Gliss cried, her chin quivering. "Please! We don't understand."
Ello's mother's expression softened. "Wait here," she said. "Let me talk to Rellu."
She hurried off with Ello at her heels.
"What was that all about?" Darb wondered.
Zann shook his head. "It's like they heard Morb's name and freaked out."
"But how would they know about Morb here?" Perda said.
"Shh," Gliss shushed her. "Here they come."
Ello was hurrying back. "I'm sorry, they're being very stubborn," he said.
"They still won't let you stay with us.
But they said you can stay in the old village for a few days."
"The old village?" Zann said.
"It's this way." Ello led them over a ridge. Then he pointed down a slope.
A single hut stood at the bottom.
The lower halves of its stilts were in the water.
"That's where the village used to be when I was born," Ello explained.
"The waters rose and submerged most of the houses, but that one is still out of reach of the gulpers. You'll be all right there."
"Why did everyone get upset when we mentioned Morb?" Perda asked.
Ello shrugged, looking uncomfortable. "I'd better go," he said.
"The others will need my help cleaning and cooking today's catch." He rushed off.
"That was weird," Darb said.
"Never mind." Gliss shivered. "It's cold out here. Let's get inside."
The hut's interior was damp and moldy.
But Perda created a fire, and Zann conjured up some food.
As they ate, Darb wandered onto a balcony facing the sea.
"The gulpers are swimming near this hut now," he reported. "They must have sensed your magic."
"Let's hope they can't knock the hut off its stilts," Zann joked weakly.
"Or they might swallow us right up!"
Perda glanced out the window. "It's getting darker. It must be almost night."
"How can you tell?" Gliss grimaced. "The rain makes everything so gloomy all the time!
No wonder these people want to escape to other worlds."
Zann yawned. "It's been a long day.
Let's try to get some sleep. Maybe we can figure out a plan tomorrow."
Zann was in the midst of yet another confusing dream about his parents when a shout awakened him.
His eyes popped open, and he sat up.
Ello was standing in the doorway. "A storm is coming!" he said breathlessly.
"Huh?" Gliss mumbled, rubbing her eyes. "So what? It never stops raining here."
"You don't understand!" Ello's voice was urgent.
"This storm is big. It may cause the water to rise again.
If that happens, you'll be cut off from the shore, and at the mercy of the gulpers!"
"What?" Zann cried. "What should we do?"
"I can't stay." Ello was already rushing off.
"Just—please—get yourself to safety!" he called out over his shoulder.
"What are you waiting for?" Gliss exclaimed. "Let's get inland!"
"Wait," Perda said. "I might have a better idea."
Zann noticed that Perda looked thoughtful. "What is it?" he asked.
"I couldn't sleep, so I've been lying here thinking about how we can get off this world," Perda said.
"I may have come up with a plan."
"This is never going to work." Gliss' voice shook as she glanced over the edge of the balcony at the dark, churning sea below. "It's a crazy plan!"
"She's right." Darb sounded doubtful. "Too many things could go wrong.
Maybe we should think about this some more."
Zann glanced down too. The waves were wilder than ever.
He wasn't sure if it was because of the growing storm, or because of the gulpers still swimming below their hut. Probably both.
"I think Perda's plan could work," he said.
"I know it's risky. But it could be our best chance of ever escaping from Skellia."
Perda nodded. "Let's join friction."
She held out her hands. Zann touched his palm to hers.
Then he looked at Gliss and held out his other hand.
She still looked scared. But she joined her palms with the others.
"Stand in the middle of the circle," Zann told Darb. "And hang on to Zing."
Darb nodded. Grabbing the dragon, he ducked under his friends' arms.
"Ready?" Perda closed her eyes. "Protect!"
"Protect!" Zann and Gliss chorused.
Instantly they were surrounded by a glowing orange bubble.
"Let's hope this Shield spell is strong enough," Perda said.
"And let's hope Darb really can tell one gulper from another," Zann added.
"I'm pretty sure I can," Darb said.
"Pretty sure?" Gliss echoed. "Or really sure?"
"Just come on." Perda sounded impatient. "Over to the edge, everyone."
They shuffled to the edge of the balcony, still contained within the Shield bubble. "Wait," Gliss said. "What happens next?"
Perda rolled her eyes. She'd already explained her plan several times.
But when Zann looked at Gliss, he couldn't help feeling sorry for her. She looked really scared.
"We need to find that first gulper," he explained again.
"The one Darb recognized back on the beach."
"Right," Perda continued. "That gulper probably swallowed our wormhole, since it was the first one to arrive after we came through."
"And we already know that even the strongest magic can't destroy a wormhole," Zann went on.
"That means the wormhole will probably still be intact inside the gulper."
"At least for a while." Darb sounded nervous.
"If gulpers feed on magic energy, won't the wormhole be digested eventually?"
"That's why we shouldn't waste any more time talking about it," Perda said. "Let's go! One, two, three . . . Jump!"
As they all leaped off the balcony, Zann held his breath, hoping the Shield spell would hold.
Splash! The glowing bubble sank under the waves, but the water didn't get inside.
"It's working!" Perda cried. "We can still breathe!"
"Look out!" Darb pointed. "A gulper—and it's not the one we want!"
"Away!" Zann yelled, rubbing his hands together.
The bubble bounced away from the gulper.
"More are coming!" Gliss exclaimed.
"We have to find the original gulper," Perda cried. "Darb, do you see it?"
"I'm looking." Darb was peering through the glowing orange wall.
"There! I think that's the original gulper coming at us right now."
"It's going to swallow us!" Gliss shrieked.
"That's the whole idea," Perda reminded her.
But her voice shook a little as she said it.
Zann didn't blame them for being scared.
He felt his own throat go dry with fear as the gulper swam closer, its enormous mouth gaping open, ready to swallow the entire group. Gulp!
"Aah!" Zann cried as they were sucked into the gulper's mouth.
For a moment he couldn't see anything.
The inside of the gulper was dark and slimy.
"It looks like they don't only eat magic," Perda said, wrinkling her nose at the smell.
"They eat fish and other stuff too."
"Does anyone see the wormhole?" Gliss asked.
"There it is!" Darb pointed.
Zann spun around and saw the wormhole glowing in the darkness.
"Hurry!" he cried. "It looks kind of weak already!"
"Quick, everybody join hands," Perda said.
Zann grabbed Perda's hand. She grabbed Gliss' hand, and Gliss grabbed Darb's. Darb picked up Zing.
Then Zann touched the side of the bubble. "Is everybody ready?"
When the others nodded, he muttered, "Dissipate."
He quickly sucked in a deep breath of air as the Shield spell bubble disappeared.
The kids were plunged into watery coldness.
Without the orange glow of the bubble, it was even harder to see.
But the wormhole threw off a faint glow of its own.
Zann kicked his feet, moving himself through the water with his free hand.
Soon he felt the wormhole tugging at him. Its pull was surprisingly strong—so strong that he felt his hand slipping away from Perda's!
"No!" He screamed, accidentally sucking in a mouthful of the disgusting water.
Perda quickly restored the shackles that had bound their arms together back in Magica, and Zann felt his arm clamped safely to hers.
A moment later the wormhole sucked them in, pressing all the breath from their bodies for a second before tossing them into the rushing whirl of the vortex.
As Zann tumbled head over heels, he heard a sharp scream behind him.
He glanced back just in time to see Gliss lose her grip on Perda's hand.
"No!" Gliss shrieked.
A second later she, Darb, and Zing were swept away out of sight!
"No!" Zann yelled. But it was too late. Darb, Gliss, and Zing were gone.
"I couldn't hold on!" Perda cried. "I tried to hold on to Gliss, but I couldn't!"
"I know," Zann said. He was glad Perda had restored the Shackle spell.
Otherwise, his friends might all be gone.
"We have to get out of the vortex. Then we'll figure out what to do."
He glanced around. A wormhole was sliding past, showing a peaceful green meadow.
He lunged for it, but his hand came up empty.
"How do we get through one?" Perda asked.
"I don't know." Zann grabbed for another wormhole and missed again.
"Wyssa got me out the first time. And Zing brought us out into Skellia."
He felt a pang of despair as he said Zing's name.
Would he ever see his fiery little buddy again? Or Darb, his best friend?
Or Gliss, whom he'd accidentally dragged into danger yet again?
Zann tried not to think about it.
"Zing got us out when he tried to grab that fish he saw.
He spotted it through the Skellia wormhole and really jumped at it.
Hang on. I'm going to try harder for the next one."
"Okay. But even if that works, how will we know which world we're entering?" Perda wondered.
"We won't. But anywhere has got to be better than here, right?" Zann glanced forward. "Hold on!"
He hurled himself toward the next wormhole.
This time he felt his fingers latch onto the edge of the wormhole. Its magic energy burned his hand.
"Ouch!" he cried, letting go. He caught a glimpse of a gleaming city as he tumbled away. "Drat!"
"What happened?" Perda asked.
"Nothing. I'll try again in a second."
This time Zann vowed not to let go, no matter what.
He lunged at the next wormhole. His fingers caught the edge, and he ignored the magical burn, pulling himself forward.
"Oof!" he said as he slid through the wormhole and fell flat on his face on the other side.
Perda landed beside him. "You did it!" she said. "Now, where are we?"
"I don't know. But at least it's dry." Zann looked around.
They had landed on an open plain surrounded by a dark forest.
A flash of lightning lit up the sky.
Strange lights flickered on and off, and strange sounds came from every direction.
The air crackled with strong magical energy.
"Where are we?" Perda asked again. This time she sounded a little nervous.
Zann climbed to his feet and then helped Perda up.
She undid the Shackle spell to release his arm.
"Come on," said Zann. "Let's—"
"Look out!" Perda shouted, yanking him back as the ground opened up at their feet.
They jumped backward as the opening grew bigger, emitting a blast of energy that sizzled several nearby trees into burnt stumps.
A second later the ground closed again.
"Let's get away from here," Perda said, backing away toward a cluster of trees.
"Stop!" Zann cried. One of the trees was reaching toward Perda, its branches snaking out like tentacles.
Zann grabbed her and dragged her out of range just in time.
He didn't stop until they were in the open, well away from any of the trees.
"What's wrong with this world?" Perda said, looking worried and confused.
Zann didn't answer for a second. He was staring at something passing by on the far side of the plain.
Something huge and hairy. It looked like a giant spider, but with ten legs and three long, curved teeth sticking out from its mouth.
"I think I just figured it out." He pointed at the creature, which was too far away to notice them.
"See that? I think it's a deca-stinger.
I recognize it from one of my parents' books—Creatures of the Known Magical Worlds."
"S—so this is a known magical world?" Perda asked. "Which one?"
Zann gulped. "I think it's . . . Fardark."
"Fardark?" Perda echoed. "Oh boy."
Zann knew exactly how she felt. Fardark was known for its dark magic and dangerous creatures.
Zann tried to remember what else he'd read about Fardark, but he was soon interrupted.
"Look out!" Perda cried, pointing up.
Zann glanced up. A huge dragon was flying down toward them, its claws bared.
Boiling droplets fell from its mouth like hail, leaving burned spots sizzling all around Zann and Perda.
Zann raised his hand to throw up a Shield spell, but realized it was no use.
Once again the vortex had drained most of their energy.
Their magic might not be strong enough to protect them.
"Run!" Zann yelled.
He grabbed Perda's hand and sprinted across the plain.
The dragon turned and came at them again.
This time Zann heard Perda cry out as one of the droplets burned her arm, leaving a red mark.
"This way!" Zann pulled her toward the trees.
They would just have to hope they weren't the same kind of trees that had tried to grab them.
As lightning flashed again, he spotted a hollow tree trunk just ahead.
Pulling Perda with him, he ducked into it.
A rain of sizzling droplets burned the earth around them.
"Did that dragon see us hide in here?" Perda whispered, peering out.
"I don't know." Zann looked out too.
The dragon landed with a thud, its red eyes searching the darkness and its nostrils sniffing the air.
Suddenly there was a wail. A second later the deca-stinger appeared and flung itself onto the dragon!
The two huge beasts rolled in the dirt, clawing each other and howling.
"This could be our chance!" Zann whispered.
"Let's get out of here while they're both distracted."
Zann and Perda scurried out of the tree trunk.
The forest was dark and spooky, and Zann didn't want to go any deeper into it.
Besides, he didn't want to get too far from the wormhole.
"Look, a cave!" Perda pointed. "Let's hide in there."
At the cave's entrance, Zann used the small amount of energy he had left to do a quick Life Force Locator spell.
The cave was empty, so he and Perda huddled inside.
As the two monsters continued to fight outside, Zann and Perda caught their breath and talked about what had happened.
"Did you see whether Darb, Gliss, and Zing stayed together?" Zann asked.
"I couldn't tell." Perda looked worried. "If Darb gets separated from Gliss . . ."
"I know. Without magic, he'd be helpless in the vortex."
Zann's mind flashed again to Venna. What had become of her? And what about Morb?
Without his stolen magic, he was a Void, just like Darb.
"We need to figure out how to find them," Perda said. "Fast!"
"How?" Zann glanced out of the cave.
"Even if we can make it past those two monsters and back to the wormhole, we can't even navigate our way through the vortex.
Let alone find our friends." He looked at Perda.
"I can't believe I dragged you all into this," he mumbled.
Perda shrugged. "You didn't drag me—I wanted to come."
Zann gave a small chuckle. "Well, we've both said we want to be explorers. Now here we are—exploring."
Perda peered out from the cave and then smiled. "Look! They're running off!"
Zann looked out. The battling monsters had stopped fighting and were now racing away in opposite directions.
"That's weird," he said. "I wonder why they're leaving."
"Who cares?" said Perda. "This could be our chance to get back to the wormhole."
She crawled out of the cave. "Come on!"
They raced out of the forest and across the dark plain, dodging random bursts of energy.
Zann could see the wormhole winking at them just ahead.
Being in the vortex was pretty scary.
But they'd just discovered that certain worlds were even scarier.
"Hurry!" he called to Perda. "We have to—argh!"
Zann suddenly felt a stinging sensation, as if he were being stuck with burning needles all over his body.
He fell to the ground, twitching and groaning.
"What's happening?" Perda cried in a shaky voice.
Out of the corner of his eye, Zann saw her fall, twitching, beside him.
Then a new creature stepped into view.
It was much smaller than the dragon or the deca-stinger—in fact, it wasn't much bigger than Zing.
It didn't look very scary either. It resembled a hairy walking mop.
Even so, Zann shivered when he saw it. "Oh no," he said. "It's a scatter beast!"
"That's a scatter beast?" Perda said. "The thing that knocked your parents off course?"
Zann couldn't answer. As the scatter beast crept closer, the stinging sensations grew worse.
Besides, Zann didn't know much more about scatter beasts than Perda did.
All he knew was that they threw off chaotic energy that confused the magic of others.
He struggled to regain control of his body, but it was no use.
The scatter beast was still approaching. A skinny tentacle appeared from amid the dirty, grayish hair and stretched toward the kids.
Zann could only stare at it, mesmerized by the spiral-shaped claw at the end.
"We have to get away!" Perda cried. She rubbed her hands together. "Blast!"
A small sizzle of energy spit out of her hand.
It made it halfway to the scatter beast before suddenly doubling back toward the kids.
At the same time, it swelled into a fireball.
"Look out!" Zann yelled, throwing himself aside.
Perda rolled away just in time too.
The fireball blasted a large hole in the rocky ground between them.
Zann tried to turn to make sure Perda was okay.
But he couldn't move anymore. He realized he'd thrown himself even closer to the scatter beast.
All Zann could do now was stare helplessly as the creature moved toward him, its claw aimed at his forehead.
Zann knew he should be scared. After all, he was about to die.
But instead the only thing he felt was regret.
He regretted that he would never find his parents, that Boz would never know what had happened to him,
and that he'd never have the chance to make up with Gliss—or even find out if she and the others had survived . . .
Then, out of the corner of his eye, he noticed something strange.
A sparkling rain of colorful glitter was falling gently from the sky, seemingly out of nowhere.
At first Zann assumed it was an illusion, that the scatter beast's energy was affecting his vision.
Then the first bits of glitter touched the scatter beast.
They sizzled and burned some of its fur, causing the beast to jump back and howl with pain.
Its wild energy went even wilder, sparking fires here and there and making the ground shudder.
"Huh?" Zann mumbled through numb lips.
Then he felt someone grab him by the arm and drag him across the hard, rocky ground.
A moment later he felt the increasingly familiar sensation of passing through a wormhole.
The vortex felt almost welcoming after Fardark.
When he felt Perda bump against him, Zann was relieved.
They'd both made it out. But who had rescued them?
"That was close," an irritated voice snapped.
"I thought I warned you about the wormholes, boy."
Zann blinked, his vision swimming back into focus.
He gasped as he finally got a good look at the person who had grabbed him.
It was Wyssa!
"W—Wyssa?" Zann stammered. His lips were still numb from the scatter beast's attack. "How did you—?"
"Save your energy, boy." Wyssa sounded irritated.
"The more you talk, the more you slow us down. Now, where are the others?"
Perda gasped. "This is the old woman we spoke with in Wormwood! She's Wyssa?"
"Yes," Zann said. The effects of the scatter beast's magic were wearing off.
But being in the vortex still made it hard to think clearly.
"How did you find us?" he asked Wyssa.
"How did you even know to look for us?"
"I have my ways," Wyssa said. "Now we need to get you kids back to Magica. Where are your friends?"
"Back to Magica?" Zann immediately thought about his parents.
He couldn't go home until he'd found them!
"You can do that?" Perda sounded relieved. "You can get us home?"
"Of course," Wyssa snapped. "But where are the others?
There should be another Red with you. A girl, yes? And the young Void?"
Zann felt his heart sink as he thought about Gliss, Darb, and Zing.
"They're gone," he said. "We got separated in the vortex earlier.
I don't know where they are now."
"What?" Wyssa snapped. She yanked at Zann's arm so hard that he cried out in surprise.
He felt his body being sucked through another wormhole.
A moment later he, Wyssa, and Perda were standing on a cliff overlooking a rough sea.
Cold wind whipped around them, and strange gray birds circled overhead, letting out shrill cries.
But Wyssa didn't seem to notice any of that. She was glaring at Zann.
"Let me make sure I understand this," Wyssa said.
"You brought your friends into the vortex.
Then you lost track of two of them?"
"Three, actually," Zann admitted. "Zing, my pet dragon, was with them too."
"You found us," Perda said. "Can't you find them too?"
Wyssa glanced at her. "It's not that easy, girl."
"Perda," Perda said. "My name is Perda. Not 'girl.'"
Wyssa gnashed her teeth, and Zann cringed.
He didn't want Wyssa and Perda to start arguing.
Not when his friends were still missing.
"How did you find us?" he asked Wyssa.
"Maybe you can find Darb and Gliss the same way."
"As I said, it's not that easy." Wyssa paced back and forth along the cliff's edge.
"The Interworld Tracking spell I used to find you is complicated.
To do it, you need an object that has some of the lost person's magic energy."
Perda folded her arms. "I've never heard of a spell like that."
"There are whole worlds out there you've never heard of, girl," Wyssa told her. "That doesn't mean they don't exist."
"So you tracked our magic energy?" Zann asked. "Mine and Perda's? How?"
"Not hers—just yours." Wyssa stopped pacing. "I used this."
She reached into the folds of her cloak and pulled out a small object. Zann recognized it right away.
"That's a chew toy I created for Zing yesterday," he said. "How did you get that?"
Wyssa tucked the chew toy away.
"Since you created it so recently, it still contains traces of your magic energy," she said, without answering Zann's question.
"I was able to use it to track you through the vortex and into Fardark."
Zann shivered, but only partly because of the cold wind.
Hearing the name "Fardark" reminded Zann of his visit with Perda to that dark and dreadful world.
"Thanks for saving us," he said. "But can't you use that chew toy to track Zing? He drooled all over it."
"The spell doesn't work that way." Wyssa frowned.
"It requires magic energy, not dragon drool."
"You said you can get us back to Magica, right?" Perda said.
"I'm sure we could find something Gliss created there."
"That would take much too long." Wyssa started pacing again.
"Your friends could be in grave danger, alone in the vortex."
"Then what are we going to do?" Perda cried. "We have to find our friends!"
Zann could only nod. His throat was too dry to speak.
He couldn't believe he'd accidentally led his friends into danger again.
If they were lost in the vortex forever, it was his fault!
Wyssa stopped pacing and looked down at the ground.
She appeared to be deep in thought.
A minute later she looked up. "I have an idea. Come."
She grabbed Zann and Perda and yanked them through the wormhole.
Soon all three of them were rushing through the vortex again.
"What's your plan?" Zann asked.
"I know how to make a potion that will show me which wormholes have been used recently," Wyssa replied.
"If your friends managed to get through one and into another world, I might be able to track them."
"Great," Perda said. "But what if they haven't gone through a wormhole?"
"Yeah, what if they're still in the vortex?" Zann added.
"It's not easy to grab one of those wormholes, you know."
Wyssa shrugged. "Let's just hope they have gotten out by now," she said.
Zann gulped, afraid to ask what she meant.
Still, he was glad that she had a plan.
First they needed to find Darb, Gliss, and Zing.
Then Zann needed to figure out a way to keep searching for his parents—without dragging his friends into more danger.
"Hold on," Wyssa said. "I need to find a world that contains the ingredients for my—"
Zann gasped, not hearing any more of what she was saying.
As he slid past another wormhole, an image of his parents' terrified faces flashed through his mind.
The vision was just like the horrible nightmares he'd been having about his mother and father.
Only this time Zann was wide awake!
Zann screamed as the fire consumed his arm.
Hoping to create more friction, he started to rub his other hand against his side.
"Stop!" Wyssa's harsh voice rang out.
A moment later the fire was gone.
Zann felt Wyssa touch his hand and arm, and the pain disappeared.
"What happened?" Perda asked. "Why is it so dark here?"
A cool white flame appeared in Wyssa's hands.
Wyssa dropped it on the ground, and it spread to surround her, Zann, and Perda so they could see one another clearly.
"You'll need to be careful here," Wyssa said. Her voice was calm now.
"Galvan is a land of extra-strong magic energy.
Any magic you perform will be greatly intensified, often in unpredictable ways."
Zann could still hear a buzzing sound.
Now he realized it was the steady hum of magic energy.
"Let me try some magic." Perda sounded intrigued.
She snapped her fingers. A cup of airberry juice appeared in her hand. "There," she said. "That didn't—"
She gasped as the airberry juice expanded and flowed over the edge of the cup like a fountain.
Soon all three of them were drenched.
"No more magic!" Wyssa snapped. She waved her hand, and the airberry juice disappeared.
"Wow," Perda said. "Just imagine what someone with Morb's powers could do in a place like this!"
Wyssa glared at her. Zann wasn't sure if that was because of the airberry juice stunt, or because Perda had mentioned Morb's name.
"Don't do any magic, either of you," Wyssa said sternly. "Leave it to me."
"Okay," Zann said. "Now, how are we supposed to figure out whether our friends are here?"
"I'm going to do a Seeking spell," Wyssa said. "Join hands."
Zann took Perda's hand and then reached for Wyssa's.
Wyssa grabbed his wrist with one hand and snapped her fingers.
A second later all three of them were yanked off their feet and flying through the air.
"Whoa!" Perda yelled. "What's happening?"
"It's the Seeking spell," Zann called back.
They were moving so fast he couldn't see a thing.
"The intense magic here must be affecting the spell, like Wyssa said.
It's pulling us toward the others! That means they're definitely here, right?"
"Not necessarily," Wyssa replied. "A Seeking spell can't be used to find one particular person.
Don't they teach you anything in those Magica schools?"
"We haven't really done Seeking spells yet," Perda said. "At least not in school."
"Well, we're Seeking anything from Magica," Wyssa explained.
"The spell could be leading us to your friends, or—oh!"
They flew through the doorway of a small cottage and came to a sudden stop.
A short man with large ears and feet was staring at them with a look of total surprise.
"Zann!" Perda pointed toward a table. "It's your parents' book—Creatures of the Known Magical Worlds!"
Zann gasped. "What's that doing here?"
Wyssa smiled at the strange little man. "Greetings, Fud," she said.
"I should have realized where my Seeking spell was leading us."
Fud smiled and clasped her hand. "Wyssa! What a wonderful surprise!"
Zann was pretty surprised too. First the Niffians had greeted Wyssa like an old friend, and now Fud was doing the same.
Until now Zann hadn't thought of Wyssa as the type of person who had many friends. Or any friends, really.
"Where did you get this?" Zann asked Fud, picking up the book.
"Wyssa brought it to me," Fud replied.
"She knows of my interest in other worlds."
"Have you visited many of the worlds in the book?" asked Perda.
"Sadly, I've visited none of them," Fud said with a wry smile.
"We Galvanites can barely manage to feed ourselves with our weak magic.
I'd have little chance of surviving the vortex."
"Really?" Zann said. "But this world has such strong magic energy!"
"That's true," Wyssa said. "And as you saw "—she glared at Perda—"it can be dangerous to perform magic in such a place.
The Galvanites have evolved to avoid that danger."
She went on to tell Fud about their search for Darb, Gliss, and Zing.
"Oh, dear," Fud said. "I'll send out a message to see if they've been spotted."
With the others following, he hurried outside.
"If these people don't have much magic, how can he send a message?" Perda wondered.
"Just watch," Wyssa said.
Fud began stomping his large bare feet on the ground.
The sound echoed like a drumbeat as the constant magic energy caught it.
Soon the rhythm was vibrating all around Zann and the others. Before long they heard another rhythm.
"Is that someone answering?" Zann asked.
"Yes." Fud frowned with concentration as he listened. "And here comes another response."
For the next few minutes, more and more drumbeats came from all directions. Finally, though, Fud shook his head.
"I'm sorry," he said, "but it seems nobody has seen your friends."
"That means they're likely not in Galvan," Wyssa said with a sigh.
"Especially since my Seeking spell didn't find them either.
Thank you, Fud. We'd better get back to the wormhole."
"Please visit again soon," Fud urged her.
"I will, my friend." Wyssa grabbed Zann and Perda. "Zap!"
Splash!
"Drat!" Zann had landed in a muddy stream, and his legs were soaked.
"This doesn't look like the right spot," Perda said.
She and Wyssa had landed on the stream bank. "Where's the wormhole?"
Wyssa shrugged. "As I said, magic can be unpredictable here."
Zann climbed out of the stream and rubbed his hands, automatically conjuring dry pants and shoes.
A second later he was wrapped in reams of heavy fabric from head to toe. "Help!" he gasped. "I can't breathe!"
Zann struggled for breath as the fabric completely enveloped everyone.
"Don't you ever listen, boy?" Wyssa's muffled voice came from nearby.
"I'd better get us out of Galvan before you kill us all."
Zann felt a hand grab him. Zap! He landed in front of the Galvan wormhole.
"Nice work, Zann," Perda said breathlessly, as Wyssa dragged them into the wormhole. "You almost smothered us!"
"Sorry," Zann mumbled.
Once again they were speeding through the vortex.
"How many magical worlds are there, anyway?" asked Perda.
"Nobody knows," Wyssa replied. "The nature of wormholes makes it impossible to know for sure."
"My parents said that hundreds of worlds have been cataloged already," Zann said.
"But more are being discovered all the time."
He thought about World X. His parents had contacted Wyssa for help in finding it. Did she know where it was?
He opened his mouth to ask. But a flash of purple light distracted him.
The symbols on Wyssa's hands were glowing again.
"Oh no," Wyssa muttered when she saw the next wormhole.
Whatever world the wormhole led to, Zann could tell she wasn't happy about going through it.
He soon landed on something soft and squishy.
Looking around, Zann could see that they were standing on a puffy white cloud floating peacefully in a clear golden sky.
Dozens of similar clouds surrounded them.
"I feel as light as a dragon's scale!" Perda exclaimed.
Zann felt the same way. He jumped and found himself floating up surprisingly high before floating gently back down to the cloud.
Perda did a somersault in the air. "Look at me! I'm flying!" she cried.
"Settle down, both of you." Wyssa's voice was stern.
"We need to figure out whether your friends are here. Quickly."
"Okay, okay." Perda sat down on a fluffy patch of cloud. "How do we do that?"
"I'm thinking," Wyssa said sharply. "Just be quiet for a moment."
Zann bounced gently, still looking around. "Hey, look at that," he said, pointing at a cloud far overhead.
It was dark and stormy, with lightning flickering through it every few seconds.
It definitely stood out in the otherwise pale and peaceful sky.
"I said, be quiet, boy!" Wyssa barked.
Her face looked pinched and anxious. Before Zann could ask what was wrong, he noticed a new cloud zooming toward them.
This one looked oddly glittery. When it came closer, he gasped.
"It's a whole flock of those little stinging dragons that Morb brought to Magica!" he cried.
"They're called flizzes," Wyssa said. "They're very useful as long as you know how to control them."
Zann recalled the painful stings he and Darb had received from the flizzes.
He conjured a sturdy stick to use as a weapon if the creatures came any closer.
"You won't need that," Wyssa said with a faint smile.
"I know exactly how to control flizzes.
I'm the one who brought them to Morb."
Zann wanted to ask how many other dangerous creatures Wyssa had brought to Morb.
But before he could speak, his mouth widened into a sudden yawn.
Lowering the stick, he sank onto the soft, welcoming cloud.
He watched the flizzes gather around Wyssa, who began speaking softly to them in a language Zann didn't understand.
Beside him Perda yawned as well. "It's been a long day, hasn't it?" she mumbled.
"I think I'll just close my eyes for a second."
Zann was drifting off to sleep too when he heard a soft snore.
Opening his eyes, he was surprised to see Perda floating.
Above them both was the dark cloud. It appeared much closer than before.
"Weird," he mumbled.
Wyssa heard him and looked over. "Oh dear," she muttered.
"They're succumbing even faster than I'd feared."
Glancing at the flizzes, she waved her hand. "Go! And hurry!"
Zann watched the flizzes speed off. "Where . . . Where are they . . . ?" Zann paused.
What had he been planning to ask? He couldn't remember. "Oh well," he mumbled. "Doesn't matter."
He felt himself floating upward, as Perda was doing.
It seemed like too much trouble to resist, so he didn't. Besides, floating felt kind of nice.
The stick felt heavy in his hand.
He let it go, watching through half-closed eyes as it drifted slowly upward.
Suddenly Zann felt a yank. Wyssa was pulling him back down.
"Wake up!" she ordered loudly. "You too, girl!"
The old woman bounced away and grabbed Perda, pulling her over to Zann's cloud.
Perda opened her eyes. "What's going on?"
Now Zann was falling back to sleep.
Breathing desperately, Wyssa gave him a good kick to the shin.
"Ow," Zann mumbled, scooting away from her foot.
"I just want a quick nap, that's all."
"You must fight it!" cried Wyssa. "Do not fall asleep!"
Zann looked at her with half-closed eyes. "Did you say something?"
He heard a snore and saw Wyssa turn her head quickly. Perda was floating upward again.
The dark cloud was very close now.
"Wake . . . up," said Wyssa, pinching Perda. The old woman was beginning to sound sleepy herself.
"Stop," Perda protested weakly.
Zann noticed his stick was getting closer and closer to the dark cloud, which was now directly above him.
He closed his eyes and felt his body move up off his cloud once more.
Nearby he heard Wyssa mumbling. "If the flizzes don't return soon, we'll have to . . ."
She slowly closed her eyes and drifted into sleep.
Zann smiled. "This is so relaxing. I could stay . . . here . . . forever."
Suddenly a bolt of magic energy shot from the dark cloud, obliterating Zann's stick.
Zann opened his eyes for a moment. "What was . . . ?"
Before he could finish, Zann fell back to sleep, unaware of the danger right above him.
"I hope Darb and Gliss came here," Zann mumbled in his sleep. "It's so relaxing."
Zann's mind drifted in and out of a dreamlike state.
Empty of all energy, all he wanted to do was float, float, float.
He was roused slightly by the buzz of the flizzes as they returned and zipped around Wyssa.
Her eyes popped open, and she dropped back down to the cloud.
"Thank goodness," she said faintly.
Zann heard Wyssa call his name, but he didn't respond.
Then he felt a hard pinch. "Ouch!" he yelped. He heard Perda cry out as well.
"We need to get to the wormhole!" Wyssa said.
"The flizzes said your friends aren't here."
Something seemed to be holding Zann back. He heard a crackle overhead.
The dark cloud was so close he could almost touch it.
He reached out but suddenly felt himself pulled backward.
"Let's go, you two!" Wyssa cried in frustration.
Just as another bolt of energy shot out from the dark cloud, Wyssa dragged Zann and Perda into the wormhole.
"Whoa!" Perda cried as the three of them tumbled wildly through the vortex. "What's happening?"
"That place drained almost all our energy," Zann said, beginning to wake up a bit. "Even Wyssa's!"
Wyssa lunged at the next wormhole they passed, scrabbling for a hold.
It was nothing like her usual, effortless navigation.
"Come," she croaked weakly. With a grunt she pulled herself through.
"Ouch!" someone said when Zann landed on the other side.
"Sorry!" Zann scooted aside quickly, fearing he'd just crushed some tiny native of this world.
But he didn't see anyone. All he saw was a small rock.
"That's better," the voice said.
"Who said that?" Zann demanded.
"I did," the voice came again. "Right in front of you."
Wyssa smiled weakly. "Ah, we're in Gabble.
Sorry about this young man's clumsiness, friend."
"Who are you talking to?" Perda asked. "Are the people here invisible?"
"Not at all." Wyssa bent and patted the rock.
"In Gabble, everything has a voice.
Not just people, but plants, animals, and other objects as well."
Zann's jaw dropped. "You mean we're talking to . . . a rock?"
"You can call me Gray," the rock said cheerfully.
Zann and Perda stared in amazement.
"Don't stand there staring like idiots," Wyssa said. "Introduce yourselves!"
"Um, hello," Zann stammered. He and Perda introduced themselves to the friendly rock.
"Welcome to Gabble," the rock said.
"Thank you," Wyssa replied. "This will be a safe place to rest," she told Zann and Perda.
Zann felt a flash of anxiety. How much time had they wasted in that cloud world? "Rest? But our friends—" he began.
"Are still out there somewhere, yes," Wyssa said.
"But we're no use to them until we've regained our energy. That requires time."
Zann realized she was right. So he and Perda wandered around, chatting with various plants, animals, and other objects.
As Perda got involved in a discussion with an opinionated squirrel, Zann talked with a tree.
"What brings you to Gabble?" the tree asked.
"It's kind of a long story . . ." Zann described their escape from the cloud world.
That led to more questions. Before he knew it, Zann was telling the tree the whole story.
"Oh my," the tree said sympathetically. "I hope you find your friends soon.
Then you can return to searching for your parents."
"I hope so." Zann sighed. "I'm afraid Wyssa will make me go back to Magica once we find the others."
"Can she do that?" the tree asked.
"She can try." Zann squared his shoulders.
"But she won't succeed. I'll sneak away if I have to!"
Just then Perda called him over to settle an argument between her and the squirrel.
After that Zann had a long conversation with a pretty flowering vine.
"Zann!" Wyssa snapped, stomping over and interrupting.
"A tree just told me you're planning to sneak off and look for your parents. Forget about that crazy plan right now.
It's far too dangerous." She stomped off again.
"I can't believe that tree told Wyssa my plans!" Zann complained.
The vine chuckled. "We residents of Gabble love to talk."
Zann saw Perda hurrying toward him. "Keep quiet about this, okay?" he whispered. "Please!"
"I'll try." The vine sounded doubtful. So Zann intercepted Perda, dragging her off to talk to a boulder instead.
Ten minutes later Wyssa approached. "It's time to go," she said.
"We should be recovered well enough by now."
"She's right, I feel better. Come on!" Perda hurried toward the wormhole.
Zann started to follow, but then he heard his name.
A bird landed on a branch beside him.
"Don't fret," the bird chirped. "Wyssa wants to find your parents as much as you do."
"No, she doesn't." Zann kicked at the dirt.
"I heard her muttering to herself just now," the bird said.
"When I asked why she was upset, she said that she feels responsible for your parents' disappearance.
She wants to find them and help get them back to your home world."
Zann frowned. "Really? How's she going to do that?"
"I don't know," the bird admitted. "She stopped talking after that."
"Zann! Now!" Wyssa shouted.
Back in the vortex, Zann thought about what the bird had said. Could it be true?
He was distracted by a bright purple glow.
"Someone has passed this way very recently," Wyssa said. "Hold on!"
She pulled them through another wormhole and into a bustling city. Zann landed hard, scraping his knee.
"Ow." He snapped his fingers. "Heal!"
Nothing happened. "Let me try," Perda said. "You've always done sloppy Healing spells."
"Don't bother," Wyssa said. "Your Healing spells won't work here.
We've just landed in a world with no magic at all."
"We're in a world with no magic?" Perda exclaimed. "You must be kidding!"
"Not at all." said Wyssa. "Such places do exist."
Feeling worried, Zann gulped. He and Perda had been unable to use their magic on other occasions.
Like when Morb was tracking them, or when they were in the Cave of the Unknown. But this situation was much worse.
Zann felt completely helpless knowing that he couldn't use magic, even in an emergency.
"This must be what it feels like to be a Void," Perda said, her voice shaking.
"Or under a Dousing spell," Zann added, thinking briefly of Venna.
"Don't get distracted," Wyssa ordered. "The signal that brought us here was strong and recent.
If your friends are here, we need to find them quickly.
And it won't be easy, since we can't use magic."
Zann took a deep breath. "Okay. If they came through the same wormhole, they should still be nearby, right?
After all, they wouldn't be able to zap anywhere else."
"Good thinking, boy." Wyssa sounded almost impressed.
"Speaking of the wormhole, I guess we can't use magic to find it again," Perda pointed out.
"We'd better make sure we remember where it is."
Zann nodded. The wormhole had closed as soon as they stepped away.
But he remembered where it was. He stepped toward the spot, waiting for the wormhole to open again.
But nothing happened. "Are you sure it was there?" Perda asked.
"Maybe it was a little more to the left."
Zann took a step to the left. The wormhole still didn't appear.
"Use your heads, you two," Wyssa said harshly.
"You need magic to open a wormhole. Everyone knows that!"
She turned and hurried off, leaving Zann and Perda staring at each other.
"But . . . if there's no magic here—" Zann began.
". . . we have no way of opening the wormhole!" Perda swallowed hard.
"So how are we ever supposed to leave this world?"
Wyssa had almost disappeared into the crowds.
"We'll have to worry about that later, I guess," Zann said. "First, let's find the others."
He and Perda followed Wyssa, which wasn't easy.
This world was much more crowded than anywhere in Magica, even First City.
"How are we going to find our friends among all these people?"
Perda wondered as she and Zann finally caught up with Wyssa.
Wyssa stared around uncertainly. "I'm not sure," she admitted.
"I suppose we'll just have to start looking."
A toddler passed by, clinging to her mother's hand.
The little girl babbled curiously, pointing at Zann's head.
"I think she was staring at my hair," Zann said as the mother pulled the toddler away.
Glancing around, he noticed something. "Look, almost everyone here has dark hair.
That should make it easier to spot Darb and Gliss."
"You're right!" Perda exclaimed. "Gliss has bright red hair like yours. And Darb's is light.
Both of them should stand out in this crowd."
Wyssa looked relieved. "Yes, that's true. Come, let's ask the natives if they've seen them."
Zann stopped a man who was passing by. "Pardon me," Zann said.
"Have you seen a girl around here with hair like mine?"
The man paused and stared at Zann. "No, I'm sorry," he said.
"Is she lost? Perhaps you should notify the police."
"The police?" Perda said as the man moved on. "What's that?"
"I have no idea," said Wyssa. "Let's check in here."
She led the way into a marketplace. It was even more crowded than the street outside.
"Look at all this stuff," Zann said. "Do you think it's food?"
"Yes—look!" Perda pointed. "Here's a whole bin full of turnips.
Teplo was right. They do come from another world!"
"If turnips originally came from this world, that means somebody traveled from here to Magica," Zann said.
"So there must be a way to open the wormhole without magic!"
"True." Perda picked up a turnip. "How do you think the people here create their food without magic?"
Just then a woman came over. "May I help you?" she asked.
"We're looking for our friends," Zann said. "A red-haired girl, a light-haired boy, and a small dragon."
"A dragon, huh?" The woman laughed, even though Zann hadn't said anything funny.
"The only dragon I've seen lately is right over there."
She pointed at a banner with a picture of a fierce golden dragon on it.
"No, Zing is much smaller, and—" Zann began.
But the woman was already talking to another customer.
After that Zann, Perda, and Wyssa asked more people if they'd seen Darb, Gliss, or Zing.
However, as soon as Zann described Zing, people either laughed at him or got angry and hurried off.
"I'm serious!" Zann insisted as yet another woman chuckled and shook her head.
"He's about this big, with reddish-colored scales . . ."
"Very funny, young man." The woman smiled. "Excuse me, I'm late for work."
As the woman hurried off, Perda sighed with frustration.
"This place is weird. It's like nobody here has ever seen a real dragon before!" she exclaimed.
Zann felt a tap on his shoulder. Turning, he saw a young man.
"Excuse me," the man said. "You're looking for a dragon? A real one?"
"Yes!" Zann suddenly felt hopeful. "His name is Zing. Have you seen him?"
The man indicated for them to follow.
He led the way out of the market, across the street, and into a shop.
The shop was crammed with knick-knacks, including a whole shelf full of fake dragons.
For a moment Zann was afraid that the man had misunderstood him.
"This way," the young man said, stepping into a dimly lit back room.
Zann entered and gasped. "Zing!" he cried, spotting his dragon cowering behind the bars of a small metal cage.
"Zing!" Zann cried again, relieved. "Hey, little buddy. Let's get you out of there."
He reached for the latch on the cage. The young man stopped him.
"Not so fast," the man said. "This creature is one of a kind—that makes him quite valuable.
I can't just let you take him."
"What do you mean?" Perda said. "He belongs to Zann. Zing is his pet."
The man smiled slyly. "He was wandering loose when I found him.
That means he belongs to me now."
Zann could hardly believe his ears. "But he wants to be with me! See?"
He pointed to Zing, who was jumping excitedly.
"I'm not saying you can't have him," the man said. "I'm saying you must pay."
"Pay?" Zann wasn't sure what the man meant.
Wyssa stepped forward. "We have no money," she said.
"Perhaps you'll accept this in trade?"
She pulled a shiny stone out of her clothes.
Zann finally realized what the man wanted.
In Magica most people could acquire whatever they needed through magic.
But Voids sometimes traded for goods and services.
And this was a whole world of Voids!
The man examined the stone, and then tossed it back.
"Not good enough. I'm sure I can find a buyer who's willing to meet my price for a real, live dragon!"
Zann was furious. First he'd lost his parents, and then his friends.
Now this man was trying to steal his dragon!
"You can't do this!" Zann yelled. "You have no right to keep him!"
"Yeah!" Perda added. "He's Zann's!"
An old woman peered into the room.
She'd been sitting behind a tall counter when Zann and the others had entered, though she'd paid them no attention.
"Is everything all right?" she asked. "I heard yelling."
"It's nothing, Grandmother," the young man said quickly. "We're just talking."
"Why don't you tell her the truth?" Perda snapped. "You're stealing Zann's pet!"
The old woman peered at the cage. "What an odd-looking dog," she commented.
Then she turned to the young man.
"What's the problem, Hyun? Give the kids back their pet."
"But Grandmother!" the young man began.
"No back talk!" the old woman scolded.
Slowly she walked to the back of the shop and opened the cage. "There you go, young ones!"
Zing flew out and dive-bombed the young man.
"Ah!" the man cried. "It's trying to bite me!"
"No," Zann said. "He's trying to flame you."
He guessed that without magic energy, Zing couldn't create fire.
"Come on, boy. Let's get out of here!"
"Thank you, ma'am," Perda said to the old woman.
"Stop, thieves!" the young man yelled.
Zann, Perda, and Wyssa ran out of the shop with Zing flying overhead.
They didn't slow down until they were several blocks away.
"Whew!" Perda said when they finally stopped to catch their breath.
"I've never been so glad to see you, Zing."
"Me too," said Zann, scratching the dragon's knobby head.
Zing panted with delight. "But where are Darb and Gliss?
They must be in this world too!"
"Zing probably doesn't know; they obviously got separated," Perda pointed out.
"Perhaps he can lead us to where he last saw them," Wyssa suggested.
Zing seemed to understand. With a whistle he took off and flew down the street. The others followed.
They ended up in front of an interesting-looking building.
The area was just as busy as the rest of the city.
"Look!" Perda exclaimed. "There's someone with red hair!"
They all rushed over. But when they got closer, Zann saw that the redhead was a short, stout man—not Gliss.
Looking around, he saw more people with light hair.
Zann clenched his fists in frustration. How would they ever find Gliss and Darb without magic?
Why did they have to end up here of all places?
If none of them ever made it home to Magica, it would be all Zann's fault.
And he couldn't stand that thought! How could he have been so angry with Gliss before?
She was the one who should be mad at him for dragging her into danger. Darb too.
The others were still searching for their friends.
But Zann stopped, completely overwhelmed by guilt and despair.
"Zann!" a familiar voice cried.
Zann gasped. "Gliss?"
Spinning around, he saw Gliss racing toward him. Darb was right behind her.
"Oh!" Perda cried, running to meet them. Zing flew after her.
Zann, Perda, Darb, Gliss, and Zing all met in an excited tangle of hugs, laughter, and relief.
"I was afraid we'd never see you guys again!" Gliss exclaimed.
"Us too," Perda said.
Darb gave Zing a scratch on the head.
"I'm so glad you found Zing. We were looking for some food and when I turned around, he was gone!"
"That guy must have grabbed him," Zann said.
"What guy?" Gliss asked.
Zann and Perda told their friends about the young man named Hyun.
That led to more questions, especially when Wyssa joined in.
Both sides ended up sharing the stories of what had happened to them.
"And then Zing led us here," Zann finished.
"Yes," Perda said. "But there were so many people here I was ready to give up! How did you find us?"
"It was Zann." Gliss glanced at Zann shyly. "We had a . . . Red Share."
Zann was amazed. "A Red Share? But I thought that required magic."
Wyssa looked thoughtful. "I thought so too.
Perhaps this land is not completely devoid of magic after all."
"Does that mean there's enough magic to open the wormhole?" Perda asked hopefully.
"No, I'm afraid not," Wyssa said.
Everyone stared at the old woman.
Finally Gliss said what they were all thinking.
"How are we going to get back to Magica?"
"Don't fret," Wyssa said. "I learned magic in a world nearly as devoid of natural magic as this one."
"Really?" Gliss said. "You can get us home?"
"I know some tricks," Wyssa said. "First we need to find a spice market."
She led them in and out of several shops, gathering mysterious ingredients—a strong-smelling powder, some dried leaves, a ceramic bowl, and more.
After a while Zann noticed that they were attracting more and more attention.
Perda noticed too. "People are staring at us," she whispered.
"I think they're staring at Zing," Darb said, sounding worried.
"What if someone else tries to grab him?"
"Or what if the man who took Zing finds us?" Zann said. "He seemed really angry."
He felt nervous as Wyssa led the way back to the wormhole.
They were pretty close to the young man's shop. What if he spotted them?
"Do you think this will work?" Gliss whispered as Wyssa started mixing ingredients and muttering spells under her breath.
Zann shrugged. He knew that Wyssa was powerful.
After all, she'd rescued him and Perda from that scatter beast.
Then again, Zann couldn't help thinking about another time when Wyssa had lost control of a scatter beast.
Maybe she wasn't quite as powerful as she let on.
A little boy came toward them, kicking a ball.
"Hi," he said, staring at Zing. "What's that?"
Zann and his friends exchanged a cautious look.
"Um, what does he look like?" Perda asked the boy.
"He looks like a dragon," the boy said.
"But dragons aren't real. My daddy said so."
Zann glanced at Wyssa. She'd finished mixing and was stepping toward the spot where the wormhole should be.
"Excuse us," Zann told the little boy. "We're kind of busy."
The boy ignored him, stepping closer to Zing.
"There's no such thing as dragons," he insisted. "So what is he?"
Zann was so anxious that he lost his patience.
"There might not be dragons in your world, but there are in ours," he snapped.
"We're trying to get home, and we're worried that a bad man might try to stop us.
So we don't have time for questions, okay?"
The boy took a step back. He didn't say anything.
"That wasn't very nice," Darb whispered.
Zann shrugged. He felt bad, but he tried not to worry about it.
All he cared about was getting out of this no-magic world.
Just then a shout came from across the street.
"Oh no!" Perda hissed. "It's the guy who took Zing!"
The young man raced toward them clutching a large net.
Behind him were two other men. They didn't look friendly.
Zann glanced at Wyssa. She was sprinkling her potion over the wormhole, which was starting to glow.
But the men had almost reached them!
"Hurry!" Gliss screamed. "They're coming!" She grabbed Darb and crowded toward the wormhole.
Zann grabbed Zing and did the same. But it was opening so slowly.
"Stop, thief!" the young man shouted. "That dragon is mine! I—whoa!"
The little boy had kicked his ball.
The man tripped over it and slammed facedown into the pavement.
"Oh no!" the other men cried, but they were running too fast to stop.
They fell on top of their friend.
"The wormhole's open!" Perda cried.
"Let's go," said Wyssa.
Everyone held hands as Wyssa pulled the group into the wormhole.
Zann barely had time to glance back at the little boy, who was grinning at the fallen men.
"Thank you!" Zann shouted to the boy.
The boy waved. "You're welcome!"
Then Zann found himself back in the vortex.
"Whew!" Perda exclaimed. "I've never been so glad to be in this crazy place."
Gliss laughed. "Yeah. At least there's magic here!"
"We'd better stop and rest," Wyssa said.
"Being in a world without magic might have weakened our energy.
And we'll need plenty to get safely back to Magica."
She pulled them through another wormhole.
This time there were no people or buildings in sight.
A babbling brook weaved its way through a grove of purple-leaved trees waving in a soft breeze.
"The magic here isn't particularly strong," Wyssa said.
"But there's enough to conjure food and fresh clothes.
Then you'd better sleep for a while."
"Good idea." Gliss stifled a yawn. "I feel as if I haven't slept in days!"
Soon they were all clothed and fed.
Zann lay down beside his friends, his mind racing with questions and plans.
Wyssa knew he wanted to search for his parents.
How could he get away without her noticing?
Before he could figure it out, his weariness overcame him and he drifted off to sleep.
He woke some time later, his heart pounding.
He'd just had a dream about his parents again.
This one had been especially intense, though Zann couldn't remember much about it.
Just that his father was trying to tell him something about Morb.
"Weird," Zann muttered. He reached into his pocket and touched the message stone.
It was warm. That was weird too.
"Are you awake, boy?" Wyssa stepped into view.
"Good. We shouldn't stay here much longer."
"Why not?" Zann asked. "What world is this, anyway?"
"It's my home world," Wyssa admitted. "I'm, er, not exactly welcome here anymore.
Besides, I promised your grandfather I'd get you kids home as quickly as possible."
"Boz?" Zann was startled. "What does he have to do with this?"
Wyssa turned away without answering, nudging the others with her foot to wake them.
"Time to go," she said. "Next stop, Magica."
Zann's friends cheered. But Zann felt his heart sink.
He should have sneaked away while the others were sleeping.
How was he ever going to escape from Wyssa now?
"I can't go back to Magica!" Zann blurted out. "Not without finding my parents."
"Don't be a fool, boy," Wyssa snapped.
"I know I can find them," Zann retorted. "I even have a clue—World X.
I know my parents wanted to find it.
Maybe that's where they are—they could be trapped there!"
Wyssa looked startled. "How do you know about—never mind," she said, interrupting herself.
"Yes, it's true they wanted to find World X.
But I have no idea where it is.
I promise I'll try to find out—after you and your friends are safely back in Magica."
"That sounds like a good offer, Zann," Gliss said.
Ignoring her, Zann glared at Wyssa. "They're my parents," he said.
"Nobody cares about finding them as much as I do!"
"I'm not so sure about that, boy," Wyssa muttered.
"Morb is—" Once again she stopped herself.
"Morb?" Perda spoke up. "What does he have to do with this?"
"Forget it. I shouldn't have said anything."
Wyssa stalked off toward the wormhole. "Let's go."
"Not until you tell me what's going on," Zann said.
"Why did you mention Morb? Is he looking for my parents too?"
Wyssa scowled and then sighed. "I suppose you deserve to know.
Maybe it will convince you not to rush off by yourself.
Yes, I've heard rumors that Morb is looking for your parents. Nobody knows why."
Zann froze. What could Morb possibly want with Zann's parents?
"Hold on," Perda said. "How can Morb be searching for anyone?
I thought he went back to being a Void when Zann defeated him."
"I don't know how he's able to use the wormholes," Wyssa said.
"But he's not keeping his search a secret." She grimaced.
"He's left a trail of terrified worlds behind him."
Perda's eyes widened. "That must be why the Skellians freaked out when we mentioned Morb's name!"
"Whatever," Zann said to Wyssa. "I'm still not going back to Magica."
He rubbed both hands on his legs, hoping this spell would work.
Touching the trunk of a sturdy tree, he cried, "Shackle!"
It worked! Magical shackles appeared, binding Zann to the tree.
Wyssa gnashed her teeth. "Stop this foolishness!
Remove those shackles at once, or I'll do it for you."
"You can't," Perda said. "Nobody can remove another person's Shackle spell."
"She's right. And you won't change my mind," Zann said.
"Take my friends home, and then we can search together. Otherwise I'll search on my own."
"You don't know what you're doing, boy." Wyssa narrowed her eyes at Zann.
"If even half the rumors about Morb's new powers are true, you won't have a chance against him."
