Zann stared at her. "You can't make me do anything," he said defiantly.
"You didn't even know when Morb was tricking you!"
"What are you talking about?" Wyssa demanded.
"When you sent my parents off course with that scatter beast, it wasn't an accident," said Zann.
"It was part of Morb's plan. He told me so himself."
Wyssa's eyes went wide. "What?" Her yell echoed through the quiet forest.
She leaped forward and touched Zann's forehead. "Truth!" she intoned.
"Ow!" Zann yelped as he felt a sizzling sensation in his head.
A second later Wyssa backed away, her eyes burning with rage.
"So it is true," she said through gritted teeth.
"I've been torturing myself all these years, thinking I was to blame for your parents' disappearance. Morb will pay for this!"
Alarmed, Zann glanced at his friends. They were all staring at Wyssa in silence. Zing cowered behind Darb.
Wyssa swept toward Zann again. "Release!" she said.
The shackles exploded. Zann gasped. "How did you—"
Before he could finish, Wyssa grabbed Gliss.
"You're in charge now, Red," Wyssa said.
"Take Zann and these others straight back to Magica."
"I . . . I . . . ," Gliss stammered. She seemed too scared to speak.
"This will ensure that you follow my orders, girl."
Wyssa put her hands over Gliss' face.
When the old woman pulled them away, glowing purple goggles covered Gliss' eyes.
"Those goggles will show you the way," Wyssa said.
"They'll also provide extra magic for navigating the vortex.
But don't try to remove them until all of you are safely back in Magica, or you'll suffer intense pain."
"I . . . I understand," Gliss said.
"Good." Wyssa leaped for the wormhole. "Revenge will be mine!" she cried as she disappeared.
"Wow," Perda said, her voice shaking. "That was scary!"
Zann nodded, no longer doubting Wyssa's power.
For a moment they all stayed quiet. "Maybe Wyssa is right," Zann thought.
Maybe it was better to let her handle the search . . .
Finally Gliss spoke up. "Zann, what do you want me to do?"
Zann turned to her and sighed. "It's not like we have much choice."
"There's always a choice." Gliss took a deep breath and reached for the goggles.
"No!" Darb cried.
"Gliss!" said Zann. "You don't have to—"
"Aah!" cried Gliss, ripping the goggles from her face.
She collapsed on the ground, writhing and crying out in pain.
Darb rushed over to her. A minute later she was able to climb back to her feet.
"Th—there," Gliss said. "If you want to continue your search, I won't stop you. In fact I'll come along."
Perda looked at Zann. "We all will."
Zann gulped. Putting himself in danger was one thing.
But could he also risk his friends' lives again?
"Are you sure?" he asked.
Gliss, Perda, and Darb nodded. Zing let out an excited whistle.
Zann suddenly felt braver. He and his friends had defeated Morb once before.
They made a powerful team, the kind of team that could do anything.
"Okay," he told them. "Let's go!"
Zann's friends headed toward the wormhole. Zann noticed that Gliss' arms and legs were shaking.
He winced, remembering how painful it had looked when she'd ripped off the magical goggles.
"Wait," he said to his friends. "Are you sure you want to come with me?
I mean, really sure? It could be dangerous. Especially if Morb is involved."
"Of course we're sure," Perda said. "Right, guys?"
Gliss was still trembling, but she smiled.
"You'd better not quit now, Zann. I don't want to think I defied Wyssa's command for nothing!"
"Yeah." Darb took Gliss' hand. "Besides, we make a good team. And we want to help."
"Okay. Thanks." Zann glanced at the wormhole.
"But we don't have Wyssa to guide us anymore. We need a plan."
"Good point." Perda paced back and forth in front of the wormhole. "Does anyone have any good ideas?"
"Wyssa said Morb left a bunch of terrified worlds behind him," Darb said.
"Maybe we could start visiting worlds and asking people about Morb. That might give us some clues."
Zann shook his head. "I'm not sure we should visit worlds randomly.
We might end up back in that no-magic world again."
Perda shuddered. "Or Fardark, or stinky Niffia, or that crazy cloud world."
She was still pacing. Just then her foot hit a stone, which tumbled toward Zann.
"Hey, check it out," said Zann, bending down to pick up the stone.
"This looks just like my message stone!"
Perda shrugged. "So what? It looks like a stone."
"No, I mean I think they're the same type of stone."
Zann fished out his message stone. It still felt warm.
He held the two stones side by side. "See?"
"Weird," Darb said. "They do look alike."
Gliss glanced around. "Look, there are more stones like that!"
She was right. Dozens of similar stones lay near the wormhole.
"I assumed my stone came from the Cave of the Unknown because I'd never seen one like it anywhere else in Magica," said Zann.
"But maybe it actually came from this world."
"That makes sense," Darb said. "This is Wyssa's home world, right?
That's probably why she used that stone to communicate with your parents."
"And with Morb," Perda added. "It also explains why none of us had ever heard of message stones before."
"Teplo and Boz knew about them," Gliss pointed out.
Perda shrugged. "They're Magic Masters. It's their job to know lots of obscure stuff."
Zann squeezed the stone in his hand.
If his stone came from this world, that might explain why he'd had that extra-vivid dream here earlier.
"I think we should look for a place to play my parents' message again," he said. "There might be more clues."
"Clues? Like what?" Perda sounded dubious.
"I don't see any place to plug in the stone," said Gliss, looking around.
"She’s right,” Perda said. "Anyway, I just thought of another plan.
We should try to follow Wyssa. She's looking for Morb, right?
And Morb is looking for Zann's parents.
So if we can catch up to Wyssa, we might find Zann's parents too."
"Wyssa left a while ago, though," Darb said.
"We'll never find her in the vortex now."
"Besides, how do we know we can trust her?" Zann asked.
"Wyssa was the one who brought those flizzes to Morb.
She also tried to bring him a scatter beast."
"That was earlier," Perda said. "She's not working with Morb anymore."
Darb shrugged. "Still, she may not be on our side.
She broke Zann's Shackle spell and put that nasty spell on Gliss, remember?"
Gliss nodded. "Plus, she used a Truth spell on Zann without his consent, and—oh! That's it!"
"That's what?" Perda asked.
Gliss pointed at Zann's forehead. "Look! When Wyssa touched Zann's face to do the Truth spell, she left purple fingerprints on his skin!"
"She did?" Zann said, reaching up to wipe away the marks.
"Stop!" Perda leaped forward, grabbing Zann's hands before he could touch his forehead.
"Don't wipe them off. Maybe we can use that purple stuff to track Wyssa the same way she used it to track Gliss and Darb!"
"I was thinking the same thing," said Gliss with a smile.
"You mean we can figure out which wormholes have been used recently, and see if she's in those worlds?" Zann said.
Perda looked excited. "It's the only good plan we have. What do you say, Zann?"
Zann turned his message stone over in his hand.
"You're right," he said. "Let's not waste any more time."
"Okay." Gliss glanced at the wormhole. "We'd better make sure we're all shackled together this time.
We don't want to get separated again."
"Good idea." Perda held out her hands. "Join friction, everyone.
We'll make this one a Mutual Shackle spell so any of us can break it if we need to."
"Just don't do that in the vortex," Zann warned.
Soon the four of them were shackled together.
Zann even conjured a harness for Zing.
"Everyone ready?" Darb asked.
"Let's go!" Perda said, leading the way toward the wormhole.
Zann held his breath as they all dived into the vortex.
It felt much scarier being there without Wyssa.
But he tried not to think about that.
"It's working!" Gliss cried, staring at Zann's forehead. "The fingerprints are glowing!"
Zann's left hand was shackled to Perda.
He used his right hand to grab the nearest wormhole.
"Hang on, everyone!" he cried as he yanked his friends through.
He felt the familiar sensation of passing through the wormhole. It felt weird but not unpleasant.
Splash!
"Drat! Aah!" Zann screamed in horror. They had just landed in a pool of boiling water!
"I'm burning!" Zann screamed. Only his head and shoulders were above the hot, bubbling water.
His friends were screaming too. But Zann could only think about his own searing pain.
A sharp whistle came from overhead. Zing was flying back and forth between the kids and the rocky shore.
Being a fire dragon, Zing was immune to heat and had already shaken off the hot water.
Seeing Zing cleared Zann's mind a little.
The wormhole was over their heads—too high to reach.
The shore was pretty far away. There was only one way he and his friends would survive this.
"Focus, everyone!" Zann yelled. "We have to zap out of the water!"
He hoped their magic would work in this world. If not . . .
He tried not to think about it.
"Everyone join hands!" Gliss cried.
Zann felt someone grab his hand. He almost yanked it away because the touch hurt his injured skin.
He forced himself to squeeze back though.
"Zap!" he cried.
He landed on the rocky shore with a grunt.
The heat was gone. Well, some of it was gone.
Looking around, Zann could see that they were in a world of flame and scorching heat.
A fiery red sky hung overhead. Steam rose from the bubbling lake.
Zann could already feel sweat beading on his burned skin.
But at least he no longer felt as if his whole body were melting.
Gliss rubbed her hands together, wincing at the pain. Then she touched Darb. "Heal!"
Instantly Darb's skin went from fiery red to its normal color.
"Thanks," he said, slumping with relief.
Gliss quickly healed herself next. Zann and Perda did the same.
"That was close." Perda looked around. "What world is this?"
"I don't know," said Zann. Zing landed, and Zann scratched the dragon's head. "Thanks for the help, little buddy."
Zing chirped, sounding nervous. A large shadow passed over the group.
Glancing up, Zann saw an enormous dragon flying overhead.
Luckily it didn't seem to notice them.
"We need to figure out whether Wyssa is here," Perda said. "Quickly."
Zann and his friends picked their way carefully up the rocky slope.
"There goes another dragon." Darb shaded his eyes to watch a shadowy creature fly by in the distance.
"Look out!" Gliss grabbed Darb and yanked him back. "You almost stepped in that puddle!"
Zann wasn't sure why she sounded so anxious until he looked down.
Right near his feet was a puddle of burning hot lava!
"Everyone be careful," Perda warned.
They continued walking. Several more dragons flew by in the distance.
The only other signs of life were a few scrubby trees and shrubs.
"This is crazy," Perda said after a few minutes.
"How are we supposed to figure out if Wyssa or Morb is here?"
Gliss mopped her brow. "It seems like the kind of place Morb would like—dangerous and scary."
A scraping sound came from behind a house-sized boulder nearby.
"Shh," Zann whispered. "That could be an unfriendly dragon."
He tiptoed around the boulder. A teenage boy was scraping at the dirt.
"Hey!" Zann blurted out. "It's a person!"
The boy spun around. "Oh! You startled me!" he exclaimed.
"Sorry. My name is Zann."
"I'm Arrano," the boy replied with a smile.
By then Zann's friends had appeared, and Zann quickly introduced them.
"What's the name of this world?" Perda asked Arrano.
Arrano looked surprised. "Don't you know where you are?"
"We just arrived through a wormhole," Gliss explained.
"Really? You came here, to Drac, from another world?"
Arrano's friendly expression changed to a worried one.
"We don't get many visitors here. It would probably be best for you to leave before they see you."
"Before who sees us?" Perda asked.
Arrano didn't answer. He was staring past the visitors.
Zann turned. A pair of dragons had just waddled into sight.
They were a little smaller than Zing but much plumper, with shiny blue scales.
"Shoo!" Gliss said, waving her hands at the little dragons. "Get out of here!"
The dragons ignored her. Darb watched them with interest.
"They look a little like river hoppers, don't they?" he remarked.
Zann nodded. "One of Boz's friends has a hopper as a pet.
It's bigger than these though." He frowned as the dragons came closer. "And much less bold."
He turned, planning to ask Arrano how to get rid of the pests.
To Zann's surprise, Arrano was nowhere in sight.
"Hey, where'd he go?" Darb wondered.
Perda shrugged. "He seemed kind of nervous or something."
"No wonder, living in a crazy world like this." Gliss shuddered.
Zing was glaring at the approaching dragons.
He sent out a warning blast of flame. The smaller dragons jumped back.
Then one of them let out a sharp cry.
The second one opened its mouth and shot out a stream of lava.
"Whoa!" Zann jumped aside. The lava hit a shrub, which was instantly burned to a stump.
"Okay, maybe they're not much like river hoppers after all," Darb said. "Let's get out of here!"
"Good idea." Zann whistled for Zing. "Come on, boy!"
Before Zing could get to Zann, one of the other dragons leaped up and batted him out of the air.
Zing landed on the hard ground with a grunt and lay there stunned.
"Zing!" Zann cried. He tried to rush over, but one of the blue dragons blocked him with another lava blast.
"I've got him!" Darb dodged around the second dragon and grabbed Zing.
"Darb! Look out!" Gliss screamed.
Both dragons had turned toward Darb and Zing, who were now backed up against the huge boulder. The dragons moved closer.
"Uh-oh!" cried Darb. "I can't get past them—we're trapped!"
"Now what?" Zann said.
He and his friends were huddled beneath some trees, hidden from the dragons flying overhead.
"This is bad," Perda said. "We're lost, and we don't have any way to contact Arrano and the others."
Just then a loud squawk came from directly above them.
"It's the dragons!" Gliss cried. "They found us!"
"No, wait." Darb peered up at the branches. "That didn't sound like a dragon."
Zann looked up too. A large bird was perched on an upper branch.
"That looks a lot like Teplo's sniffer goose," Darb said.
"Only smaller and with a shorter neck."
Perda sighed. "This is no time for identifying native species, Darb.
Besides, that goose doesn't look very friendly.
Let’s get moving." She grabbed Darb's arm and started to drag him away.
"Quiet!" Gliss warned. "Here comes a dragon."
Zann hid behind a tree as a medium-sized dragon walked past.
With every step thick orange smoke puffed out of its nostrils.
"This is crazy," Zann said once the dragon was out of sight.
"We can't just wander around looking for that wormhole."
"Yeah," Perda agreed. "Besides, we'll have to use magic to levitate over the boiling lake anyway.
Let's just save time and zap there."
"We can't," Gliss said. "We're lost, remember?"
"I can try a Seeking spell," Perda offered.
"That's how I found the wormhole back in Swamp Bottom."
"Good idea," Zann said. "Join friction."
Perda, Gliss, and Zann rubbed their hands together. "Seek," Perda said.
"It's working!" Zann could feel the magic energy tugging at him.
The Seeking spell led them through the valley below the trees.
Zann was climbing over some large rocks when he heard a rustling sound overhead.
He looked up and saw a large dragon flying straight at them.
"Everyone get down!" he shouted.
Zann threw himself behind a boulder. A blast of fiery air hit the spot where he'd just been standing.
"I think that's a flame fury!" Darb said.
"Like the ones that powered the Dragon Wagon. They must come from this world!"
"Great," Gliss said grimly. "All the more reason to get out of here!"
"We'd better zap away," Zann said. "Zap!"
He felt a twinge, but nothing happened.
"Oh no!" Perda cried. "That Seeking spell used up our magic energy!"
The fury was circling toward them again.
Flames were already curling out of its snout. Darb stood up.
"Darb!" Gliss cried. "Get down!"
Cupping both hands around his mouth, Darb took a deep breath and let out a loud honking sound.
"What are you—" Zann began.
Suddenly an answering honk came from the direction of the trees!
A second later the goose flapped into sight and spit a blob of goo directly at the dragon.
The fury howled, falling to the ground with an earth-shaking thump.
It pawed frantically at its face, trying to rub away the thick goose spit.
"What are we waiting for?" Perda cried. "Run!"
Zann took off with the girls at his heels and Zing flying overhead.
Darb paused just long enough to give a honk of thanks and then followed.
They'd only been running for a few minutes when they almost stumbled over a wormhole.
"The Seeking spell found a different wormhole!" Gliss exclaimed.
"Good," Perda said, panting. "We might not have enough energy left to levitate.
And I definitely didn't feel like swimming in that lake again!"
Darb cast a nervous glance over his shoulder.
"I think I hear that dragon coming. Hurry!"
Zann grabbed Perda's hand. Perda held out her hand to Gliss, who was holding Darb's hand. They all dived into the wormhole.
Soon the friends were hurtling through the vortex.
"Hold tight, everyone," Gliss said. "It makes me nervous to be here without our Shackle spell."
"Hey, Darb," said Zann. "How did you know that goose would help us?"
"I remembered the fake snuffer goose from the Dragon Wagon," Darb explained.
"When I realized we were in the furies' home world, I guessed that goose we saw must have been a snuffer."
"But how did you know how to call it?" Perda asked.
"Because of Teplo’s pet sniffer goose," Darb said.
"I picked up a few words of its language while we were staying with Teplo.
Since sniffer and snuffer geese look similar, I guessed their languages might be related." He shrugged. "Luckily, I was right."
"Wow." Zann was impressed. He never would have thought of any of that!
"You saved us from being roasted, Darb."
"Yeah." Gliss shuddered. "Roasted and eaten."
"Hey, Zann," Perda said. "Your purple marks are glowing again."
Zann grabbed at the next wormhole and tumbled through it.
Jumping to his feet, he was prepared to fight or run, but he quickly relaxed.
This world didn't look scary at all.
"Where are we?" Gliss wondered, climbing to her feet.
Perda shrugged. "Wherever it is, it looks boring."
"Yeah." Zann stepped away from the wormhole, which swirled shut and disappeared, leaving almost no color anywhere.
Everything—the sky, the ground, the trees and shrubs—was dull shades of beige and gray.
"At least there aren't any scary creatures attacking us," Gliss said.
Darb nodded. "I don't see any signs of people either. How are we going to figure out if Wyssa's here?"
"Zing!" Perda scolded. "Don't eat that. We don't know if it's safe."
The dragon was nibbling on a leaf. "He must be hungry," Zann said.
"I am too. Let's conjure some food while we figure out what to do."
"I'll do it." Gliss rubbed her hands together, but nothing happened. She frowned. "It's not working."
"Uh-oh." Zann gulped. "What if we're stuck in another world without magic?"
"We can't open the wormhole again without magic!" Gliss exclaimed. "We could be trapped here forever!"
Crash!
Zann spun around as something landed behind them.
It was a large platter of puckerberry pancakes!
"The food!" Darb said. "It's here. I guess the spell worked after all."
"It just took a long time." Perda stuck her finger in the pancake syrup and licked it. "Mmm!"
"It's weird that the spell took so long to work," Zann said.
"We should try another spell and see if the same thing happens."
"I'll do it." Perda rubbed her hands together. "Levitate!"
They all waited. Several moments passed before Perda's feet finally lifted off the ground.
"Magic must work really slowly here, that's all."
Zann stepped toward the wormhole and waited.
Eventually it swirled open again. "Phew! We're not trapped after all."
"Good." Perda reached for a pancake. "Let's eat, and then we can look for Wyssa."
Darb peered into the distance. "Someone's coming."
Several people were moving slowly toward them.
They were very slim and tall, with extra-long arms and legs.
Their skin, hair, and clothes were the same dull colors as the rest of their world.
"Should we run away or stay and talk to them?" Gliss asked.
"They look pretty friendly," Perda said. "Besides, I'm guessing we can outrun them if we have to."
Several minutes later the natives reached the visitors.
"Greetings, strangers," one of them said. His voice was slow but friendly. "Welcome to Chronos."
"Thank you," Zann said. "We just arrived through the wormhole."
"Is everything always so slow here?" Perda asked.
Long-drawn-out chuckles emerged from several of the Chronians.
"That's the first question every visitor asks," said one Chronian.
"Yes, time moves more slowly here than it does in most other worlds."
"That's right," another Chronian continued. "For every hour that passes in Chronos, just seconds pass in the vortex or most other worlds."
Zann already felt impatient with the Chronians' slow speech.
"Has anyone else visited lately?" he asked. "A woman named Wyssa?"
"Yes," one of the Chronians said. "Wyssa arrived here earlier. But she moved on immediately."
Zann frowned. Their tracking method was working.
But they couldn't seem to catch up with Wyssa!
"Do you know where she was going next?" he asked.
"Was it a place called World X? A newly discovered world?"
"Wyssa wasn't here long enough to tell us about her plans," a Chronian said.
Another Chronian spoke up. "Wait—Wyssa might not have said anything.
But a traveler who passed by a few days ago did mention a new world."
"Really?" Zann spun to face him. "Was the traveler a tall, skinny guy named Morb?"
"No." A look of confusion passed slowly over the Chronian's face.
"It was a trader who passes through Chronos frequently.
He visits many worlds in his travels."
"What did he say?" Zann's heart pounded.
Could this be the clue that would lead to his parents?
Maybe they wouldn't need to catch Wyssa after all!
"The trader has heard rumors," the Chronian said.
"Supposedly there's a world with wormholes that lead not only into the vortex, but directly into other worlds as well!"
"But that's not how wormholes work," Perda said.
"You have to travel through the vortex to go from one world to another."
The Chronian shrugged. "I know. The trader wasn't sure it was true either.
He hasn't seen this strange world himself."
"If it's real, it could be World X," Zann said.
"It sure sounds like the kind of place that my parents would want to find."
He glanced at his friends. "We should go!"
Perda yawned and reached for another pancake.
"Why don't we rest here for a little while first?
You heard what they said—even if we stay here for hours, only a few seconds will pass everywhere else."
Zann wanted to argue, but he could see that his friends were hungry and tired.
"All right," he said. "But let's make it a short rest, okay?"
The Chronians led them to a gray town nearby.
The local innkeeper offered the visitors food and drink, which was nearly tasteless but filling.
Then she showed Zann and his friends to comfortable beds.
Zann was sure he'd never be able to sleep.
But he drifted off quickly and fell into another vivid dream.
His parents were running in terror through a forest with dark magic swirling around them.
Like everything else in Chronos, the dream moved slowly.
That gave Zann time to see details he hadn't noticed in his previous dreams.
In the forest there were tiny houses with doors no higher than his mother's knee.
While the forest seemed dark, the sky overhead was a brilliant shade of blue.
Zann finally awoke, blinking in the pale gray light.
Could anything in his dream be a clue to finding his parents?
Lots of worlds had blue skies. But not many worlds had such tiny houses.
Even Fud from Galvan was too big to fit through those small doors.
Eager to get moving, Zann woke his friends.
It seemed to take forever for the Chronians to guide them back to the wormhole.
Then Zann had to wait for the mutual shackles to appear, and for the wormhole to open.
But finally he and his friends were back in the vortex.
"Wow," Gliss said as wormholes rushed past.
"It feels weird to be living at full speed again."
"Yeah." Darb looked at Zann. "Hey, the purple mark is glowing!"
"Good." Zann grabbed the next wormhole and pulled his friends through.
The world they landed in was dark, with jagged lightning splitting the sky. Zann recognized it and gasped.
Apparently Perda recognized it too. "Oh no! We're back in Fardark!"
"Let's get out of here!" Zann exclaimed. "Hurry!"
He and Perda yanked the others back through the wormhole before it could swirl shut behind them.
Zann was relieved when they were back in the vortex.
"That was close," Perda said.
"Yeah," Zann agreed. "But what if Wyssa is in Fardark? Or Morb?"
"That definitely looked like the kind of place where they would hang out," Gliss said with a shudder.
"It doesn't matter," Darb said. "It was too risky to stay."
"Right," Perda agreed. "And if Morb and Wyssa had gone there, they probably would have moved on by now anyway.
Nobody would stay in Fardark for long."
Zann thought of something. "Actually, we know my parents aren't there.
The skies in Fardark are dark, not blue.
Plus, Perda and I didn't see any creatures small enough to live in those tiny houses."
"Are you sure your dreams are showing you where your parents are?" Darb sounded dubious.
Zann had told his friends about his latest dream while they all walked back to the wormhole in Chronos.
"The more dreams I have, the more sure I am," Zann replied.
"I think the images are coming from my message stone.
The most realistic dream I had was when we were resting in Wyssa's home world." He remembered something else.
"Also, I bet that was Wyssa's world we passed the time I had the waking dream! Remember?
All I saw through that wormhole were some trees with purple leaves—just like the ones in Wyssa's world!"
Gliss looked confused. "So we passed Wyssa's world twice?"
"Yeah. Perda and I ended up in Fardark twice too." Zann shrugged.
"That does seem weird, now that I think about it."
"Not really," Perda said. "I did some research on the vortex back in Swamp Bottom, and—"
"You did?" Zann broke in.
Perda shot him a look. "I told you I was thinking about becoming an explorer.
I started preparing by reading all your parents' books, including the one called Voyages Through the Vortex."
"Oh." Zann was surprised she had read all of those books. "What did you find out?"
"Haven't you read your parents' books, Zann?" Gliss asked.
"Sure. I mean, some of them." Zann shrugged sheepishly.
"Actually, I've mostly just looked at the pictures of the cool monsters and stuff.
They wrote the vortex book when I was really young."
"The vortex isn't like a regular road or tunnel or anything like that," Perda explained.
"It's just a magical space between worlds that's always shifting in unpredictable ways.
Nobody knows exactly how it works. That's why it's important to have an experienced guide like Wyssa if you're not experienced yourself.
You also need strong magic to help you navigate.
Otherwise you can get yourself in trouble—at least that's what the book said."
"Your parents must have pretty strong magic, huh, Zann?" Gliss said. "Even though they're not Reds?"
"Yeah. Plus they have lots of experience traveling between worlds."
But for once Zann wasn't really thinking about his parents.
Perda's words had reminded him of Venna. She'd had very strong magic.
But she'd been under a Dousing spell when she fell into the wormhole. What had become of her?
He pushed the thought aside, realizing that Perda was still talking.
"So there's no way to predict which wormhole we'll pass next," she was saying.
"The next one could lead back into Magica.
Or it could take us into Fardark yet again.
Or into a brand-new world—maybe even one that's never been discovered before."
"Or World X," Zann murmured.
"Let me get this straight." Gliss sounded worried.
"We have no way of finding a wormhole back into Magica?"
Perda shrugged. "Not unless we get lucky."
"Or find Wyssa," Darb said. "Or somebody else who can guide us."
"Like my parents." Zann felt a tingling on his forehead.
The marks were glowing again. "Hold on!" he said, reaching for the next wormhole.
As he grabbed the wormhole’s edge, he caught a glimpse of blue sky.
He tried not to get too excited though.
Lots of worlds, including Magica, had blue skies. Still, he couldn't help hoping.
Splash!
"Drat—glurb!" Zann gurgled as he felt himself sinking under water.
"Oh no," he thought. "Did we land in Skellia again?"
But he quickly realized that this water was much calmer than the rough seas of Skellia.
It was also much cooler than the boiling lake in Drac.
When Zann came up for air, his friends were bobbing in the water nearby.
"Where are we?" Zann asked, pushing a clump of wet hair out of his eyes.
"I don't know," Gliss said. "But it looks nice."
They were in the middle of a large, tranquil lake.
Pretty silver and gold fish darted around, nibbling at the swaying water grasses.
On shore a green lawn sloped gently up to a lush forest.
A gleaming city of elegant spires and towers stood atop a hill in the distance.
When Zann and his friends swam to shore, they heard birds singing and felt a warm, gentle breeze.
The ground was soft and springy beneath Zann's feet.
He snapped his fingers to conjure dry clothes.
"Good. Our magic works here," he said. He touched his hair to dry it.
"I just have one question. Why are so many of the wormholes located over water?"
Darb started to laugh. Then he stopped, leaning closer to stare at Zann's forehead.
"Uh-oh," he said. "Zann, your face is clean!"
"Gee, thanks," Zann said. "Yours looks pretty clean too."
Perda gasped. "No, Zann. This is a problem!" she cried.
"When your head went under water, Wyssa's fingerprints must have washed off.
We have no way of tracking her anymore!"
"I knew my parents were still out there!" Zann exclaimed. "They must have found World X."
"Yeah. Too bad we still don't know how to get there," Perda said.
Darb looked thoughtful. "We know World X has a blue sky.
If we peek through the wormholes and check every world with blue skies, we'll find World X eventually."
Zann smiled hopefully. "That could work!"
"There are lots of worlds with blue skies though."
Gliss glanced up at the Paxian sky.
"Yeah. Including that creepy no-magic world we got stuck in," Perda said.
"We'll be careful," Zann said. "We'll hang onto the edge of each wormhole so it can't close behind us.
If we recognize that no-magic world, we can duck back into the vortex before we're trapped."
"Like we did the second time in Fardark," Perda said with a nod. "I guess that could work."
Vee was listening carefully. "If you find Morb, will you look for our stolen mibbit?" she asked. "We're very worried about it."
"Sure," Darb said. "What do mibbits look like?"
"I'll show you." Vee closed her eyes.
Soon a small, fluffy creature hopped out of the forest.
Zing let out an excited chirp. "Not so fast," Zann said, grabbing the dragon.
"That little critter is definitely not lunch."
"It doesn't look very scary," Perda commented as the mibbit nibbled at the grass.
Vee smiled. "I know. But trust me—you don't want to panic one."
"How can we rescue the stolen one without panicking it?" Darb asked.
Vee picked up the mibbit. It snuggled into her arms.
"If the mibbit panics, you can calm it by rubbing its ears."
She demonstrated, and the mibbit let out a squeak of pleasure.
Darb was watching intently. "May I try?"
"Certainly." Vee held out the mibbit.
"Easy, little fellow," Darb cooed. He rubbed the mibbit's long ears.
Vee smiled. "The soothing effects usually last a couple of hours."
Perda looked impatient. "Let's get going. The sooner we warn someone about Morb, the better."
"Right." Zann took a step toward the lake.
"Guess it's time to get wet again."
"There's no need for that." Vee set down the mibbit, which hopped away into the forest.
"I can take you there by boat."
Minutes later Zann and his friends were back in the vortex.
"Pax was nice," Gliss said. "I wouldn't mind visiting again someday."
"Yeah." Perda laughed. "Just watch out for those scary mibbits!"
Zann was barely listening. He watched for glimpses of blue through the wormholes.
The first world they passed showed a drab green sky, and the next two skies were gray.
Then he spotted a flash of blue. "There's one!" he cried.
He was so excited that he pulled himself all the way through the wormhole, flopping on his stomach on the other side.
"Oof!" Darb grunted as he landed beside Zann.
"Hey," Perda complained, sitting up. "You were supposed to hold onto the edge, remember?"
Zann's face flushed. "Sorry," he mumbled, glancing back at the wormhole as it swirled shut. "I forgot."
"Um, guys?" Darb said. "We're not alone."
Five girls stood in a semicircle, staring at the visitors.
All of them were Zann's age or younger.
They looked almost like regular Magicians, except for their green skin and vine-like hair.
"What are they?" one of the girls whispered to the others.
Zann climbed to his feet. "Hey. What world is this?"
The girls all stared at him. "It speaks!" one of them said.
Another girl noticed Zing. "Look, a dragon!" She let out a whistle.
Zing chirped with delight and scampered over, snuggling against her leg.
Zann was surprised. Zing didn't usually warm up to strangers so quickly. Zann glanced at Darb, who shrugged.
One of the girls turned to address Gliss and Perda.
"What sort of odd creatures are you traveling with?" she asked.
"You mean Zing?" Perda said. "He's a fire whistler."
Hearing his name, Zing let out another chirp.
"Not the dragon, silly," the tallest girl said, laughing.
"We mean those creatures." She pointed at the two boys.
"Zann and Darb?" Gliss said uncertainly. "What do you mean?"
"They're so odd!" the girl said. "We've never seen anything like them!
Are they dolls, made to look almost human?"
"Or perhaps some magical apparition?" Another girl looked excited. "We've heard tales of such things!"
"We're not dolls or apparitions," Zann said.
All the girls giggled and stared. "It speaks almost as if it understands us!" one exclaimed.
Gliss shook her head. "I don't understand. They're just boys."
"Boys?" The oldest girl echoed. "Is this a species related to humans?"
"Wow, you've really never seen boys before?" Perda sounded amazed. "How can that be?"
"Never mind," Zann said. "We're wasting time."
He glanced at the spot where the wormhole had been. "Is there magic in this world?"
The girls stared at him in wonder, not responding. Perda repeated Zann's question.
"Of course there's magic here," one of the girls told her.
Next Zann asked about Wyssa and Morb.
Once again the girls merely stared. But when Gliss repeated the question, the girls shook their heads.
"You're the first visitors in many moons," one said.
"Okay." Zann was already tired of the strange girls. "Then let's get going."
"Did you hear what it said?" a girl exclaimed.
"Yes. I'll fix it." The oldest girl let out a puff of air toward Zann and Darb.
Suddenly the two boys were completely immobilized!
"Hey!" Zann cried—or tried to anyway. He could barely move his lips.
"What did you do to them?" Perda demanded.
The girls giggled. "They're fine," one said.
"Yes," another said. "We don't want them to run off just yet, that's all.
First we must show them to Mother!"
Zann and his friends careened through the vortex.
They were moving so fast that the passing wormholes all blurred together.
Seconds later they crashed into another world.
There had been no chance of holding onto the edge of the wormhole this time.
Zann felt himself fly at least a dozen yards into the new world.
Splash!
"Drat!" Zann sat up and looked around.
The first thing he saw was the bright blue sky overhead.
Then he noticed a wormhole winking right beside the stream he was sitting in.
That was weird. How could it still be so close?
"Zann!" Perda cried. "Look!"
She pointed at some houses nearby. They were no taller than Zann's knee.
"Yes!" Zann cried. "We're here—oof!"
He was yanked off his feet. Mother's spell was still working!
The message stone pulled Zann and the others through the forest at such speed that Zann felt dizzy.
Thump!
"Ouch!" Zann blurted out as he bumped into something.
"Hey!" a disgruntled voice complained. "Watch where you're going."
Even before the person turned around, Zann knew exactly who it was.
"Wyssa!" He gasped. "Oh no!"
"What are you kids doing here?" Wyssa demanded.
"You?" Perda frowned at Wyssa as she brushed herself off.
Zann felt his heart sink as he realized the mistake.
"Mother's magic brought us to the stone's rightful owner—the last person who possessed it."
"Wyssa," Darb said, realization dawning on his face.
Zann nodded, feeling crushed. "I can't believe I got my hopes up," he mumbled.
"Stupid spell!" He tossed the message stone away.
Perda grabbed it. "You should keep the stone. It could still be a clue."
Zann frowned. "I never want to see that thing again."
Perda shrugged and tucked the stone into her own pocket.
Wyssa was glaring at all of them. "Well? Why aren't you kids in Magica?"
Gliss took a step backward. "Um . . ."
"Oh, never mind." Wyssa waved a gnarled hand.
"I don't care. The important thing is I've found him!
I've traced Morb to this world!" Her eyes glittered angrily.
"Really?" Zann still felt disappointed. But maybe all hope wasn't lost.
At least they'd found Wyssa. And if Morb was here, maybe Zann's parents were too.
"Is this World X?" Gliss asked.
"I believe so. Look!" Wyssa snapped her fingers.
Dozens of wormholes instantly winked into sight all around them!
Zann glanced into the nearest one. "That is so weird.
I don't see the vortex at all. Just a bunch of trees."
"I see a dragon through this one!" Gliss said.
"It's true!" Perda looked awed. "The wormholes here lead directly into other worlds."
"Wow." Darb said. "So we could step straight back into Magica if we found the right wormhole?"
"Yes!" Gliss sounded excited. "I wonder how we could find it?"
Zann ignored them. "So where's Morb?" he asked Wyssa. "How do you know he's here?"
"I have my ways." Wyssa looked grim.
"When I find him, I'm going to drag him straight through to Fardark, where I'll feed him to the first scatter beast I find!"
Zann gulped, thinking back to his time in Fardark.
For a second he almost felt sorry for Morb. Almost.
Just then a tiny man hurried into view. "Wyssa!" he exclaimed.
"I have news." He stopped short when he noticed Zann and the others. "Oh, you have company."
"Never mind them," Wyssa said. "Tell me what you know, Whistlefeather. Is he here?"
"Yes," Whistlefeather said fearfully. "Morb is indeed here in Rood.
And we've heard that he's brought prisoners from Magica with him!"
"Prisoners from Magica?" Zann blurted out. "That's got to be my parents!"
He grabbed Wyssa's sleeve. "We have to find them!"
"Thank you, my friend," Wyssa said to Whistlefeather.
She shook off Zann's hand. Then, snapping her fingers, she zapped out of sight.
"No!" Zann cried.
"It's okay, Zann." Perda reached into her pocket. "We still have this, remember?"
Zann and his friends barely had time to grab one another before they were whisked off again by Mother's spell.
They flew through the forest and up a steep hill before coming to an abrupt stop at a wall of rocks.
"You again!" Wyssa didn't seem pleased to see them. "Hush, or he'll hear us."
Zann glanced around. The rocks led to a gorge, on the other side of which was a massive waterfall.
Over the roar of the water, he could hear voices.
Zann peeked over the rocks and gasped. It was Morb!
"Keep your head down!" Wyssa hissed.
Another person stood between the evil villain and the edge of the cliff.
"Oh!" Gliss whispered, peering out beside Zann. "Is that Venna?"
Venna was staring at Morb, looking terrified.
"You can't do this!" she cried. "It's not right!"
Morb lifted a hand and rubbed his fingers together.
"I'm the one who decides what's right around here," he sneered.
"Now prepare to go for a little swim."
Venna glanced fearfully down at the water behind her. "No—p-please," she stammered.
"Why is she so scared?" Perda whispered.
"She must still not have magic," said Gliss.
"But she doesn't need magic to swim." Perda sidled closer to the cliff's edge.
When she looked down, she saw why Venna was so scared. "Oh no!"
"What?" Zann moved over to peer down as well. "Oh, wow—is that a gulper?"
"I guess now we know why Morb went to Skellia," Darb said grimly.
"You have to stop him!" Zann urged Wyssa. "You have to save Venna!"
But it was too late. Just then Morb snapped his fingers.
Venna screamed as magic energy shot from Morb's hand, sending her tumbling down into the gulper's waiting jaws!
"Oh no!" Zann exclaimed. He dropped the stone.
Instantly the vision of his parents was gone.
"What is it?" Perda asked. "Did you see them too?"
Zann nodded, too overwhelmed to speak. His parents had looked so real—and so scared!
"But why are we seeing them now?" Perda wondered.
"I've touched that stone lots of times."
"Message stones are mysterious things," Wyssa said.
"They hold on to the magical essence of all who touch them."
"That's how Mother used the stone to help us," Gliss put in.
"Mother? Who's that?" Venna asked.
Gliss, Perda, and Darb quickly told her about their adventure in Zon, the world with no boys.
"Interesting," Wyssa said when they'd finished.
"Mother's spell must have made the stone's messages stronger, allowing Perda to see them too."
"Does this mean Zann's parents are nearby?" Gliss asked.
Wyssa nodded. "Such magic works best when it's close to the source of the message."
"The source—you mean Zann's parents?" Darb asked. "Are they here in Rood?"
"It seems likely," said Wyssa.
Zann gasped. "Oh!"
Wyssa continued. "My guess is that Morb has just returned to wherever he's holding Zann's parents captive, and they became frightened."
"And their fear caused the stone to send that vision to whoever was touching it." Venna peered at the stone. "Fascinating!"
"If Morb is back with his prisoners, he probably found the Horn already," Perda pointed out.
"Not necessarily." Wyssa turned to Venna. "Tell me where it is."
"Wait!" Zann blurted out before Venna could respond. "Don't tell her."
"What?" Wyssa glared at Zann. "This is no time for games, boy."
Zann felt nervous, especially when he remembered how easily Wyssa had broken his Shackle spell. But he stood his ground.
"I know you want to punish Morb," he said.
"But first we need to find my parents.
Morb might be the only one who can lead us to them."
He expected Wyssa to get even angrier.
Instead she looked at the ground and sighed.
"You're right," she said. "This is my chance to make things right.
Not just by making Morb pay for what he's done, but also by doing what I can to help Nax and Asta."
"Thanks." Zann was relieved. He told Wyssa where they'd seen the Horn.
Her expression darkened again. "The only thing hiding it was some rubble?
I'm sure Morb had the Horn within seconds after leaving here."
"We need to find him before he uses it," Venna said.
"But how? I don't know if he has a lair here in Rood."
"I have an idea." Wyssa pursed her lips and whistled.
Several tiny people zapped into view. Whistlefeather was among them.
"Have you found him?" Whistlefeather asked eagerly. "Is Morb gone?"
"I'm afraid not," Wyssa said. "We need your help.
Does he have a lair in this world?"
Whistlefeather hesitated, trading a look with the other Roodians. "Yes, but . . ." His voice trailed off.
"We'd like to help," a Roodian woman said, her voice trembling.
"But we fear Morb's retribution. He's holding our queen prisoner."
"Your queen?" Zann recalled the tiny, frightened woman from his vision.
Whistlefeather nodded. "We're afraid that if we tell you where Morb's lair is, he'll toss the queen through the nearest wormhole."
Perda shrugged. "What's so bad about that?"
"It would kill her," Wyssa said grimly.
"The Roodians told me they cannot pass through any wormhole."
The Roodian woman nodded. "Many have tried in the past.
All were flung back into Rood—lifeless."
"Wow," Gliss said. "I guess that's why Rood stayed undiscovered for so long."
"Well, it explains why Roodians can't visit other worlds."
Perda glanced at a wormhole blinking nearby.
"But there are wormholes to so many other worlds here!
I'm surprised nobody has ever come through one of them."
"The wormholes here don't work like most wormholes," Whistlefeather said.
"One can pass from Rood to any other world.
But the wormholes only work in one direction.
Rood itself can only be reached via the vortex."
"Yes," Wyssa added. "And there's only one incoming wormhole in Rood.
It's very unpredictable." She sighed, rubbing her forehead.
"In any case, we can't endanger the queen. We'll have to find another way . . ."
"Wait." A young Roodian stepped forward. "Any other way will take too long. We'll tell you where Morb is."
"Prince Doni, no!" another Roodian exclaimed. "Your mother—"
"My mother would want us to help these people."
The prince squared his tiny shoulders. "She's the bravest person I know.
She would want to defeat Morb, no matter the risk to her own safety."
He snapped his fingers. A piece of parchment appeared in his hand.
"Morb is forcing many of our people to act as his servants, cleaning the lair and preparing food. They drew this map."
"Why would Morb need servants?" Darb wondered.
"He should be able to do that stuff with magic."
"He loves bossing people around," said Perda. "That's probably why."
Wyssa was examining the map. "Thank you," she told the Roodians.
"We'll try to rescue your queen if we can."
Prince Doni nodded his thanks. "But be careful!" he warned.
"The Gray Gorge is a dangerous place."
Zann wasn't worried about danger. He had to find his parents!
"What are we waiting for?" he said. "Let's go!"
Wyssa nodded. "Zap!"
Zann landed with a grunt on hard ground.
Looking up he saw a forbidding stone tower shrouded in ghostly gray fog.
He looked down and realized everyone was standing near the edge of a huge chasm.
It was so deep Zann couldn't see the bottom.
A howling wind whipped in and out of it, pulling in anything it could grab.
"Aah!" Zann cried as he felt himself suddenly losing balance.
"Help!" Gliss shrieked. The wind had knocked her down and was whipping her hair over her face.
She was now struggling to hang onto the edge of the chasm.
"Hold on!" Darb lunged toward her, but he ended up almost falling over the edge himself.
Zing flew overhead, whistling with alarm. A gust of wind grabbed the dragon, tossing him end over end.
"To me!" Wyssa shouted.
Suddenly Zann felt himself being grabbed by magical energy.
It yanked him backward, away from the terrifying drop-off.
Soon the entire group was safely out of the wind's reach.
"Wow, that was close!" Perda exclaimed.
Venna nodded. "No wonder Prince Doni warned us that the Gray Gorge was very dangerous."
Darb stared up at the stone tower. "That looks like Morb's kind of place."
"Yeah," Zann agreed. "And my parents are in there!"
His heart pounded at the thought that they might be so close.
After all this time, was he finally going to be with them again?
"How are we going to get in there?" Gliss wondered.
"Good question," Zann muttered. The tower was perched halfway across a narrow, ancient-looking stone bridge spanning the Gray Gorge.
"Prince Doni said Morb built this place," Perda said.
"It must have taken a lot of magic to do that, especially in a spot like this."
"Indeed." Wyssa sounded grim. "It seems he must have figured out a new way to steal magic. Lots of magic."
Zann studied the tower. "The wind will make it hard to cross the bridge without falling into the gorge," he said.
"But otherwise, it doesn't look that bad.
The gate is small enough to step over."
He pointed to a short gate blocking the entrance to the bridge.
"I suppose it's only meant to keep Roodians out," Venna said.
"Yeah. Or keep them in," Gliss added.
"I doubt they're thrilled to be Morb's servants."
"So what are we waiting for?" Perda took a step toward the bridge.
Wyssa narrowed her eyes. "It seems odd that there's no sentry."
"Yes, it does," Venna said. "I'm sure Morb must have some sort of Shield spell on the place."
"There's only one way to find out. Come on!"
Zann hurried toward the bridge. Bracing himself against the gusty wind, he stepped over the gate. Perda was right behind him.
"Wait," Wyssa called from the other side of the gate. She pointed past Zann. "What's that?"
Zann peered through the fog. Something was sitting on the bridge just ahead. It was small and fluffy.
"Oh!" Zann exclaimed. "It must be the missing mibbit!"
"Aw, it's cute." Perda smiled and stepped forward.
"Wait," Zann said. "It looks kind of tense."
"Here, mibbit, mibbit!" Perda cooed. She grabbed for the creature. It squawked and leaped back.
"Careful, don't panic it or—" Zann gasped as a shock wave of magic energy hit him. He saw Perda collapse to her knees.
The mibbit was sending out confusing energy waves, just like Vee had described!
Zann had never felt anything like it before.
He couldn't move or think clearly. Unlike with the scatter beast attack, though, there was no pain.
Still, he felt completely helpless. What if Morb looked out a window and spotted him and Perda on the bridge?
He heard moans from behind him. With great effort he turned his head far enough to see the others.
Venna was clinging to a tree, gasping for breath.
Gliss was on the ground, helpless—and sliding toward he dizzying drop-off! Zing wasn't far behind her.
Zann wanted to save them. But he still couldn't move.
In fact, he realized he and Perda were dangerously close to the edge too.
He looked for Wyssa, hoping she could help them.
But she looked just as helpless as the others.
She'd stopped herself from rolling over the edge by clutching the gate.
But Zann could see that her grip was weakening.
Another wave of magic struck them all.
Zann felt himself teetering on the edge of the bridge.
Was this the end for him—for all of them?
Then he saw movement near the gate.
He couldn't turn his head, but he rolled his eyes far enough to see what was happening.
It was Darb! He was jumping over the small gate.
Dodging Zann and Perda, Darb hurried over to the mibbit.
"Easy, little fellow," Darb said soothingly.
He gently picked up the mibbit and stroked its ears, just as Vee had taught them.
A moment later the energy waves were gone.
"Whoa!" Perda gasped, sitting up and moving herself away from the drop-off.
Zann did the same. "Thanks, Darb," he said.
"But why didn't the mibbit's magic affect you?"
Darb shrugged, cuddling the mibbit. The fluffy creature looked happy and relaxed now.
"Maybe it's because I'm a Void," he said.
"I don't have any magic for the mibbit to affect."
Wyssa nodded. "I think you must be right, boy."
Zing flew toward Darb. He circled him, sniffing at the mibbit curiously.
"Down, boy," Zann told his dragon. "That mibbit is not a snack!"
Venna brushed the dirt off her clothes and frowned at the mibbit.
"I'm guessing that thing was supposed to be Morb's security guard," she said. "Shall we proceed?"
Zann opened his mouth to say yes.
But his words were lost as an eerie howl echoed from the depths of the gorge.
Gliss' eyes widened. "What was that?"
Before anyone could respond, a huge head on a long, snakelike neck arose from the dark gorge.
The orange glow of its eyes cut through the fog like flames.
With a loud roar, the creature exposed a mouth full of sharp fangs.
Wyssa went pale. "It's the Beast of the Otherworld!"
"The Beast of the Otherworld?" Zann echoed. "What's that?"
He didn't recognize the creature from his parents' books.
And he was sure he'd remember something that looked like that!
"It's the most horrible beast in all the worlds." Wyssa shuddered.
"How was Morb able to transport it from its home on Narakan?"
"Narakan?" Venna sounded startled. "I thought that world was only a myth."
"Apparently not," Wyssa said. The creature hissed, and a dark, viscous substance dripped from its jaws and sizzled on the stone bridge.
"How big is that thing, anyway?" Perda cried as the enormous head rose even higher.
"Big!" Zann answered. "And it doesn't seem to be in a good mood either!"
The Beast let out a hoarse, echoing cry.
Then its head snaked toward Zann and the others.
"Run!" Venna shouted.
The humans scattered. Zann lunged toward the gate and skidded across the rough stone on his hands and knees.
When he glanced back, the Beast was raising its head again.
Zann noticed that the dark goo wasn't coming from its mouth after all.
It was oozing out of its head.
"Look out!" Gliss screamed. "It's going to strike again!"
Spurting angry flames, Zing flew toward the Beast.
"Zing, no!" Zann shouted. "It's going to eat you!"
The Beast snapped at the small dragon. Zing barely escaped.
"We have to zap away!" Gliss cried, grabbing Darb's hand.
"No!" Wyssa said. "That's the worst thing we can do.
If the legends are true, the Beast can catch hold of Transport spells and pull its victims back—straight into its jaws."
"So we're trapped?" Perda snapped her fingers, and a sword appeared in her hand. "Then we'll have to fight."
Zann stared at her for a second. When had Perda become so brave?
He couldn't imagine any other kid his age facing down a monster so calmly.
But this was no time to think about such things.
Rubbing his hands together, Zann conjured his own sword.
"Stand back, kids," Venna called. "I'm going to blast it."
"Wait," Wyssa said. "I don't think that will—"
Blast!
A bolt of energy shot out of Venna's hands.
It flew straight at the Beast. The Beast opened its giant mouth . . .
Gulp!
"Did the Beast just eat the Blast spell?" Gliss cried.
Zann didn't have time to answer as he dodged another sizzling drop of slime.
He found himself beside Darb, who was still cradling the mibbit.
"The mibbit doesn't seem too worried," Zann commented.
Darb nodded. "Vee told us the effects of the ear-rubbing would last a few hours, remember?" he said.
"Too bad. I bet the mibbit was the only thing holding the Beast back before."
"You're probably right. No wonder the mibbit was tense with that thing around." Zann glanced up. "Get back!"
He and Darb leaped away in opposite directions.
The Beast's head slammed down, shaking the whole bridge.
"Hurry! Run while it's stunned!" Perda shouted.
"Maybe it won't be able to climb out of that pit and chase us."
Zann sprinted for the gate. He was only halfway there when a shimmering wall of magic energy shot up in front of him.
"What's that?" Venna cried.
Zann didn't answer. He lowered his head and ran straight toward the magical wall.
But he bounced off it and stumbled into Darb.
"Oof," Darb grunted. He fell backward, almost slipping off the edge of the bridge.
To catch himself, he had to drop the mibbit.
The fuzzy creature landed on its feet and just stood there, flicking its ears lazily.
"Look out!" Perda yelled. "The Beast is coming for you guys!"
Zann grabbed Darb and dragged him away from the Beast.
The Beast's orange eyes glowed, and another wall of magic energy sprang up inside the first.
"Why did it make another wall? The first one seemed to be working pretty well." Zann winced, touching his shoulder.
He would definitely have a bruise to heal later—if he survived this.
"I think it's herding us back toward itself."
Suddenly Perda looked scared. "Look! It's drooling."
"This is hopeless!" Gliss cried, her voice shaking.
"The Beast is going to eat us, and there's nothing we can do about it!"
Darb grabbed the mibbit. "Isn't there anything you can do?" he asked Wyssa and Venna.
Wyssa was peering at the magic walls. "Let me think, let me think," she muttered. "There must be a way . . ."
Zann glanced from Wyssa to his friends.
Perda and Gliss were clinging to each other, looking terrified.
Zing was hiding behind Venna. Darb, cradling the mibbit, was looking nervously at the Beast.
The hideous creature was sizing them up, as if deciding whom to eat first.
Suddenly Zann's eyes lit up. "I've got it! Everyone run toward the tower!"
"What?" Venna said. "Are you crazy?"
Zann didn't answer; he raced along the bridge toward the tower.
Perda caught up to him. "Zann, the door is bolted shut!
And we won't have time to try to open it with a spell. The Beast will have us cornered!"
"Just go." Zann shoved her forward and then turned to make sure the others were following.
Wyssa was the last to run past. She gave Zann a strange look.
"I hope you know what you're doing, boy."
Zann hoped so too. He glanced at the Beast, which was already gathering itself for another attack.
As the huge head snaked toward him, Zann sprinted after the others.
He could feel the creature's hot breath on the back of his neck.
A drop of viscous goo landed on his shoulder, burning right through his shirt.
Zann yelped in pain. He picked up speed, trying not to imagine the Beast's sharp teeth digging into his skin.
"Uh-oh." Zann stared after the flizzes. "What now?"
"Should we use magic to find our way?" Venna suggested.
"We might as well," Gliss said. "Wyssa used magic to create that knife just now."
She rubbed her neck where the tree had grabbed her.
"That was minor magic," Wyssa said. "Any kind of searching or mapping spell would be—oh, hello."
A Roodian servant was rushing toward them.
"The prince sent me to help you," he said in a hushed, urgent tone.
"He realized you'd never find the queen and the other prisoners.
Morb has put a Bewilderment spell over this whole place."
"I knew it!" Wyssa muttered.
"But we servants need to be able to find our way around to do our jobs."
The Roodian cast a nervous look around as he showed them a small object.
"That's why Morb gave each of us one of these."
Perda gasped. "A talisman! Just like the one Morb used to control the trolls!"
The Roodian handed the talisman to Wyssa.
"It blocks the effects of the Bewilderment spell.
Now you'll be able to find the prisoners' cell."
He quickly told them the way and then scurried off.
With Wyssa in the lead, Zann and the others followed the Roodian's directions.
Soon they reached a large, dimly lit chamber.
A haze of odorless smoke made it impossible to see more than a few steps ahead.
"This should be the cell." Zann peered in. "Do you guys see anything?"
"I can't see a thing through all this misty stuff," Gliss complained.
Zann took a few careful steps forward, waving a hand to clear the haze. "I think I see something . . ."
Zann's voice trailed off; his eyes widened in horror.
A scatter beast was stepping out of the mist!
Zann's heart raced. His head filled with memories of his last scatter beast encounter.
He tried to speak, to warn his friends.
But his voice seemed frozen in his throat.
"Was that Roodian servant working for Morb?" he thought with a shudder.
"Did he send us straight into a trap?"
The scatter beast paused, its tentacle waving lazily as it shambled closer.
"No!" Venna shouted. But Zann barely noticed; all he could do was stare at the horrifying creature moving toward him.
Suddenly there was a loud squawk. Zing flew around Zann and the others, spitting fire and whistling urgently.
"Zing, what are you doing?" Zann mumbled, barely feeling the burn of Zing's flames. "Save yourself."
Zing let out a chirp of irritation and flew out of sight.
For a moment Zann thought the dragon had taken his advice and escaped the way they'd come in.
Then Zann heard another whistle. A second later something thumped into his back—hard.
"Hey!" Zann blurted out as he stumbled forward.
He was about to fall right on top of the scatter beast! "No—oof!"
He landed hard on the stone floor of the chamber.
"Huh?" Zann muttered. He couldn't see the scatter beast anymore.
Zann leaped to his feet and backed up a few steps.
Suddenly the scatter beast was there again, in the same spot where Zann had just fallen!
Zing landed beside the scatter beast. The beast didn't seem to notice the dragon at all.
Zann's wild heartbeat slowed. For the first time, he realized he wasn't feeling the pain and other crazy magical effects he'd felt in Fardark.
The only thing immobilizing him was his fear.
Taking a cautious step forward, Zann reached for the scatter beast. His hand passed right through it!
"It's an illusion!" Zann shouted with relief. "The scatter beast isn't real!"
He glanced around. Everyone else, except Zing, was staring straight ahead, looking terrified.
"S-scatter beast?" Perda's eyes never left the blank spot right in front of her.
"I'd be happy to see a scatter beast right now.
Maybe it would scare away that huge swarm of tickle bugs!"
"Tickle bugs?" Zann wrinkled his nose. Tickle bugs had ten legs and whirligig wings and liked to land on people.
They were annoying, but they weren't scary. Well, except to Perda.
Suddenly Zann remembered that Perda was terrified of the goofy insects. He'd once scared her with one.
"I get it," he muttered. "Guys, none of this is real!" he said loudly.
"Whatever you're seeing—tickle bugs, scatter beasts—they're just another one of Morb's spells.
Somehow he's making us each see whatever scares us the most."
Venna still didn't move. "Maybe you're right.
But that cave hisser sure looks real to me.
And everyone knows they don't like sudden movements."
Zann sighed and then glanced at Zing. "Come on, little buddy. Let's show them."
The two of them jumped in front of each person, revealing that whatever each was seeing wasn't real.
"Thank goodness!" Gliss stumbled backward. "I was sure that thunder charger was going to eat me!"
Darb nodded. "I thought I was about to fall into a deep, dark hole."
"What did you see?" Perda asked Wyssa.
Zann waited for Wyssa's answer. What could possibly terrify someone like her?
"It's not important." Wyssa frowned, peering farther into the misty room.
"This type of spell is very complex and difficult to cast.
With so many real creatures roaming his lair, Morb would only bother to use a spell like this to protect something very important."
She muttered a few words under her breath. Then she waved a hand.
"Reveal!" she intoned.
The chamber seemed to melt away, revealing that it had all been an illusion.
Zann and the others found themselves standing in an icy cave.
A tiny woman was frozen in a block of ice.
She was motionless, except for her eyes, which darted pleadingly from one person to the next.
"Can you show us Morb's contraption?" Venna asked the queen.
"I'm not sure exactly where it is," the queen replied.
"But now I understand why Morb forced me to tell him where he could find the Magica wormholes.
We'll probably find the contraption near one of them."
"You know how to find the wormholes leading to Magica?" Perda asked.
"As the ruler of this world, I'm the only one who knows the location of every wormhole."
The tiny queen stretched proudly to her full height.
"I'm also the only one with the power to instantly summon every wormhole in Rood to me."
"Really?" Gliss exclaimed. "Can you do that now? Summon all the Magica wormholes?
Then Morb can't do whatever horrible thing he's planning to do!"
The queen smiled faintly. "I'm afraid it doesn't work that way.
I can't summon individual wormholes. Only all of them at once.
We would be overwhelmed by every wormhole to every world there is."
"Oh." Perda sounded disappointed. "Too bad."
Zann felt impatient. "Then how are we going to get to wherever Morb's new contraption is?"
"Follow me," said the queen.
She started down the hallway. Zann and the others followed.
"There are multiple wormholes to Magica," Zann said.
"How do you know which one Morb will be near?"
"There's only one Magica wormhole within the walls of this fortress," the queen replied.
"I expect that's the one Morb is planning to use."
As he ran, Zann felt something burning him.
At first he thought it was Zing flying too close.
Then he realized it was the message stone in his pocket. It was fiery hot.
"Hurry," he urged. "We must be almost there!"
"We are. It's just ahead." The queen led the way through an arch.
Zann followed, and then immediately skidded to a stop.
They were in a stone room with an enormous contraption in the middle.
Like Morb's previous machines, this one was hideous and made up of many different parts.
The first thing Zann noticed was two large, glowing horns sticking out of the top.
The second thing he noticed was his parents.
Their arms and legs were shackled together, and Morb was shoving them up against the terrible machine!
"Stop!" Zann shouted. "Mom, Dad—it's me!"
"Zann!" his mother cried.
"Zann?" Morb echoed with a scowl. He gestured to several trolls that were hanging around in the corner. "Grab them, you fools!"
Zann tried to duck away, but there was nowhere to run.
The trolls grabbed Zann and the others.
"Don't kill them," Morb ordered the trolls.
"Not just yet, anyway." He smirked at Wyssa.
"I didn't expect to see you again."
He widened his gaze to include all of them.
"Or any of you, for that matter.
But now that you're here, I hope you'll stick around and enjoy the show."
Zann heard Wyssa muttering under her breath. Morb heard it too.
"Let me guess," Morb sneered. "You're planning to try some powerful, little-known spell you've learned during your travels.
Don't bother—it's too late. My new pets have already latched onto their victims."
He waved a hand toward the contraption.
Tiny creatures, hundreds of them, were swarming out of a tank in the center of the contraption.
The creatures looked like small, brightly colored cave crawlers.
Zann gasped in horror as the small rodents scampered all over his parents.
"Memory mice!" Wyssa spat. "Of course! I should have guessed you'd use them."
"What are memory mice?" Darb asked.
"They feed on people's memories," Wyssa said.
"Their feeding has the side effect of creating very strong magical energy."
"They eat memories?" Gliss frowned. "How awful!"
"Not necessarily," said Wyssa. "In their home world, they're a beloved and valuable species.
They help people by deleting painful memories.
They also create much useful energy out of useless or unwanted memories."
Zann struggled to free himself from the troll holding him. "Mom, Dad!" he called.
"I'm afraid your parents can't answer you, boy," Morb said.
"They're busy right now—having all their memories devoured."
"Like anything," Wyssa went on, "memory mice can be used for evil."
She shot Morb a disgusted look. "Normally a person must invite the mice to latch on, and they only feed for a limited amount of time.
Morb must have overridden that instinct with some kind of spell."
"Clever, isn't it?" Morb smiled. "My Memory Machine can use any memories to summon the power it needs.
I could have used my Roodian servants.
Even trolls' feeble brains have enough memories to work."
He chuckled. "But I liked the irony of using Magica memories to destroy Magica.
Besides, I already had these two as my prisoners.
They were very useful in helping me find my way to Rood."
"Your only true talent is holding a grudge," Wyssa retorted.
"It's not Nax and Asta's fault you were born a Void."
Morb ignored her. "I'm glad you're here, Zann.
Perhaps you can be useful to me at last.
I've ordered the mice to drain your parents of all memories of Magica.
If that's not enough to fill the machine . . ."
He touched a large clear tube on one side, which was rapidly filling with glowing, sparking magic energy.
"Well, then perhaps I'll have to top it off with your memories."
"No!" Zann blurted out.
"Wait," Perda said. "What happens when the tube is full?"
"Why, then all I have to do is open this hatch," said Morb, smiling wickedly.
"The energy will get sucked through any wormhole within range.
As it happens, the only wormhole in this room leads directly into Wyssa's old home of Wormwood."
Venna looked nervous. "And then what happens?"
"Then the energy will explode," Morb said. "Blowing all of Magica to smithereens!"
"You can't destroy Magica!" Perda cried to Morb.
She turned to Wyssa. "You have to stop him!"
Wyssa said nothing. She was staring at the contraption in horror.
"It's too late," Morb sneered. "No one can stop me now!"
Zann stared at his parents. Their bodies twitched as the memory mice scampered over them.
"Are the mice really sucking out my parents' memories?" he asked.
"That's right, boy," Morb said. "But don't worry.
Once their memories are emptied, I'll have no further use for your parents. You can have them back."
Zann shuddered. He'd never imagined there could be anything worse than being separated from his parents.
Now he wasn't so sure. He couldn't stand the thought of finding them just in time to watch them forget everything.
Would they remember their old home in First City?
Or that family vacation they'd all taken to the Flower Forest?
Would they even remember him?
Morb turned to the Roodian queen. "I'm glad you're here to witness this," he taunted.
"Without you, it never could have happened."
Still thinking about the past, Zann stared at his parents.
Then he noticed a couple of memory mice sniffing curiously in his direction.
He looked over at Wyssa. "How do people invite the mice to eat their memories?" he whispered.
She appeared confused. "Simply by opening their minds to them."
"Good." Zann glanced at his friends and Venna.
"Start thinking about Magica," he whispered.
"Any memories you can come up with.
And invite the mice to come to you."
"What?" Perda looked alarmed. "You mean ask those things to eat our memories?"
Zann nodded. "There are five of us, and only two of my parents," he said.
"Maybe we can draw the mice away!"
Morb glanced over. "What are you whispering about over there?" he snapped.
"You should be grateful that you're here to see this.
Otherwise you'd have only moments to live." He smirked.
"Of course, I can't guarantee you have much longer than that.
The Beast of the Otherworld is always hungry."
Zann ignored Morb and focused his thoughts on home.
As more and more memories flooded his mind, Zann tried to send them toward the mice, inviting them to share.
One mouse wiggled its nose. Then it jumped down from Zann's father and took a step toward Zann.
A second mouse followed, and then a third.
Soon all the mice were scampering across the room, headed for Zann and his friends.
"N-now what?" Gliss asked nervously, backing away as far as the troll restraining her would let her.
Once again Morb had turned away to taunt the Roodian queen.
When he finally noticed the memory mice moving away from his machine, he let out a howl of fury.
"To me!" Wyssa intoned at the same time.
Zann held his breath as Wyssa's spell grabbed his parents and dragged them over to join the others.
A split second later, the trolls were flung against the walls, and a Shield spell appeared around the rest of the group.
"No!" Morb flung a bolt of energy at Wyssa.
But it bounced off the glowing shield and ricocheted around the room.
Zann hardly noticed. His parents looked dazed and weak.
They stared at him blankly, and for a moment he was afraid it was too late.
Then his mother's eyes brightened. "Zann?" she whispered, reaching out to touch his face. "Is it really you?"
Zann's father smiled feebly. "We've missed you so much, son."
"They remember you!" Perda exclaimed.
"Of course we do," Zann's mother said. "But my head feels so fuzzy . . ."
"You're lucky. The mice probably didn't focus on any particular memory," Wyssa told Zann's parents.
"They just nibbled away here and there.
You two will be weak for a while, but your memories should come back."
Zann finally looked out through the shield.
Morb was gnashing his teeth and stalking back and forth, occasionally blasting a troll.
"It's not enough!" he cried. "I still don't have enough power!"
"He's right. Look!" Perda pointed to the tube.
The glowing energy stopped just short of the top.
Morb snarled and then climbed into the machine!
"Even a Void has memories," he hissed.
"I suppose mine will work just as well as any.
I have a few childhood memories I wouldn't mind getting rid of!"
Venna gasped. "We have to do something!"
"Stand back," Wyssa said grimly.
She waved a hand, and the shield disappeared.
Wyssa sent a huge Blast spell flying toward the contraption. But it stopped short, fizzling away.
"It's not working!" Gliss cried.
"I can see that, girl," Wyssa snapped.
"The power of the Horns is blocking all magic."
"Maybe I can still get through." Darb handed the mibbit to Gliss and then rushed toward the machine.
But some unseen force bounced him back.
He landed on the stone floor with a grunt.
Venna paled. "There's no way to stop him! Magica is doomed!"
Morb cackled as the mice continued to feed.
His body slumped weakly, but his eyes glittered with triumph.
"How do you like that?" he spat.
"It took a Void to figure out how to focus enough magic energy to destroy Magica." He grinned nastily.
"Then again, who else but a Void could really appreciate the true power of magic energy? Others take it for granted.
But I could see how something that's harmless when used for small spells can be devastating when used for large ones!"
"What are we going to do?" Perda cried.
Zann didn't answer. All he could do was watch as the tube filled to the top.
Morb brushed the mice off himself and got out of the machine.
His mouth curled into an evil smile as he flung the hatch open.
Zann stared in horror as the energy flowed toward a wormhole blinking in the corner.
Through the opening he caught a glimpse of the rough bark of the ancient Wormwood tree.
It was too late—Magica was about to be destroyed!
Suddenly Zann had an idea. He turned to the queen.
"Your Majesty, summon all the wormholes!"
For a second the Roodian queen looked confused. Then her eyes widened.
She raised a hand, and the air buzzed with new energy.
"What are you doing?" Morb snarled, still weakened from the mice's feeding.
Suddenly the room was flooded with thousands of wormholes!
Morb looked stunned. "What—how—" he stammered.
Zann held his breath, hoping he was right about what would happen next.
If he was wrong, he might have just destroyed not only Magica, but also every other world.
He glanced through a nearby wormhole. In a world he didn't recognize, a funny-looking dragon was nibbling on a tree.
Bzzt! A tiny spurt of energy snaked in and fizzled out against the dragon's scaly side.
Zann spun around and spotted the rough seas of Skellia through another wormhole.
Bzzt! A gulper leaped up and swallowed a small blob of energy hovering over the waves.
Everywhere he looked, Zann saw bits of energy fizzling out harmlessly in various worlds.
"It worked!" he cried. "The energy got divided into so many different worlds that it became completely harmless!"
"But how did you know that would happen?" Perda asked.
Zann shrugged. "It was what Morb said about how something that's powerful in large amounts is harmless in small amounts."
Morb gnashed his teeth. "I should have killed you when I had the chance!"
"But you didn't." Wyssa stepped forward and snapped her fingers.
Instantly Morb was shackled to her. Then she pointed at the contraption and muttered a few words. Both horns exploded into shrapnel.
Zann and the others ducked, covering their heads until the dust settled. Then Venna stood up.
"Now what are we going to do with Morb?" she asked. "There will have to be a trial."
"Agreed," Zann's mother said. "Nax and I will have plenty of evidence to present."
Zann's father nodded. "I imagine the Red Council will banish him to the Wastelands forever."
Wyssa scowled. "I'll save you all the trouble."
She yanked at Morb, who struggled weakly.
"No!" he cried. "Don't let her take me!"
Zann winced, remembering what Wyssa had said about feeding Morb to a scatter beast.
Then he looked at his parents. Because of Morb, Zann had almost lost them all over again.
Still, did even Morb deserve the fate Wyssa had in mind for him?
"Wait!" Gliss stepped forward. "After you're finished with him"—she glanced at Morb— "will you do something else?"
"What is it, girl?" Wyssa sounded impatient.
"We visited a world called Skellia," Gliss said.
"The waters were rising, and the people were scared. Can you help them?"
Wyssa raised an eyebrow in surprise. "I know Skellia," she said.
Her voice softened. "And yes, if the Skellians are ready to leave, I can help."
Darb stepped forward too. "Also, can you return this mibbit to Pax?"
"Of course. The Paxians must be worried about him."
Wyssa waited while Darb rubbed the creature's ears before handing it over.
Then she glanced around. "Any other errands you need me to handle for you?"
Her tone was sharp, but Zann caught a twinkle in her eye.
"I think that's it," he said, "but . . ." He hesitated, staring at Morb.
"What are you going to do with him?"
"Only what he deserves." Wyssa gave a jerk on the shackles.
"I'm sure the queen can help direct you all home. Good-bye."
Dragging Morb, Wyssa stepped into the wormhole.
The evil villain cried, "No!"
"Are we there yet?" Zann joked as he and his parents walked toward their house.
Zing was circling overhead, whistling joyfully.
"You tell me, son," his father joked back. "I've never been here before."
After Wyssa had departed with Morb, the Roodian queen sorted through the wormholes.
First she located the one leading into Wormwood, which Venna used to return to First City.
Then, after a long search, the queen found the one leading into Swamp Bottom.
"I can't wait to see what Boz has done with the interior," Zann's father said when they stopped in front of their house.
His wife chuckled. "Don't expect too much," she warned.
"My father was never much of a decorator."
They headed inside. There was no sign of Boz.
"Look!" Zann's mother exclaimed. "Those are the blink images from our trip to the Flower Forest."
She and Zann's father hurried over for a closer look.
Meanwhile Zann heard footsteps. A moment later his grandfather burst into the room.
"Zann!" Boz exclaimed. He rushed over and hugged Zann tightly.
Then he gently shoved him away and glared.
"Where in all the worlds have you been?
I've been worried sick! The Directory showed nothing of your whereabouts, and every spell I tried was—"
Zann's mother stepped up behind Boz.
"Hello, Dad," she said. "Did you miss me too?"
Boz's jaw dropped. "Asta?" he whispered.
Then, his nose quivering wildly and his eyes widening, he spun around.
"And Nax too! What—how did you . . .?"
Zann laughed. "We'll tell you all about it!"
That night Zann fell asleep happy. At one point, in the middle of the night, he was awakened by a terrible dream.
Morb had escaped! And Zann's parents were in trouble . . .
But as Zann looked around, he remembered where he was.
He was back in his own bed. His parents and Boz were nearby.
Zing's fiery breath was warming his toes.
For the first time in four years, Zann felt content.
It was a beautiful day in First City, and the streets buzzed with energy.
At the edge of Treeview Park, the king and queen of Magica were speaking to a large gathering.
Angry people held banners and signs. Some signs were magical, with flashing messages that changed words or colors.
Others were plain signs written by hand.
There had been many protests lately, and now the king and queen were trying to calm down the crowd.
A square-jawed man watched from a balcony overlooking the park.
His big hands rested on a railing, and a door behind him was open to an opulent apartment.
"Void rights," he muttered. "What a concept. Seems popular though."
Suddenly he gasped, his knees buckling as his head exploded with pain.
Pressing his hands to his head, he staggered through the door and collapsed onto a sofa.
A moment later the pain faded, and his eyes opened wide with surprise.
"Who is this?" he exclaimed. "How are you—?"
He paused, listening to a voice only he could hear. Then he nodded.
"Yes, of course I remember you. Who could forget?"
He barked out a short, humorless laugh. "But I thought you were dead!
That crazy old woman told the palace that she was going to . . ."
His words trailed off and he cocked his head, listening again.
