"Yes, I see," he said. "Well, I'm glad.
I've missed your business. But where are you now?"
A loud cheer rose from the gathering below, but the man hardly heard it.
The voice in his head was speaking again.
"Who? Oh," the man said. "Yes, I can do that."
This time when he listened, he frowned.
He rose to his feet and began pacing.
"I never fail!" he snapped. "Never! Besides, I know the perfect person to help us."
Another brief pause followed. "Of course I know who is trustworthy.
If you doubt my judgment, perhaps you should find someone else!"
He listened again, his mouth curving into a slight smile. Finally he nodded.
"Yes, I'm glad you see that." He wandered back onto the balcony and glanced at the scene below.
"It's a deal. We shall make them all pay!"
He laughed along with the voice in his head. "I'll begin immediately."
"See you tomorrow, Zann," someone called.
Zann waved without looking to see who'd spoken, and then stepped outside.
After two months at First City Academy, he knew most of the kids' names.
But he still didn't feel as if he had true friends.
"Not like back home in Swamp Bottom," he thought.
Zann grimaced, reminding himself that Swamp Bottom wasn't "home" anymore.
Rubbing his fingers together, he stepped away from the building and muttered, "Zap!"
Splash!
Zann looked around. He was standing in a neighbor's decorative fountain.
"Drat," Zann said.
The neighbor was picking flutter flowers nearby.
"Sorry," Zann said to her.
She looked irritated for a second before her expression changed.
"Oh, it's young Zann, the hero!" she exclaimed.
"How are you? And how are those worlds-traveling parents of yours?"
"Fine, thanks," Zann said politely. "Excuse me, I have to go."
It still felt strange when people treated him like a celebrity.
Months had passed, but it still happened all the time.
He hurried over to his house. When he opened the front door, Zing flew out.
The dragon chattered and spat flames.
"Sorry I'm late," Zann told Zing. "I had to stay after school for an assembly about Void rights.
The headmaster said that we're all supposed to work at getting along—Reds, Voids, dragons . . ."
Zann hadn't been paying much attention to the Void rights protests.
But the assembly had made him think about Darb.
And that made him homesick for Swamp Bottom again.
He hadn't seen Darb for more than two months—nor their friends Perda and Gliss.
Zing started zipping around overhead, sending flames everywhere. Zann conjured some dragon treats.
"It's okay, boy," he called, tossing Zing the treats.
"I know you've been stuck in the house all day.
But now we can go to Palace Park and play.
I just have to stop by the lab first to tell Mom and Dad where we're going."
Zann considered sending his parents a message moth.
Luckily, they'd stopped monitoring his every move.
But for a month or so after Morb had been banished from Magica, Zann had had to check in with his parents all the time.
Zann tried to grab Zing to zap them both to the lab.
But the little dragon wouldn't hold still long enough.
"Okay, I guess we'll walk," Zann said with a shrug.
He headed down the street, whistling for Zing to follow.
Zing sped past him, diving to shoot flames at a passing flip fly.
"Hey!" A man cried, jumping aside as the flames missed the fly and almost hit him.
"Oops," Zann called and grabbed Zing by the wing.
"Come on, little buddy, let's take the quick way."
Zap!
They landed across the street from the lab where Zann's parents worked.
Zing yanked free immediately, diving down to attack a wiggle weed growing out of a crack in the sidewalk.
Zann hardly noticed. He stared at a group of about a dozen people.
They were marching around in front of him holding a Void rights banner.
Several people stood nearby and watched the marchers.
"Not another protest!" Zann muttered, shaking his head.
He forgot about that when he saw a message moth fluttering toward him. Zing saw it too.
"Zing, stop!" Zann grabbed the moth before the dragon could incinerate it.
Zann smiled when he spotted several names scrawled on one wing.
The moth had come from his friends in Swamp Bottom!
Before he could read their message, he heard a shout of anger.
"Give that back, you fire-breathing thief!"
Zann stuck the message moth in his pocket and then grabbed Zing.
The little dragon had snatched a glowberry muffin away from one of the people watching the protest. The man looked angry.
"Zing!" Zann wrenched the muffin out of Zing's mouth.
It had teeth marks and burns on it.
Zann looked at the man. "I'll conjure you another one, sir."
"You'd better!" the man grumbled. "There's a reason most people don't keep fire whistlers as pets, you know."
Suddenly his expression changed and he peered closely at Zann.
"Wait, a fire whistler—hold on. Are you the Red kid who saved Magica from Morb?"
Zann never knew what to say when people asked him questions like that.
He couldn't have saved anything without help from his friends and others.
So he said nothing. Instead he rubbed his hands together to create a new glowberry muffin.
But the man brushed it away. "I'm a reporter for the First City Flash.
I came here to cover this protest, but nothing much is happening."
With a snap of his fingers, he opened a note window in the air beside him.
"I'd love to get your opinion on all the recent protests in First City," the reporter went on.
"I'm sure everyone in Magica would love to know what their young Red hero thinks of the Void rights movement!"
Zann shrugged. "I haven't been paying much attention," he answered truthfully.
"I'm completely in favor of Void rights, of course.
Other than that, I'm not very interested in politics."
Zann's words appeared on the note window as he said them.
"But you must have heard what people are saying."
The reporter glanced at Zann's bright red hair.
"Some non-Reds think the Red Council is almost as greedy as Morb himself.
They say the Reds have too much power, and allowing them to control the relics Morb dug up is dangerous.
They say that Magica's ancient relics belong to all citizens, and that the people should have a say in what happens to them. Not the Red Council."
Zann had heard those comments. But he hadn't paid much attention to them.
The relics were dangerous—that much he knew.
They could have given Morb enough power to take over all of Magica.
But Zann trusted his parents and the others to handle the relics wisely now.
"I'm sure my parents are doing what they think is best," he said.
"But you’d have to ask them about the details."
The reporter frowned at the note window.
He seemed disappointed. Then he shrugged and brightened.
"All right, then," the reporter said. "What's going on with you these days, Zann?
I'm sure everyone would enjoy hearing an update on your life since Morb's, er, permanent departure."
Zann winced at the last two words.
Nobody ever came right out and said that Morb was dead.
But Zann suspected he was. Wyssa had been furious when she'd dragged the villain through the vortex.
But she'd never returned to Magica after that, so nobody knew for sure what she'd done with Morb.
"I really need to go," Zann said, glancing toward his parents' lab.
"This will only take a moment." The reporter smiled.
"How are those friends of yours doing?
I understand they returned to your old hometown."
"Yes." Zann slid a hand into his pocket to check on the message moth.
"We moved to First City. But their families are still in Swamp Bottom."
"Yes, yes." The reporter glanced at the note window to make sure it was recording everything Zann said.
"Speaking of family, I heard that your grandfather, Boz, came out of retirement to start working with the Red Council again.
Is he helping to catalog the relics?"
Zann bit his lip. "Um, I don't pay much attention to that kind of thing."
He hoped the reporter would get bored and end the interview.
But the reporter didn't look bored at all.
"What was it like traveling through the vortex?" he asked.
Zann hesitated, thinking back to those travels.
Traveling through the vortex had been scary. It had also been exciting.
But Zann didn't want to tell this stranger about that.
He gulped and tried to think of some way to escape.
"Excuse me!" A girl's voice came from behind Zann.
"Are you a reporter for the First City Flash?"
Turning, Zann saw a girl he recognized from school.
She was a year ahead of him, and he didn't know her name.
"Yes, I am," the reporter told her. "But I'm busy right now."
"Okay," the girl said. "But I just heard that Laddno is here.
He's speaking soon in the palace square."
"Laddno is here?" someone nearby exclaimed. "Is that true?"
The girl shrugged. "I don't know. It's just what I heard."
The reporter looked excited. "I'd better get over there!" he said. "Thanks, young lady!"
He snapped his fingers and zapped out of sight. Other people zapped away too.
"Who's Laddno?" Zann asked the girl.
She laughed. "I thought everybody had heard of him.
He's a super-successful businessman. He's also the new leader of the Void rights movement."
She rubbed her fingers together to conjure a dragon treat, which she tossed to Zing.
The dragon snapped it up eagerly and then whistled happily at the girl.
"Oh, right." Now Zann remembered hearing his parents mention the name. "Is Laddno a Void?"
"No. He's just interested in equal rights for everyone in Magica.
But listen, you should get out of here.
That reporter might come back once he finds out Laddno isn't really speaking to the crowd."
"Huh?" Zann was confused. "But you just said—"
The girl giggled. "I could tell that you wanted the reporter to stop bothering you, so I said the one thing I knew would get him to leave."
Zann smiled at the girl from school.
"Thanks for getting rid of that reporter," he said. "I'm Zann."
"I know." She smiled. "Everyone at the Academy knows who you are. I'm Mari."
"Nice to meet you. Do you live around here?" Zann asked.
Mari shook her head. "I live in Treeview."
Treeview was a wealthy neighborhood on the southern edge of the city.
"Do you live near here?" Mari asked.
"No. But my parents' lab is right there." Zann pointed across the street.
Mari's eyes widened. "I've heard about them!
Are they really working with all the ancient magical relics Morb found in the Cave of the Unknown?"
She sounded impressed. "Like the Dragontamer's Charm, and the Mask of Zanta? That must be fascinating!"
"Yeah." Zann shrugged. "Do you want to come in and meet them?"
"Yes!" Mari exclaimed. "I'm super interested in that kind of work.
I want to be a researcher someday."
Zann felt another pang of homesickness. Perda was interested in research too.
She was always investigating other worlds and new forms of magic.
He led Mari into the lab, with Zing following.
His parents were both bent over their work when Zann entered.
Zann felt happy every time he saw them.
They'd been lost in the vortex for four years, and he still could hardly believe they were really back.
"Zann!" His mother, Asta, spotted him first. "How was school today?"
"Fine." Zann waved toward Mari. "This is Mari. She goes to the Academy too."
"Hello, Mari." Nax, Zann's father, strode over to shake hands.
"Any friend of Zann's is a friend of ours."
"It's an honor to meet you both," Mari said.
"I've heard a lot about your work."
"It keeps us busy." Zann's mother chuckled.
"Would you like a tour of the lab?"
"I'd love it!" Mari eagerly followed Asta into the next room.
Zann stuck his hand in his pocket.
"What do you have there, son?" his father asked.
"A message moth from my friends back home."
Zann shot his father a sheepish look. "I mean, from Swamp Bottom."
His father patted his shoulder. "It's okay, Zann.
You lived there for over four years. I'm sure you miss it."
"Only a little," Zann said quickly. "It's a pretty boring place. But I do miss my friends."
He pulled out the moth and scanned the message on its wing.
"Are they coming to the party?" his father asked.
Zann's birthday was in a couple of weeks.
His parents had suggested a party to celebrate, and Zann had invited the gang from Swamp Bottom.
"They're not sure yet." Zann sighed and released the moth, which flew out the window.
"Gliss' parents don't want her to ride a dragon this far.
And they're not sure if they'll be able to take time off to zap her and the others here."
"Hmm." Nax scratched his chin. "Well, maybe they'll work something out."
Zann hoped so. First City was far from Swamp Bottom—much too far for his friends to zap here on their own.
Before Zann could say anything else, Mari rushed back in.
"I just saw the Mask of Zanta!" she cried, her eyes sparkling.
"This is the most incredible day of my life!"
Asta followed her, smiling. "Mari volunteered to help us catalog the relics," she told her husband.
"I'd love to help!" Mari said. "The teachers at school say I'm very precise.
I promise I won't make any mistakes."
"That's very nice of you," Nax told her.
"We might take you up on that, Mari."
Clunk!
Everyone jumped as a device crashed to the floor.
It had a dial and a small hose.
Zing quickly snatched the device up in his mouth.
"Zing!" Asta grabbed the device from the dragon. "You naughty beast."
"What is that thing?" Zann asked.
"It's called an infusinator." His mother set the device back on the shelf.
"It's a new invention we're working on."
She shook a finger at Zing. "And it's not edible!"
"You have so many interesting things here."
Mari peered at another item. "What's this?"
"The guidelink? Zann's father invented that one," Asta said.
"We think it might allow people to navigate the vortex more easily."
Nax grinned. "Yes, but don't get too excited yet. We're still working out the kinks."
"What does it do?" Zann asked, thinking back to how difficult it had been to travel through the vortex.
"It does several things," Nax said. "So far it seems best at locating and locking onto sources of magic power."
"That way, travelers can recover their magical energy faster," Asta said.
"It also helps them avoid worlds with weak or no magic."
Zann shuddered, remembering the time he and his friends had almost been trapped on a world with no magic.
"That's amazing," Mari said. But this time she sounded a little nervous as well as impressed.
Zann wasn't surprised. Most people had never even seen a wormhole up close, let alone traveled through the vortex.
"The vortex isn't that scary," he told her.
"It's actually pretty cool. We visited this one world where—"
He stopped as another message moth fluttered in and flew over to Mari.
"Oh," she said, scanning the wing. "Sorry, I have to get home to watch my little cousins.
Thank you for showing me the lab."
She smiled at Zann and his parents. "See you at school, Zann."
As soon as she was gone, Nax grinned. "I'm glad you're making friends, Zann.
Especially with such a smart and pretty girl!"
Asta was grinning too.
Zann scowled. "Very funny, Dad," he muttered.
"I'm taking Zing to the park for a while."
He grabbed the dragon and zapped away before his parents could tease him anymore.
The dinner table at Zann's house was crowded that night.
Boz and Teplo were there, along with Teplo's assistant, Fala. Teplo's sniffer goose was there too.
The foul-tempered bird lurked under the table, honking at Zing and biting Zann's feet.
Boz had also invited his friend Saffa and her husband, Staz.
Like Boz and Teplo, Saffa was a very skilled Magic Master.
"I can't remember the last time I was at a table with so many Reds," Staz commented with a chuckle.
"I hope Laddno and his anti-Red followers don't find out."
Teplo looked up from his food. "Is Laddno part of the anti-Red crowd now too?
I thought he was only involved with Void rights."
"Maybe so." Boz stirred his puffnut soup, his long nose quivering.
"But he's getting people awfully riled up.
The mood here in First City feels tense, especially with all those powerful relics at the lab sending out extra magic energy."
"The king and queen are quite concerned about all the unrest," Fala said.
Nax nodded. "Venna keeps muttering about the anger Laddno is churning up between Voids and non-Voids."
He looked around the table. "There's also a certain amount of anger between Reds and non-Reds."
Zann was surprised by the worry in his father's voice.
Sure, he knew there had been some anti-Red sentiment in First City lately. But that was nothing new.
Even back in Swamp Bottom, a few people seemed to resent the fact that Reds had stronger magic than everyone else. He thought about Jev and grimaced.
"Is your soup all right, Zann?" Asta asked.
"Sure." Zann pushed Jev out of his mind. That was one good thing about moving to First City.
He would probably never have to see that jerk again!
His mother returned her attention to the conversation. But Zann stopped listening.
He had more important things on his mind than politics.
He hoped Gliss' parents would change their minds about the dragons.
After all, Zann, Perda, Darb, and Gliss had ridden dragons to First City before.
And Darb was friendly with a local dragon breeder.
Zann was sure the breeder would let the kids borrow a couple of dragons again.
"Oh!" Saffa said suddenly. "There's news." She snapped her fingers, and a large floating image appeared above the table.
It showed a crowd of people shaking their fists and yelling.
Many of them held signs about Void rights.
"Oh dear," Saffa said. "This image is from the future.
It shows a protest that will take place soon."
Boz read the words appeared on the image.
"Laddno says it will be the biggest protest yet."
Zann was reading too. "Ugh! It's going to be on my birthday!
I hope Gliss' parents don't hear about it."
"Who's that, boy?" Teplo peered at him.
"Gliss . . . You mean your Red friend? Isn't she in favor of Void rights?"
"Yes," Zann said. "And her parents are too, I think.
At least they seem to like Darb just fine. But they're kind of overprotective."
"I see," his father chimed in. "You're afraid all the unrest will make them worry about letting Gliss come to the big city."
"Right." Zann yanked his foot away as Teplo's goose bit it again.
"And if they won't let her come, the others might not be allowed to come either."
Fala looked sympathetic. "That's tough, Zann. I know you four are awfully close."
Suddenly Zann had an idea. "Hey, if my friends can't come here for my party, why don't we go to them?"
He quickly grew excited. "We could celebrate my birthday in Swamp Bottom!"
His parents traded a look with Boz and the others.
"I don't think that will work right now, Zann," Asta said. "I'm sorry."
"Why not?" Zann said. "It would be so much easier for us to just zap out there."
"No, your mother is right," Boz said.
"It's not a good time for any of us to leave First City."
"But don't worry," Nax added. "We'll figure out something to get your friends here."
Zann wanted to ask his father how he planned to make that happen.
But Nax was already turning to tell Saffa and Staz about something Venna had said the day before.
Zann clenched his fists under the table, ignoring the goose as it yanked on his pant leg.
It wasn't fair! All his parents thought about was their work.
They were almost as bad as Venna herself, and everyone knew her whole life revolved around her role on the Red Council.
Zann couldn't sit there anymore. He nudged the goose away with his foot and stood up.
"May I be excused?" he said. "I want to take Zing out for a walk before it gets dark."
"Good idea, Zann," his father said, barely looking at him.
Soon Zann was wandering along the quiet street near his house.
Zing had played for a long time at the park earlier, so he wasn't as hyper as usual.
But when a heat hornet buzzed by, Zing shot out a burst of flame and flew after the bug.
"Wait up, Zing," Zann called. "I don't want to—hey, what's that?"
A bright image had appeared in midair when Zing flew past, but now it was gone.
Zann stepped closer, assuming the image would appear again. Nothing happened.
Zann moved around the sidewalk, but still the image wouldn't reappear.
Zann conjured a dragon treat. "Zing, come back here!" he called.
When Zing came near, the image appeared again.
But when Zann stepped closer to it, it disappeared.
"Weird," Zann murmured. "Why does it disappear when I'm nearby?"
"Because you're a Red, that's why," a voice said from behind Zann.
Surprised, Zann spun around. He was even more surprised when he recognized the figure stepping out of the shadows.
"Jev!" Zann blurted out.
"What are you doing in First City?" Zann asked, stunned to see Jev.
Jev ignored the question. "It's a new kind of magic," he said with a smirk.
"Your parents aren't the only ones who can invent stuff, you know."
"Huh?" Zann was still confused by his old enemy's unexpected appearance.
He glanced at Zing, who was flying overhead, whistling suspiciously at Jev.
"What are you talking about? What new magic?"
"The image, dummy." Jev rolled his eyes.
"The new magic makes the image visible to any living thing except Reds.
See?" He stepped forward. The image appeared again.
This time Zann was able to get a better look.
It was an ad for the mass protest on his birthday.
"What's the big deal?" Zann said with a frown.
"Everyone knows about that protest. It's been all over the news."
"Maybe." Jev stepped back, and the ad disappeared again.
"But the image is a good way to make it clear that Reds aren't welcome there."
Zann's head was spinning. He'd been wishing all week for visitors from Swamp Bottom.
However, Jev definitely wasn't one of the people he'd had in mind!
"I thought the protest was to promote Void rights," Zann said.
"Why wouldn't Voids want Reds to support that?"
"You're so naive." Jev was still smirking. "Things are changing in Magica.
And Reds like you probably won't like what's coming.
That's why my parents decided to come to First City.
We want to help Laddno bring about those changes."
"Laddno?" Zann was surprised to hear the man's name again. "You've heard of Laddno?"
"Hasn't everyone?" Jev said. "He's one of the most successful businessmen in Magica.
He knows how to get things done. Including the Void rights stuff and, you know, other things.
Now that he's involved, everything is going to change. Just you wait and see."
Zann wasn't sure what Jev was talking about.
But he didn't want to talk to his old enemy anymore.
"Excuse me," Zann said. "I'm sure you don't want to be seen with a Red like me. So I'm out of here."
He grabbed Zing, snapped his fingers, and zapped away.
Splash!
"Drat," Zann grumbled, realizing he'd barely stopped to think about where he wanted to land.
He glanced around and recognized a small local park. Good.
At least he hadn't accidentally zapped to Wormwood or some other nasty place.
He stepped out of the small pond where he'd landed.
Zing flew off to chase a bird in the treetops.
Zann looked around again. The park was deserted.
Zann rubbed his fingers together, preparing to zap back home.
Then he paused and decided to wait a moment.
Talking to Jev had made Zann curious about Laddno.
Everyone seemed to be talking about this guy lately.
Yet Zann knew almost nothing about the man.
"I'll check the Directory," he thought.
The Directory listed the names of all the people in Magica, along with basic information about each of them.
Zann rubbed his hands together again, creating more magic friction.
A book-like magical image appeared in the air in front of him.
Countless tiny photos floated in the image.
"Laddno!" Zann said.
Instantly, the photos scattered as Laddno's picture expanded to fill the screen.
Zann scrolled quickly past the photo. Thanks to the ads for the protest, he already knew what Laddno looked like. Now he wanted information about him.
Zann scanned the entry. As Jev had mentioned, Laddno was listed as being a businessman.
Some citizens of Magica had no talent or patience for certain types of creative magic.
So they hired people like Laddno to help them conjure a nicer house or more comfortable furniture or clothing that fit them properly.
And of course, Voids couldn't create their own things at all.
They had to rely on family members, friends, or people like Laddno to conjure all their clothes and other necessities.
Zann read that Laddno had been born in First City and was a few years younger than Zann's parents.
He was known to have fairly strong magic for a non-Red, and he currently lived in the wealthy neighborhood of Treeview.
"Treeview," Zann muttered. "That's where Mari lives. Maybe she knows him."
Next he read about Laddno's involvement in the Void rights movement.
The Directory said he'd joined just a few weeks earlier but had quickly become the leader of the movement.
Before closing the Directory, Zann decided to check for Wyssa.
The last time he'd done that, her entry looked the same as it always had.
That was shortly after she'd taken Morb away though.
"Wyssa," Zann said. Laddno's page disappeared, replaced immediately with Wyssa's.
The page had a new note: Presumed to be off-world.
"Wow. She really is gone," Zann thought.
"I wonder what world she's on now."
Zann closed the Directory. "Come on, Zing," he called to the dragon, who was still sniffing around in the treetops.
"Let's go home and—aah!"
Zann's head suddenly throbbed with pain.
He staggered back, grabbing a tree to steady himself.
He squeezed his eyes shut and waited for the pain to pass. It felt like a Red Share.
But this seemed different from previous Red Shares.
For one thing Zann couldn't tell which Red the Share was coming from.
He also wasn't sure which emotion had caused it.
Was it pain? Fear? Anger? Or some combination of all three?
The feeling started to subside. Zann breathed out with relief.
Then he gasped as the feeling washed over him again.
The pain wasn't quite as strong this time, but now a faint voice came with it.
Zann couldn't tell who was speaking, but the person was saying just one word: "Help!"
"Wow," Zann blurted out as the faint voice and the pain finally disappeared.
"That was the weirdest Share I've ever had."
He was worried about Boz and the other Reds back at his house.
What if something had happened after he'd left?
Zann grabbed Zing and zapped back to his family's dining room.
His father smiled brightly at him. "You're back, Zann."
"Yep." Zann glanced around, relieved to see that everyone seemed to be okay. "Is everything all right here?"
"Of course." Teplo reached for the puckerberry pudding.
"Except that we're running out of dessert."
Most of the other adults chuckled. But Boz stared at Zann.
"What's the matter, my boy?" he asked.
"You look as agitated as a panic bug."
"Something strange just happened," Zann said. He told the adults about the Red Share.
"That is odd," Saffa said when Zann finished.
"If the Share didn't come from any of us, it must have come from another Red whom you know."
Boz stood up and rubbed his fingers together.
"We should check around. Just in case."
"Don't worry, though, Zann," Nax said. "The close presence of so many powerful relics could be causing this.
Their energy has been interfering with all magic energy, especially for Reds, who are more sensitive to magic."
Zann nodded slowly. He wanted to believe his father was right.
But he couldn't help remembering how desperate that faint voice had sounded.
That night Zann had trouble falling asleep.
He stared at the ceiling, still thinking about that weird Red Share.
Who was trying to contact him? Boz and the others had checked with most of the Reds they knew, and so far everyone was fine.
Tap! Tap!
Zann sat up when he heard a light rapping on his window.
A spy fly fluttered outside. Zann was confused.
Spy flies usually stayed hidden while spying.
But this one was trying to get his attention.
After hesitating a moment, Zann opened the window.
He gasped as the spy fly dived straight into his ear.
"What's going on?" Zann thought. "I didn't summon a spy fly."
Suddenly an image filled his mind, and in it he saw his three best friends!
"Hi, Zann!" Perda waved, looking pleased with herself.
"If this works, you should be seeing all of us right now."
Gliss grinned. "Yes, Perda is still trying to invent new kinds of magic. Like tinkering with spy flies."
Zann could hardly believe it. Seeing his friends was great!
"Hi, guys," he murmured, even though he knew they couldn't hear him.
Suddenly he felt more homesick than ever.
His friends chatted for a while, filling him in on all the news around Swamp Bottom.
They even mentioned that Jev had moved away, though none of them knew where he'd gone.
"I know where he is," Zann thought with a sick feeling.
But he didn't think about Jev for long.
He was more interested in listening to his friends.
"Okay, we should send the fly off now," Darb said at last.
Gliss nodded. "We haven't figured out how to get there for your birthday yet."
"But we'll definitely be there," Perda added.
"Even if we have to take a wormhole to First City!"
"I'm sure that won't be necessary," Gliss said with a shudder.
"Although Perda has been studying up on the vortex lately!"
Zann felt alarmed. Perda was bold enough to do something crazy like jump into a wormhole.
He'd been the same way once. But he had a healthy respect for the vortex these days.
The spy fly wiggled out of Zann's ear.
Zann didn't know how to get it to spy on him and return to the three kids, though he planned to ask Perda.
So he summoned a message moth and inscribed a quick note to his friends.
Then he fell asleep, thinking about good old Swamp Bottom.
Zap.
Zann landed across the street from the Academy the next morning. Several people raced toward him.
"Red!" one shouted, sounding angry. "We don't want your kind here."
Zann realized he'd landed in the middle of yet another protest.
"Leave me alone!" Zann exclaimed. "I'm leaving."
He snapped his fingers to zap across the street and into the school.
But instead he landed on his rear end right in front of the door.
"Drat," he muttered, remembering that the Academy had a special kind of Shield spell over it.
The Shield was there to prevent kids from zapping in or out during the day.
Zann's old school in Swamp Bottom was a lot smaller, so it didn't need that kind of spell.
Grumbling, he opened the door and hurried inside. He almost crashed into Mari.
"Hi, Zann!" She greeted him with a smile. "Did you just get here?"
"Yes," Zann said. "I ran into another protest outside."
"I saw that too." Mari didn't sound very interested.
"Hey, did your parents say anything about my offer to volunteer at their lab? I really want to do it."
"They didn't say anything to me," Zann said. "I can remind them if you want.
They're so busy these days that they might have forgotten."
"Could you? That would be great!" Mari said. "Thanks, Zann."
Zann didn't answer. He'd just spotted another familiar face.
"What's he doing here?" he said, annoyed.
Mari followed his gaze. "You mean Jev? He just enrolled here."
"Great," Zann said with a sigh. "That's just great."
That afternoon Zann couldn't wait to escape from school.
Jev had been in all of Zann's classes.
Zann was already tired of his old enemy's sneers and dirty looks.
He hurried outside and took a deep breath.
He rubbed his fingers together to create magic friction.
But before he could zap away, he noticed a message moth flapping toward him.
The message was from his friends.
Zann smiled. "My friends are coming!"
Several days later Zann rushed for the door as soon as school ended.
He heard Mari laugh and call his name.
"Why are you in such a rush?" she exclaimed, catching up with him.
"I thought I was the only one so eager to escape today!"
"I think everyone is ready to leave." Zann looked around.
The next week was a school holiday, and all the students looked excited.
"But why are you so eager? I thought you liked school."
"I do." Mari smiled. "But I like working at your parents' lab even more.
Want to walk over there with me?"
"I can't today," Zann said. "My best friends are arriving later for a visit."
Zann had been happy ever since receiving the message moth.
Gliss' Uncle Gar was coming to First City for a meeting.
He'd offered to zap Zann's friends there for the party.
That reminded Zann—he'd meant to invite Mari to his party the next day.
He opened his mouth to tell her about it. But just then Jev walked over.
"Watch out, Mari," Jev said with a smirk.
"If you keep hanging out with Reds, people might start to talk."
Zann frowned at him. "Mind your own business, Jev."
Then he hurried away, figuring he could send Mari a message moth later.
He didn't want Jev to hear about the party, especially since Gliss would be there.
Even though Gliss was a Red, Jev had always liked her.
When Zann got home, Zing was the only one there. The dragon looked at him expectantly.
Zann shook his head. "No park today, little buddy. We have guests coming."
Zann ducked as Zing shot an angry flame at him.
He felt sorry for the dragon being cooped up in the house all day.
But he knew Zing would be happy when Darb arrived later.
Darb had a special bond with animals, including dragons.
He conjured up some snacks and puckerberry juice.
Then, feeling restless, he wandered around the house.
He was still waiting when his parents came in.
"Are your friends here yet?" Asta asked.
"Not yet," Zann said. "You left the lab early?"
Nax nodded. "We wanted to be here when your friends arrive."
"Besides, we're not needed at the lab." Asta chuckled.
"Your friend Mari is so enthusiastic, she's doing the work of three people.
I'm glad you reminded us to contact her."
Zann noticed that his father was holding something.
"Isn't that one of your inventions, Dad?"
"Yes, it's the infusinator." Nax held it up.
"I thought Darb might want to use it while he's here."
"It will provide him with magic energy," Asta added.
"It uses a magical technique we discovered in a world called Atmo.
Atmo's magic source is the energy in its air.
Some plants and animals can ingest large quantities of that energy and store it for future use.
"We heard Morb used leeches from Atmo to power one of his contraptions," Asta added grimly.
Zann shuddered. Those blue leeches were horrible!
"Does the infusinator use leeches too?" he asked.
"No, it's made out of wood from lung trees," Asta said.
"Lung trees have an amazing ability to store magic."
"Darb just needs to breathe in stored energy from this hose," Nax said.
"Then he can use that energy, just like any Magician."
"But we brought back only one piece of wood from the lung tree," Asta said.
"And we've already used a lot of its energy while experimenting.
So Darb will have to use the infusinator carefully."
"I thought it could suck magic out of the air," Zann said.
His mother shook her head. "Only in Atmo. Magica's energy works differently.
We're still trying to figure out how to refill it."
"We've been experimenting with different techniques," Nax added.
"For now, Darb won't be able to zap long distances or do anything else that requires lots of energy.
But at least he can create food and do other simple tasks."
"Yes, and we hope he'll let us know what he thinks of it," Asta added.
"This infusinator is only a prototype, but if it works well, we—"
"Surprise!" Perda cried, appearing in front of them. "We're here!"
Gliss appeared next, holding onto Darb's arm.
Zann grinned, so happy to see the three of them that he hardly knew how to respond.
Zing let out a burst of flame and raced toward Darb.
"Hi, Zing." Darb smiled and scratched the dragon's scaly head. "I've missed you."
"I've missed you guys too," Zann blurted out. "I'm so glad you're here!"
For the next few minutes, the four of them couldn't stop talking.
There was so much to catch up on!
A few times, though, Zann couldn't help feeling a little awkward.
His friends mentioned people and events he didn't know anything about.
But mostly it was great to be with them again.
After a while his parents showed Darb the infusinator.
"We'd love for you to try it out and let us know how it works for you," said Nax.
"Oh, sure." Darb seemed a little uncomfortable. "Thanks."
Zann had conjured a bed for Darb.
But since Zann's house was fairly small, Saffa and Staz had offered to let the girls stay with them.
Teplo had offered too, but Zann knew Perda and Gliss wouldn't want to deal with Teplo's cranky goose.
"Let's go to Saffa's so you can settle in," Zann said.
"I'll show you my neighborhood on the way."
The kids headed out, with Zing scurrying along at Darb's heels.
"That's the park Zing and I go to," Zann said, pointing. "And over there is—"
Suddenly that weird feeling struck Zann again.
This time the pain was so strong, it knocked him to the ground!
Zann writhed on the ground, his head exploding with sounds, feelings, and images.
Once again fear, pain, and anger surged through him.
A faint voice called for help as waves splashed and rain pounded down.
Feeling seasick, Zann pressed both hands to his forehead.
"Zann!" Perda cried. "What's wrong?"
Zann squeezed his eyes shut, trying to block out her voice.
The cry in his head was a little louder now, and it sounded vaguely familiar.
Who could it be? Zann tried to focus as the cry came again.
"Help me!" the person cried. "Please, someone help me before it's too late!"
Then the feelings disappeared as abruptly as they had come.
Zann sat up, sweating and breathing hard.
"Zann!" Darb was squeezing his shoulder. "Are you all right?"
"I—I think so." Zann gulped in a breath and slowly climbed to his feet.
His whole body felt shaky. "I mean, yes, I'm okay. This has happened before."
He described the mysterious Shares he'd been receiving. His friends looked confused.
"Are they Red Shares or not?" Gliss asked.
Zann shrugged. "I don't know. I can't tell who they're coming from."
"Are you sure it's not Boz, or some other Red that you know?" Darb asked.
Zann shook his head. "I checked last time.
Boz and the others contacted every Red they could think of, and nobody knew anything about the Shares."
"That's weird." Perda chewed her lower lip, looking thoughtful.
"I've never read anything about this kind of magic."
"My mom and dad think it could be a result of having all those relics close by," Zann said.
"They said the relics possess such strong and ancient magic that they might be affecting our regular magic."
"Speaking of the relics, I hope it's not Morb contacting you," Perda said half-jokingly.
"Maybe he's up to more magical tricks."
Gliss frowned at her. "It couldn't be Morb.
Wyssa made sure that he will never do magic again."
"Or anything else," Zann put in with a shudder.
"I was only joking," Perda told them. "Do you think it's—"
A shout interrupted her. Two women were hurrying toward them. They both looked excited.
"It's you, isn't it?" one woman exclaimed. "The hero kids?"
The second woman pointed at Zing. "I even recognize the dragon!" she cried. "But I forgot his name!"
For the next few minutes, Zann and his friends had to answer the women's questions.
Finally Zann made an excuse to hurry away.
"Maybe we should take a shortcut to Saffa's house," Zann said. "Let's go through the park."
He led the way. Halfway across the park, he heard voices ahead.
"Uh-oh," Gliss said with a smile. "Do you think more of our fans are looking for us?"
Just then a group of people marched into view, waving signs.
Perda's eyes widened. "Is it one of those Void rights protests we keep hearing about?" she whispered to Zann.
Zann nodded. "There are even more protests now," he said.
"A guy named Laddno took over the movement."
"Oh, I've heard about him," Gliss said.
"My parents were talking about how hard he's working to bring attention to the Void rights cause."
Zann glanced at Darb, who was staring at the ground.
Before Zann could say anything, Perda nudged him.
"Look!" she exclaimed. "Is that Jev? What's he doing in First City?"
Zann sighed. "He's here for the protests."
Jev was marching with the others, waving a colorful sign.
He spotted Zann and his friends and came over.
Zann expected him to say hi to Gliss, but Jev ignored her.
He ignored Zann too and only gave Perda a halfhearted smile.
Instead Jev's eyes were focused on Darb.
"Hey, Darb," he said in a friendly voice.
"I didn't expect to see you in First City."
Darb looked surprised. Zann knew how he felt.
Jev had always been mean to Darb and the other Voids in Swamp Bottom.
In fact, that was how Zann and Darb had become friends.
Soon after moving to Swamp Bottom, Zann had stood up to Jev when Jev was bullying Darb.
Jev shot the others a dirty look.
"You shouldn't be hanging around with Reds," he told Darb.
"Why don't you come with me? I can introduce you to some people who are working to get equal magic for all—even Voids like you."
"No thanks," Darb said. "I'd rather stay with my friends."
Jev frowned. "Suit yourself," he said. "But Laddno wants everyone to join in the struggle for equality."
Suddenly cheers came from the group. Most of the protestors were yelling Laddno's name.
Jev brightened. "He's here!" he cried. "I heard he might come today."
He smirked at Zann and Gliss. "You might want to hide your hair, you two."
Jev dashed away before anyone could respond.
Gliss looked uneasy. "Let's get out of here," she said.
"Hold on for a second." Perda stepped forward and peered over the heads of the crowd.
"I want to get a look at Laddno."
"Me too," Zann said. He and his friends stood on their tiptoes as a man strode onto a dais that someone had just conjured.
Zann recognized Laddno right away from the ads.
He had a large, square head and broad shoulders.
His deep-set eyes swept over the crowd.
"Greetings, citizens of First City!" Laddno shouted, raising both hands. "Thank you for coming today."
"Void rights!" someone in the crowd shouted.
"Banish the greedy Reds!" someone else shrieked.
The rest of the onlookers cheered loudly.
Gliss shivered. "Come on, you guys," she said. "We shouldn't be here."
This time Zann agreed. "Let's go." He grabbed Darb and Perda, and Perda grabbed Gliss.
"Zap!" Zann whispered, aiming for Saffa's house.
The next morning Zann took his friends to his parents' lab for a tour.
Perda wanted to see where they worked and check out their latest inventions.
Saffa decided to go too. When they arrived, they found Boz there with Zann's parents.
"Would you like to see the relics?" Asta asked Zann's friends.
"Sure," Perda said. "Is the Mask of Zanta here?"
"You already saw that," Gliss reminded her.
"That was when it was lying around in the Cave of the Unknown," Perda said. "Seeing it here is different."
Zann followed his mother and his friends into the next room.
"Wow," Gliss said when Asta showed them the Mask of Zanta.
It was locked in a glass case. "That's amazing. And kind of scary."
"We keep this relic separate from the others, since it's probably the strongest one we found," Zann's mother said.
"Other than the Horn of the Otherworld, maybe. But that was destroyed."
Zann shuddered, remembering how Morb had tried to take over Magica with the Horn.
They moved on to the other relics waiting to be cataloged.
Zann's mother even took out a few for the kids to touch.
None of the other relics were as powerful as the Mask of Zanta, but still, Zann felt ancient magic crackling around them.
"What are you going to do with them?" Perda asked, examining an old, cracked cup.
"Are you still planning to destroy them all?"
"We're not sure yet." Asta sighed.
"Most members of the Red Council would prefer that the relics weren't around, in case someone like Morb ever tries to use them for evil purposes.
But a few members think we should keep some relics."
"Like Venna?" Zann guessed. The head of the Red Council had been opposed to destroying the relics all along.
She wanted to store them away in case the items' strong magic was ever needed.
"I see why she thinks that." Perda carefully set down the relic she was holding.
"If someone as strong as Morb does come along, the relics could help us fight him."
Zann's mother nodded. "Yes, that's Venna's argument," she said.
"But my father and a few others believe it's not worth the risk. They think—oh, hello, Mari."
Mari had just entered the room. She was holding another relic.
"Hi," she said, looking surprised to see so many people in the lab.
"Excuse me. I didn't mean to interrupt."
"No, it's okay." Zann stepped forward. "This is Mari, a friend from my new school," he told the others.
"Mari, these are my friends from home—Perda, Darb, and Gliss."
Mari smiled. "Nice to meet you."
"Same here," Gliss said. "Are you coming to the party?"
"Oops!" Zann said. "I've been meaning to invite you.
It's this afternoon, but I'd love for you to come."
He smiled sheepishly. "Sorry for the late notice."
"That's okay," Mari said. "I think I can come. Thanks for the invitation."
She set down the relic she was holding and followed them back into the main room.
Boz and Saffa were leaning over one of Nax's inventions while he explained how it worked.
"What is that?" Perda hurried over. "It looks interesting!"
Nax smiled at her. "I call it the guidelink.
It will help people travel through the vortex more easily."
Just then the door flew open. Zann was shocked to see the king and queen of Magica rush in.
Right behind them was Venna, followed by a Red, a man whom Zann had never seen before.
Zann's friends also looked shocked by the sight of the king and queen.
"Who's that guy?" Darb whispered. "He looks familiar."
"I don't know," Zann whispered back.
"Good! You're all here," the queen said, staring at Boz, Saffa, and Zann's parents.
Then she spotted Zann and the other kids. "Oh! Hello, youngsters."
"We need to talk," Venna told the other adults, ignoring the kids. "It's important."
The king rubbed his fingers together. "I'll zap us all to the palace. It will be private there."
"All right." Zann's mother rubbed her hands together and stepped toward the king.
Then she widened her eyes. "Oh! Some of the relics are still out."
"I'll take care of them," Mari said.
"Thanks, Mari," Asta said. "I'm sure we'll be back soon."
The adults zapped away.
"I wonder what's going on," Gliss said.
Perda rubbed her chin. "I'm wondering the same thing," she said.
"Do you think they're talking about what to do with the relics?"
"I doubt it," Zann said. "They've been talking about that for months. This seemed urgent."
"Maybe it's about the Void rights protests," Gliss suggested.
"Why would that be urgent?" Perda asked.
"Boz says Laddno is stirring up too much unrest," Zann said.
"He thinks the protests are turning people against the Red Council, and Reds in general."
"Wow, really?" Perda looked surprised.
Mari cleared her throat. "Excuse me," she said.
"I'd better go take care of those relics." She hurried into the other room.
"She seems nice," Gliss said.
Perda wandered over to pick up the guidelink.
"Do you think this really works?" she said. "Maybe we should test it out."
"What do you mean?" Gliss' eyes widened nervously.
Perda laughed. "I'm just kidding. But Zann's dad wants Darb to try out his other invention, right?
It would be fun to try this one too. I'd love to see more worlds!"
"Not me," Gliss declared. "I never want to see the inside of the vortex again!"
Zann took the guidelink from Perda and put it on a shelf.
"Let's go home and get ready for my party."
He glanced at the spot where the adults had zapped away.
"I just hope my parents and Boz get back from the palace in time."
Everyone was having fun at Zann's party.
His parents had returned from the palace just in time to greet the first guests.
Boz, Teplo, and Saffa had arrived a little late, but they all seemed to be enjoying themselves now.
The delicious food and fancy decorations that Zann and his parents had conjured made the house look festive.
"This is great, Zann!" Perda said. "Your First City friends are really nice."
"Thanks." Zann had invited several kids from his new school, and most of them had come.
Mari hadn't shown up yet though. He hoped she wasn't insulted because he'd invited her at the last minute.
"Over here, Zann!" Gliss called from nearby.
"We're going to play Conjure and Vanish."
Zann smiled, forgetting about Mari. Conjure and Vanish was one of his favorite party games. He and Perda hurried over.
"It's your party, so you go first," Gliss told him.
"Okay." Zann rubbed his hands together to create magic friction.
He closed his eyes and focused on the object he wanted to conjure—a swamp shiner.
That was a type of lamp he'd used when exploring the swamp back home.
He then used a Vanishing spell to make the lamp invisible before anyone could see it.
"Are you ready?" a kid asked eagerly.
Zann opened his eyes and nodded. "Gliss, you can go first," he said.
She reached for the invisible item, feeling all around it. "Is it a drinking glass?"
"Nope." Zann grinned and pointed to Perda. "Next?"
Perda smiled as soon as she felt the object. "That's easy! It's a swamp shiner.
You made them all the time when we used to sneak out at night to look for flash fish."
"Right!" Zann grinned at her. "Now it's your turn to conjure something."
The sun went down, and everyone was still having fun.
Some kids danced while others talked and ate snacks.
One group of kids played a game of exploding dominoes.
Zann was drinking some airberry punch when his father hurried over.
"Your mother and I just got called back to the palace for an emergency meeting," Nax said.
"Another one?" Zann said. "What's going on?"
His father looked distracted. "We'll tell you later.
Right now, just keep having fun with your friends."
He zapped away with Zann's mother. Zann suddenly noticed that Boz was nowhere in sight. Neither were Teplo or Saffa.
Then he spotted Perda standing by the door to the backyard.
Seeing her made him feel happy and sad at the same time.
He was glad that Perda and his other friends were there.
But they would have to go home in a couple of days.
How long would it be before they were all together again?
He hurried over to Perda. "Want to get some fresh air?" he asked.
"Sure." She smiled.
They went out onto the patio. The air was cool, with a slight breeze that ruffled Perda's hair.
"Wow, you look—," Zann blurted out, and then stopped himself.
"What?" Perda asked.
Zann gulped. He'd been about to say that she looked pretty.
But suddenly he felt awkward about saying that.
"Uh, you look older," he said instead. Then he laughed. "Two months older, I guess."
Perda blinked, seeming confused. Before she could respond, the door burst open.
"There you are, Zann!" a kid from school exclaimed.
"There's a huge protest starting outside right now."
"Yeah!" Another schoolmate came up behind him.
"Laddno said it's going to be the biggest one yet! Let's go check it out!"
The pair rushed for the front door. Perda started to follow.
"Wait, where are you going?" Zann asked.
"We should see what's going on," she said.
Everyone headed out the front door. Zann sighed, not very interested in another protest.
But his best friends were following the crowd, so Zann followed too.
"It's at the palace square," one of the kids called.
"Let's zap there so we don't miss anything."
The kids from First City started disappearing. Perda grabbed Zann's hand.
"You'll have to zap us there," she said.
"I don't remember how to get to the palace."
Zann nodded, grabbing Gliss with his free hand.
She was already holding onto Darb's arm.
"Zap!" Zann cried.
When they landed, Zann saw a massive crowd in the square outside the palace. People waved signs and shouted.
"Wow," Perda said. "This is crazy!"
Zann nodded. "I can't believe the king and queen are allowing a protest like this so close to the palace."
Just then Laddno stepped into view near the palace doors.
"This is an important day!" he shouted. "Please welcome my esteemed guests."
The palace doors opened, and the king and queen walked out.
"What's going on?" Gliss said. "They're not joining his movement, are they?"
"We have an important announcement," the king said. His voice sounded shaky.
The queen took her husband's hand. "The king and I are stepping down as your leaders—immediately."
Zann felt stunned. Some people shouted out in dismay, while others cheered.
"Wow," Perda exclaimed. "This is really—"
"Aah!" Another mysterious Share suddenly seized Zann.
Images of rolling waves filled his mind.
He heard the voice again. Who was it?
Zann squeezed his eyes shut and tried to focus on the voice. A terrified-looking face flashed into view.
Zann gasped, and his eyes popped open. His friends were staring at him.
"Did it happen again?" Perda asked.
"Yes," Zann said. "I know who's trying to contact me."
"Who?" Gliss asked.
Zann gulped. "It's Ello!"
"From Skellia?" Darb exclaimed.
Zann nodded, thinking back to the drowning world they'd visited and the boy who'd helped them escape from it.
"Ello is still stuck in Skellia," he said grimly. "And he needs our help!"
"What are you talking about, Zann?" Perda demanded.
"How could Ello send you a Red Share?
He's not a Red—he's not even from Magica!"
Zann could hardly hear her over the noise of the rally.
"Let's go back to my house!" he shouted. He grabbed his friends. "Zap!"
Zann's house was a mess from the party.
When the kids arrived, Zing was standing on a table eating some leftover snacks.
He zipped over to Zann, chattering angrily and shooting flames.
"Sorry, boy." Darb patted the dragon. "We didn't mean to leave you behind."
Zann rubbed his fingers together and then pointed at some cups on the table. Poof! They disappeared.
Perda and Gliss magically cleaned crumbs off the floor as Zann removed the decorations from the walls. Soon the house was clean.
Remembering Ello's terrified face, Zann looked at his friends. "We have to help Ello."
Gliss sat down. "Tell us what you saw, Zann."
Zann described the mysterious Share as carefully as he could.
By the time he was finished, his friends looked worried and confused.
"Why would Ello still be trapped on Skellia?" Gliss said.
"Wyssa promised to get the Skellian people to safety on another world."
"But she was going to get rid of Morb first," Perda said.
"Maybe he did something to her before she could save the Skellian people."
Zann shook his head. "I doubt it. Wyssa is pretty strong, and Morb had no magic at all when they left."
"Yeah," Gliss said. "But Wyssa was really angry and focused on Morb.
Do you think she forgot about Skellia?"
"Maybe we can contact her and ask," Darb suggested.
He was sitting with Zing curled on his lap.
Perda wrinkled her nose. "Contact her? How? She could be anywhere in the known worlds."
"Or the unknown ones," Gliss said. "She seemed to know about worlds nobody else knew about."
Zann felt impatient. "I think Ello's in trouble.
We don't have time to try to track down Wyssa," he said.
"That will take too long—especially if she doesn't want to be found."
"Good point." Perda nodded. "So what should we do?"
Zann paced back and forth across the room. "I'm not sure."
Darb looked thoughtful. "I wonder how Ello got a mental message through to Zann.
I thought the Skellians had weak magic.
That's why they couldn't escape when the waters started rising, remember?"
"It was because of the gulpers too," Perda said.
"But never mind how Ello sent the message.
The important thing is that he needs our help."
Zann stopped pacing. "Maybe we can ask my parents to—"
A crackle of magic interrupted him. Boz, Saffa, Teplo, and Zann's parents appeared in the room.
They paid no attention to the kids.
"What are we going to do?" Asta rubbed her head.
"This is a disaster!" Teplo exclaimed.
The other adults started talking too. Zann hurried over and tapped his dad's arm.
"We have to tell you about something," Zann said.
"Remember that weird Red Share I had?"
"Not now, son," Nax said before Zann could continue.
"We need to figure out how to deal with what the king and queen just did."
Zann had almost forgotten about the king and queen's announcement.
"Their resignation is effective immediately," Boz told the kids, shaking his head so hard that his long nose swayed back and forth.
"And they've already gone into hiding."
Saffa nodded. "They refuse to communicate with anyone."
"That's weird," Perda said.
"Yes." Teplo rubbed his chin. "Worse yet, there's been no final decision on how to handle the relics."
"That's what the meeting was about earlier today," Asta told the kids.
"The king and queen wanted us to stop cataloging the relics until a new vote takes place."
"They didn't explain why," Saffa said. "Do you think they already knew then that they were going to resign tonight?"
"Listen," Zann said. "You have to hear what I—"
"Laddno isn't giving us much time to figure things out," Nax said to the other adults.
"Laddno?" Perda chimed in. "How is he involved?"
"He's already calling for an election to replace the king and queen," Teplo explained.
"Lots of people seem to agree that it should happen as soon as possible," Asta added.
"Many believe that the Red Council shouldn't be in charge of the election this time."
"What?" Gliss blurted out. "But the Red Council always runs elections!"
Zann was surprised. "Venna isn't going to like this," he said.
"Venna has already announced her candidacy," Saffa told him.
"She'll win easily, especially if nobody runs against her."
"That's fine," Boz said. "We should start preparing to help her."
Zann traded a look with his friends. This was all big news.
But they could worry about it later. Right now they needed to help Ello.
"Okay," he said to the adults. "But I was about to tell you—"
Once again the room crackled with magic.
This time Venna appeared, her face nearly as red as her hair.
"You'll never believe who just announced he's running against me," she said. "Laddno!"
All the adults gasped.
"What?" Asta cried. "He's not the least bit qualified to lead Magica.
He's never been involved in the government before.
The only thing he's done is run a business."
"I know," Venna said grimly. "I've already called an emergency meeting of the Council."
"What are we waiting for?" Boz rubbed his fingers together. "Let's go!"
Zap!
"Now what are we going to do?" Zann said after the adults had all zapped away. "Ello needs our help!"
Perda shrugged. "It's simple. If the adults can't help us rescue him, we'll just have to do it ourselves."
"We're going to help Ello ourselves?" Gliss cried.
"But how? He's trapped on Skellia, remember?"
"We went to Skellia before," Perda said. "We can go there again."
"You mean through the vortex?" Zann felt a shiver of fear, but he shook it off.
"You're right. It's the only way to help him."
"We've traveled through the vortex before," Perda said.
"In fact, we've spent more time in the vortex than anyone we know—except for Wyssa and your parents."
She looked at Darb and Gliss. "We can do this."
Zann smiled, impressed by Perda's courage.
"Okay," Zann said. "Should we try to use the wormhole in Wormwood, or—"
"Stop!" Gliss exclaimed. "We can't just rush off through the closest wormhole."
"Again," Darb added, tickling Zing under his chin.
Perda frowned. "Are you two saying you don't want to help Ello?"
"He saved us when we got stuck on Skellia," Zann said.
Gliss shook her head. "That's not what I'm saying at all."
Her voice was shaky, but she sounded certain.
"I'm saying that if we're going into the vortex, we need to be sensible about how we do it."
"Okay then," Zann said. "So what should we do?"
Darb spoke up. "I have an idea. What about that guidelink Zann's parents invented?"
Perda gasped. "What a great idea! They said it might help people navigate the vortex."
"It should be able to help us find sources of magic too," Zann said.
"On Skellia the gulpers usually eat wormholes as soon as the wormholes appear.
But the guidelink might help us find more wormholes. Then we can all get away."
Darb nodded. "That's exactly what I was thinking."
Zann smiled at him, impressed again. Darb didn't have any magic, but he was one of the smartest people Zann knew.
"Do you think your parents would let us use the guidelink?" Gliss asked Zann.
"No way," Zann replied. "Not if they knew we were planning to travel in the vortex.
We'll have to take it from the lab without telling them."
Zann felt bad saying that. He didn't want to deceive his parents.
But they were so worried about other things.
He didn't want to add to their worries now by telling them about Ello.
"It's a good thing the adults are distracted by politics," Perda said.
"We can probably rescue Ello and get back before they notice we're gone."
Zann hoped she was right. Navigating the vortex was tricky, and they wouldn't have Wyssa to help them find their way home this time.
Gliss looked out the window. "It's getting pretty late.
Let's get a good night's sleep and then find an excuse to visit the lab in the morning."
"Are you going to the lab today?" Zann asked his parents and Boz at breakfast.
He was nervous about how he and his friends would sneak the guidelink out of the lab.
"Yes." Nax helped himself to a goofruit muffin.
"We need to store the relics safely until after the election."
"I still can't believe Laddno wants to be king," Boz said.
Once again the adults started talking about politics.
A few minutes later, Perda and Gliss arrived with Saffa.
"Ready to get to work?" Saffa asked the other adults.
"Can we tag along?" Perda asked. "I'd love to see more of the lab."
"Of course," Asta agreed. "You'll have to stay out of the way though. We have a lot to do."
When everyone arrived at the lab, Perda and Gliss distracted the adults with questions.
Meanwhile Zann and Darb slipped off to the room where the guidelink sat.
Zann grabbed the device from the shelf.
"Uh-oh. Someone's coming!" Darb whispered.
Mari had just walked in. Zann tucked the guidelink into his pocket.
"Sorry I missed your party, Zann," Mari said.
"I had to do something with my family instead."
"Oh, that's too bad," Zann said. "It was fun."
Just then Zann's mother hurried over. She looked serious.
Zann felt the guidelink in his pocket. Had she seen him take it?
But Asta was looking at Mari. "I'm glad you're here, Mari. We need your help."
Zann cleared his throat. "I guess we'll get out of your way then," he said.
He shot his friends a meaningful look.
His parents and Saffa barely seemed to notice his comment.
But Boz looked up as Zann and his friends headed toward the door.
"Hold on," Boz said. "I'll zap home with you.
I have some work to take care of at the house."
Zann gulped. "Um, you're coming home now? But you just got here."
Nax heard him and looked over. "It's better if your grandfather is with you.
These are unsettled times in First City, and there's safety in numbers."
Zann sighed. This wasn't part of their plan!
How were they supposed to sneak away from Boz long enough to get to a wormhole?
Boz was already rubbing his hands together, preparing to zap away. Just then Mari approached Darb.
"I almost forgot," she said, smiling at him.
"I heard about a Void Rights meeting that's happening today.
People will be talking about some new breakthroughs in magic sharing."
"Magic sharing?" Perda echoed.
Mari nodded. "It's the future of equality for Voids," she explained.
"You should go to the meeting, Darb!"
"Um, I probably won't have time," Darb mumbled.
"Here's the information, in case you change your mind."
Mari told him when and where the meeting would be taking place.
Then Saffa called her, and she went over to get instructions from her.
"Ready, kids?" Magic was sparking from Boz's fingertips. "Let's zap!"
Zann rubbed his own fingers together, trying to hide his dismay.
How were they supposed to save Ello now?
Zann peeked into Boz's room. He was hunched over his notebook, writing furiously.
"I wish he would go back to the lab," Zann told his friends.
Perda sighed. "We'll never save Ello if we're stuck here."
The kids listened to some music until Boz poked his head into the room.
"Keep it down in here. I'm trying to concentrate!"
"Sorry," Zann said. "Um, can we go for a walk?"
"All right," Boz said. "But don't be long.
I'll conjure us some lunch in an hour."
The four friends hurried outside.
Perda groaned. "We only have an hour," she said.
"That's not nearly enough time to save Ello."
Zann nodded. "So let's do something else for an hour," he said.
"Maybe Boz will decide we're safe on our own and then go to the lab after lunch."
Gliss looked at Darb. "That Void Rights meeting should be starting around now," she said.
"What if Mari was right, and there really are new ways for Voids to get magic?"
Darb stared at the ground. "That might be interesting," he mumbled.
Perda shrugged. "Let's check it out."
"Do you really think Gliss and I will be welcome there?" Zann pointed to his hair.
"I wish I knew how to do a Masking spell," Perda said.
"What's a Masking spell?" Zann asked.
"I read about it in an old book in the Swamp Bottom library," Perda said.
"The spell was discovered in another world.
It can make a person look exactly how he or she wants to look.
You two could get rid of your red hair."
"I'll just conjure a wig for myself," Gliss said.
Zann conjured a large hat.
The meeting had already started when Zann and his friends arrived. A large crowd filled the room.
Several people stood on the stage, including a young man with wild black hair.
Perda had noticed someone else. She elbowed Zann. "Look, there's Jev," she whispered.
Zann looked. Jev was standing near the stage with his parents.
"Now we'll demonstrate some of the Void magic we just told you about!" the young man with the black hair announced.
"Void magic," Gliss repeated softly. "I guess Mari knew what she was talking about."
Zann nodded and watched as the young man held up a wooden cane.
"This came from a world called Atmo," the man said.
"It allows someone to leap long distances."
"Atmo is the world my parents were talking about," Zann whispered to his friends.
"I wonder how these people got their hands on stuff from other worlds."
He watched as the young man used the cane to leap from one end of the room to the other.
The crowd gasped. After that the young man and his friends showed off some other items.
They had a canteen that stayed full no matter how much someone drank from it.
They displayed a shirt that could expand or contract to fit anyone of any size.
Two of the presenters held up a pile of rubbery fabric.
"This is a boat that comes to life without magic," one announced.
"I'm a Void, and even I can make it work. Watch!"
The Void pulled a little tab. The audience gasped again as the fabric expanded.
A minute later it had taken the form of a small boat.
"Wow!" someone cried. "How did you do that?"
The young man smiled. "Once Laddno is king, he'll explain everything.
He already vowed to share all this magic and more with everyone—including Voids."
Cheers rang out around the room. "Laddno will have control of all those relics from the Cave of the Unknown," the man continued.
"And he will share that immense power with everyone in Magica.
The Red Council will no longer be allowed to hoard the relics for its own purposes."
"That's not what the Red Council is doing," Zann muttered.
"Soon we'll have magic of our own!" an excited Void shouted. "Hooray for Laddno!"
"Hooray for Laddno!" several others cried.
Then a man raised his hand. "But I heard the Red Council is trying to destroy all the relics.
What if the members succeed before Laddno takes power?"
"No!" several people shouted.
"Maybe we should storm that lab right now!" someone yelled.
A few people cheered, though others looked troubled. Zann gulped.
Should he zap to the lab to warn his parents?
He started rubbing his fingers together just in case.
But the young man onstage raised both hands for attention.
"That might not be necessary," he said.
"Laddno is working on something big—something that could render the relics unnecessary."
Murmurs arose from all around the room.
Zann couldn't help feeling curious about Laddno's work himself.
The young man smiled at the crowd.
"Surely everyone here has heard the tales from the Old Times," he said. "Including stories about the Source?"
Zann blinked. The Source? That sounded familiar, but he couldn't quite remember what it was.
"The Source is where all of Magica gets its magic," the man said.
"It's where our world's native magical power comes from.
It's where that power is stored until you snap your fingers or rub your hands together to summon it."
"But I thought the Source was a myth," a woman called out.
The young man smiled. "I did too. But Laddno knew better.
He's sure he can find the Source and figure out how to control it.
That way he can share its power fairly." He clasped his hands together.
"Just think! Soon every Void in Magica will have as much access to magical energy as the most powerful Magic Masters!"
"Hooray for Laddno!" someone shouted again.
The room erupted with cheers and excitement.
Darb leaned closer to Zann. "Can we get out of here?" he whispered.
Zann nodded, already backing toward the door. "Exactly what I was thinking."
Zann and Darb headed out of the meeting. Perda and Gliss followed them.
"What's wrong?" Gliss asked. "Darb, I figured you'd want to stay and find out more.
Just think—soon you might have magic of your own!"
"I'm not sure I want that," Darb said softly.
"I mean, sometimes I think it might be nice to conjure my own food instead of asking someone else to do it. But . . ."
"But what?" Gliss sounded perplexed.
"All I want to do when I grow up is become an animal caretaker," Darb blurted out.
"What if having magic gets in the way of that?"
Now Zann understood why his friend looked conflicted.
Most Voids were limited to a few simple jobs that required no magic.
One of those jobs was animal caretaker.
Darb had dreamed of doing that for as long as Zann had known him.
"I understand," he told Darb. "But Magica will still need animal caretakers even if all the Voids get magic."
"Maybe," Darb said. "But . . . I'm used to being a Void. I actually don't mind it."
Zann was shocked. How could anyone not want magic?
Still, Darb was his friend, so Zann didn't question him.
Instead he flashed a smile at Darb and changed the subject.
"Do you think Laddno can really do what he's promising?"
"I doubt it," Gliss said. "That guy says Laddno has some secret knowledge.
But nobody knows for sure if the Source is real."
"I read that it might be deep beneath Mount Mystery," Perda said.
"Or maybe inside the Cave of the Unknown."
"If the Source is in the Cave, then Laddno is out of luck," Zann pointed out.
"The Cave was destroyed, remember? Let's get home before Boz starts to worry about us."
When the kids reached Zann's house, a magical note was floating in the living room.
"It's from Boz," Zann said. "Venna called another meeting.
Boz won't be back for several hours."
Perda's eyes widened. "This is our chance to help Ello!"
Zann swallowed. He knew Boz would be furious if he ever found out that the kids had gone out again.
Zann quickly pushed that thought out of his mind and checked his pocket to make sure the guidelink was still there. "Let's go."
They headed back outside. Zing tried to come with them, but Darb convinced the dragon to stay behind.
"Maybe I should stay too." Gliss looked pale.
"I swore I'd never go near a wormhole again!"
"You'll be fine." Perda grabbed her hand. "Let's zap straight to Wormwood."
Wormwood was as creepy as ever. A variety of makeshift huts huddled around the central green where a gnarled and ancient tree grew.
The wormhole at the tree's base wasn't visible, but Zann remembered exactly where it was.
On the way to the tree, they passed Wyssa's old hut.
An older man with gray hair sat outside.
He stared suspiciously as the kids went by.
Suddenly there was a growl from the tent next door to Wyssa's hut.
A small silver dragon leaped out, spitting shards of ice.
"Eek!" Gliss cried. "Stay back!"
"Sorry!" A young man hurried out of the tent and grabbed the dragon. "She won't hurt you."
"Hey, it's you!" Perda blurted out. "The guy from the meeting."
The man brushed his wild hair to the side.
"Oh, were you there?" he asked in a friendly voice.
"I hope you enjoyed it—especially you." He smiled at Darb. "You're a Void, aren't you?"
"You live here?" Zann said before Darb could answer. He peered past the man.
Piles of strange items filled the tent.
Other items lay in the grass outside the tent.
"Yes, home sweet home." The young man noticed Zann's red hair and frowned.
He turned back to Darb and Perda.
"Some mess, hmm? I brought home a bunch of stuff from the meeting."
"We should go." Gliss sounded nervous as she glanced toward the tree.
The man ignored her. "Are you interested in joining our group?" he asked Darb.
"We can use more help to get the word out about Void Rights."
Zann expected Darb to mutter "no thanks."
Instead Darb cleared his throat. "Did you say you brought back some things from the meeting?" he said.
"I'd, uh, love to see that boat again."
"Of course!" the man exclaimed. "Our mission is to share new kinds of magic with everyone.
Come in and look at it all you like."
"Actually I was hoping to borrow the boat for a while," Darb said. "I'd like to study it."
The man looked uncertain. "It's the only one we have.
Laddno went to great personal trouble to acquire it."
"I wouldn't need it for long," Darb added quickly.
"I'd be happy to bring it back to Laddno campaign headquarters tomorrow to discuss how I can help the cause."
The man still looked hesitant. But finally he smiled. "I suppose that would be all right."
Soon the deflated boat was draped over Darb's shoulders. The kids hurried toward the tree.
"What was that all about?" Zann asked.
Darb smiled slyly. "We're going to Skellia, right? A drowning world with weak magic?
I thought a boat that doesn't require magic might come in handy."
"Good thinking, Darb!" Perda said. "Now we won't have to use magic to create a raft."
"And that means we won't attract the gulpers." Zann shivered, thinking of the magic-eating creatures that swam in Skellia's waters.
When Zann and his friends approached the tree, the wormhole spun open.
"I was hoping the wormhole had disappeared," Gliss joked weakly.
"Not this one," Zann said. "It's been here for a long time."
Perda laughed. "Hey, maybe the Source is located right here under this spooky old tree with its super powerful wormhole!"
"Who knows?" Zann snapped his fingers. A Shackle spell linked the friends' hands together.
Zann stepped toward the wormhole. "Let's go!"
Zann felt dizzy as he and his friends tumbled through the vortex.
Lights flashed and strange worlds passed by.
Slowly he reached into his pocket and pulled out the guidelink.
"Give me that!" Perda called over the whooshing sound of the vortex.
"I think I can make it work."
"I hope you're right!" Zann placed the device in her hand.
He wished he'd paid more attention when his parents were explaining the device's abilities.
Perda fiddled with the guidelink.
"What are you doing?" Gliss asked her.
"I'm supposed to rub it to create friction," Perda said.
"Then I focus on what type of magic I want it to find.
It should pull us toward any world nearby that matches my thoughts."
She frowned. "But so far nothing is happening!"
"You have to figure it out!" Gliss sounded frantic.
"Otherwise we could end up flying through the vortex forever!"
Suddenly Perda swerved toward one of the wormholes, dragging her friends with her.
Zann grabbed the wormhole's edge. Instantly the wormhole pulled them in and spat them out on the other side.
Zann held his breath, expecting to splash into the stormy waters of Skellia.
Instead he landed on wet ground. "Oof!" he blurted out.
Gliss sat up and rubbed her head. "Ouch," she said.
Then she looked around. "Hey, this isn't Skellia."
"Not unless the oceans disappeared since we were here," Darb said.
The world they'd landed in looked similar to Magica.
They were in a forest clearing, with tall trees shading the light of a bright orange sun.
Birds swooped overhead, and an insect buzzed in the grass nearby.
"Oh well." Perda sighed. "I guess I'm still figuring out how the guidelink works."
"At least this world looks nice and peaceful." Gliss peered around.
Then she wrinkled her nose and looked down.
"It's kind of soggy right here though.
Let's find a drier spot to rest and regain our energy."
Zann nodded. It took a lot of energy just to stay conscious in the vortex.
They usually had to rest before they could travel again.
"Wait! Don't go anywhere yet," Darb said.
"We need to pay attention to landmarks so we can return to the wormhole when we're ready."
"Oops. Good point," Zann said. As usual, the wormhole had spun shut as soon as they'd moved away from it.
Now it was only visible as a tiny ripple in the air.
If Zann hadn't known it was there, he wouldn't even have noticed it.
"I see a crooked tree over there, and some blue flowers," Gliss said.
"Good," Perda said. "We'll definitely be able to spot that tree again.
Now let's go uphill. It should be dry there."
She led the way up a gentle slope.
Soon they reached a sunny clearing. Zann flopped onto the dry ground and looked at Perda.
"So why didn't the guidelink work?" he asked.
She shrugged and sat down beside him.
"I think I know what I did wrong," she said.
"I was focusing on the gulpers from Skellia, since they probably have the most magic on that world.
But when Gliss said the thing about flying through the vortex, I thought about birds."
Darb watched a bright purple bird land nearby and peck at some yellow flowers.
"There definitely are a lot of birds here," he said.
"Maybe they're the source of this world's magic."
"They could be," Zann agreed. Then he frowned.
"Uh-oh. Do you think our magic will work here?"
"I hope so, or we won't be able to open the wormhole!" Gliss' eyes widened.
"We'd better test it. I'll conjure us something to drink."
She snapped her fingers. Blink!
Zann felt a sudden surge of magic energy.
At the same time, the entire landscape around them changed!
The sunny meadow had disappeared. They were now sitting in the shade of several large trees.
A small flock of multicolored birds perched on a squat shrub with shiny blue leaves.
Zann gasped and jumped to his feet.
"What happened? Did we accidentally zap somewhere else?"
"I don't think so." Darb looked around.
"We're still on a hill. And the position of the sun hasn't changed.
I think we're in the same exact spot."
"But everything around us looks different!" Perda said. "The trees, the birds . . ."
"That must be how magic works in this world," Darb said.
"Gliss' magic friction changed the landscape around us."
"Yeah." Zann gulped. "I wonder if it made that crooked tree move around too.
We might not be able to find the wormhole without it."
"Oh no," Gliss said. "What about the wormhole itself?
What if it moved? What if it's gone?"
Perda held up the guidelink. "This is supposed to be able to locate strong sources of magic, right?
Maybe it can lead us back to the wormhole."
"Do you know how to make it do that?" Darb asked.
"No." Perda bit her lip. "But I'll figure it out."
She rubbed the guidelink. Blink!
The landscape changed again. Now the kids found themselves standing among bushes with spiky leaves.
Nearby several large, six-legged creatures with shaggy fur sniffed around in the grass.
"Hmm," Perda said. She rubbed the guidelink again. Blink!
Now a deep, tangled forest surrounded the kids.
Blink!
Again the scenery changed. Now the open meadow was back.
But instead of birds, there was a swarm of large insects buzzing around a tree with purple bark.
"Stop!" Gliss grabbed the guidelink out of Perda's hand.
"Every time you create friction, the landscape changes!"
"Sorry." Perda looked nervous.
Zann knew how she felt. It seemed like they couldn't use magic in this world at all—not without getting lost.
So how were they going to find their way back to the wormhole?
While Zann, Perda, and Gliss were beginning to panic, Darb appeared calm.
"Don't worry," he said. "I think I can get us back to the wormhole."
"How?" Gliss cried. "We can't use magic!"
Darb smiled. "I can't ever use magic. I'm used to living without it. Give me a minute."
He squinted up toward the sun and then glanced around.
"What's he doing?" Perda whispered.
Zann shrugged. "Let's wait and see."
