Gliss frowned. "But there are no wormholes in the Far Frontier."
"Never mind that," Perda said.
"How are we going to get into Wormwood, past that weird, sticky Shield spell?"
Zann grinned. "You just answered your own question," he told her.
"We can go in through the wormhole!"
"The wormhole is dangerous!" Gliss cried. "There must be another way into Wormwood."
"No, Zann is right," Perda said.
"We can't waste time. Morb is already taking over Magica!"
"How will we reach a wormhole?" Darb asked.
"There's one in the palace, but there's no way we can sneak in there."
"There's one in Edgewood," Perda said. "Wyssa brought us there once."
"Perfect," Zann said. "Let's zap there now."
A moment later they stood in front of the Edgewood wormhole.
"Are you sure this is a good idea?" Gliss asked.
"We don't have the guidelink anymore. How are we going to navigate through the vortex?"
Perda frowned. "Good question. It could take a long time to find our way to the Wormwood wormhole."
"If we can find it at all," Darb said.
Zann shrugged. "Do you have a better plan?
We're wasting time arguing about this."
"We'll waste even more time if we get lost in the vortex," Gliss said.
"I think we should—Wyssa!"
The old woman had just zapped into sight nearby.
"There you are!" Wyssa exclaimed.
Surprisingly, she seemed glad to see everyone.
"What are you doing here?" Zann asked.
"Are you trying to escape through the wormhole?"
"No, I was looking for you, actually," Wyssa said.
"I have something important to tell all of you—especially you."
She jabbed a finger toward Zann.
"Okay, what is it?" he asked.
Wyssa opened her mouth to reply.
But just then Gliss let out a scream. "Trolls!" she cried.
Zann spun around. Half a dozen trolls were charging toward them.
"Let's get out of here!" Wyssa shouted.
She grabbed Zann with one hand and Darb with the other.
Zann had just enough time to grab Zing's tail before the whole group dived into the wormhole.
They weren't in the vortex for long.
Before Zann could catch his breath, Wyssa tugged them toward another wormhole.
Seconds later they emerged in Wormwood.
"Whew!" Gliss exclaimed. "That was quick."
Zann looked around. "Uh-oh," he said. "More trolls are coming!"
Several trolls had been lounging in the shade of the Wormwood tree.
Now they hurried toward Zann and the others.
Zing flew up and whistled his distinctive song.
The trolls slowed down and craned their necks toward the little dragon.
"Hurry!" Perda whispered. "Let's hide while Zing distracts them."
She led the way into a large hut nearby.
A moment later the trolls seemed to lose interest in Zing.
They blinked, looked around, and then wandered off and disappeared into a different hut.
"They're so stupid that they forgot what they were doing," Zann whispered.
"Never mind that." Perda was peering out the door. "There's the contraption!"
Zann couldn't believe he hadn't noticed it right away.
It was near the gnarled old tree, just to one side of the wormhole.
"It looks so evil!" Gliss whispered with a shiver.
Darb nodded. "It doesn't look much different than it did when we saw it in the Far Frontier."
"Yes." Wyssa sounded relieved.
"It's still not finished. Otherwise we would be too late to stop Morb."
"How do you know it's not finished?" Perda asked.
"That's what I started to tell you." Wyssa glanced at Zann.
"I'm pretty certain that Morb plans to place the Mask of Zanta in the empty space on top.
That's the most powerful relic there is. If we don't stop him, the results will be—"
"Don't give away the surprise, Wyssa," a voice interrupted.
Zann spun around. "Morb!" he exclaimed.
The villain had just stepped out of the shadows at the back of the hut.
Zann turned again, planning to run.
But several trolls now blocked the hut's one opening.
"Don't even think about trying to zap away," Morb warned.
"The spell I've placed over Wormwood won't allow that."
He pointed a finger toward Zing, who was already whistling again.
The little dragon dropped like a rock.
"Hey!" Darb cried. "Immobilization spells are illegal!"
"Haven't you caught on yet?" Morb sounded amused.
"The old rules don't apply anymore.
I'm in charge now, and that means that I make the rules!"
He reached into his robe and pulled out the Mask of Zanta.
Wyssa gasped. "You can't!"
"Silence, old woman." Morb held up the Mask, studying it.
"It's beautiful, isn't it? Terrifying, but beautiful."
"It's beautiful," Wyssa snapped. "But it's wasted on that thing out there."
"My contraption?" Morb raised an eyebrow. "What do you mean?"
"I thought you would try to take over Magica again," Wyssa said.
"But there's no way you can do that with a travel contraption."
"A travel contraption?" Perda echoed. "Is that what it is?"
Morb chuckled. "Yes, the crazy old woman is correct," he said.
"But don't fret. I doubt anyone will be disappointed by what I have planned.
Horrified, yes, but not disappointed.
The only thing that contraption has to do is get me safely through the wormhole."
He pointed one bony finger toward the tree.
"And then pull the Wormwood tree in after me."
"No!" Wyssa blurted out.
Zann was confused by Wyssa's panic.
Did it really matter if Morb took the Wormwood tree through the wormhole?
Morb laughed. "So you finally figured it out, hmm?" He taunted her.
"It sure took you a long time, Wyssa."
"What is it?" Gliss asked. "What did you figure out?"
Wyssa looked grim. "That tree. It's the Source."
"Huh?" Zann said. "The source . . . You mean the Source of all magic?"
"The Source is real?" Perda said.
"Oh, yes, it's real." Morb sounded pleased with himself.
"That tree pulls all of Magica's energy from the vortex."
"But that means . . ." Zann began slowly.
"It means," Wyssa said, "that removing it would leave Magica with no magic energy at all!"
Zann's head spun. Morb was going to steal all of Magica's magic energy!
Morb chuckled. "I can understand why you're all upset."
He turned to face Darb. "Except for you, perhaps.
Voids like you can rule Magica now.
You'll never have to put up with being mistreated again."
He scowled for a moment, his eyes angry and faraway.
Then he glanced at Wyssa. "By the way, you can mark this off as another world that you've destroyed."
"Huh?" Zann said. "You can't blame her for what you're doing."
"Oh, but I can." Morb smirked.
"She taught me everything she knew about magical contraptions."
Zann traded a confused look with his friends.
What was Morb talking about?
"I thought magical contraptions were invented right here in Magica, during the Old Times," Perda said.
"Don't they teach you kids any real Magica history?" Morb rolled his eyes.
Zann turned to Wyssa. "What is he talking about?"
Wyssa looked pale. "It's true. During the Old Times, the vortex was much smaller.
Many worlds had yet to develop, or to connect to the others."
"Yes," Morb said. "That made the vortex much easier to navigate."
"Indeed." Wyssa nodded.
"Back then people from different worlds shared their ideas and techniques.
Many of the relics from the Cave of the Unknown came from other worlds."
"Like the Horn of the Otherworld," Darb said.
"It came from a beast from another world, right?"
"Yes," Wyssa said. "And many forms of magic originated in other worlds, including the contraptions that Morb has built."
"But the idiots who took over during the Days of Discipline banned those types of magic," Morb said.
"They didn't want magic to be available to everyone. They wanted to control it."
"That's not why they banned those types of magic," Wyssa said.
"It was because old King Zanta, the last king of the Old Times, was an evil tyrant.
He used magical contraptions to control people.
He caused all sorts of chaos in Magica."
"I've read about that," Darb said.
"The people rose up against King Zanta.
That's how the Days of Discipline began."
"There's something else." Wyssa focused on Zann.
"You are a direct descendant of King Zanta himself."
Zann gasped. "Really?"
His friends looked stunned. Even Morb seemed surprised.
"Are you inventing lies to distract me, old woman?" he demanded.
"Not at all. That's why their names are similar," Wyssa said.
Zann shook his head slowly.
"Mom said my name was an old family name." He gulped.
"I never asked where it came from though."
"She probably doesn't know its full history," Wyssa said.
"Most of that era has been long forgotten."
"Enough of this talk," Morb spat out.
He touched his fingers together and sent a sizzling blast of energy toward Wyssa.
Gliss screamed and the others gasped.
But Wyssa raised her hand and the blast bounced away, hitting a troll.
As the troll raced off, wailing in pain, Wyssa smirked.
"Nice try, Morb," she said. "You'll have to work harder than that to . . ."
Her voice trailed off as the sudden clicking of antennae filled the air.
Zann spun around. The hut was swarming with the same beetles he'd seen in the Far Frontier.
"No," Wyssa whispered, backing away.
She tripped over a rough spot of ground and fell.
"Wyssa!" Perda cried as the beetles swarmed over the old woman.
"Get them off!" Zann yelled.
He grabbed at one of the insects.
But the beetle slipped away before he could get a grip.
"Use a Blast spell!" Perda rubbed her hands together to create friction.
But suddenly her movements slowed.
Zann tried to rush over to Perda.
But his body was moving in slow motion too!
"It's a spell." Gliss lifted a hand slowly and pointed at Morb.
Morb threw back his head and laughed.
"Oh, why didn't I think to use a Sloth spell on you kids before?
That would have saved me a lot of trouble!"
Zann slowly turned to look at Wyssa.
She was completely covered in bugs.
"What are those things, anyway?" Darb asked.
Morb smiled. "Ah, it's nice to see a Void with some curiosity.
Blank bugs are loosely related to dragons, though they have none of a dragon's cunning or individuality.
They're mindless drones with little intelligence and even less free will.
They only follow their basic instincts: move, eat, sleep." His smile widened.
"And thanks to Wyssa, every person on her home world now lives as a blank bug."
"What?" Perda said.
Morb grinned. "I lived there for a time, remember?
At first they welcomed me.
But as I gained knowledge and power, they turned against me.
So I tricked Wyssa into helping me build a contraption.
She had no idea what my plan was.
But I was able to use that contraption to alter the entire population.
Now they are all blank bugs!"
Gliss looked horrified. "Now we know why Wyssa freaked out when she saw those things earlier."
Zann shivered, imagining what it would be like to live as a mindless blank bug, or to know that people he cared about had to live that way.
"Maybe that's why she's so cranky all the time," Darb murmured.
Morb waved a hand. "Enough chitchat. I have work to do."
He strode out of the hut, throwing up a glowing green wall to block the entrance.
As soon as he disappeared, Zann felt the Sloth spell lift.
"Whew!" Perda shook out her arms.
"That spell felt weird. Now what are we going to do?"
She glanced at the beetles crawling over Wyssa.
The old woman wasn't moving.
"I don't know," Zann said.
"But we have to stop him, or Magica will lose all of its magic!"
Zann and his friends tried blasting through Morb's Shield spell, but it was too powerful.
Perda peered through the translucent green wall.
"Morb seems to be adjusting something on the contraption," she said.
"We have to stop him before he puts the Mask on it."
"I know." Zann paced around the hut.
"But how do we do that?"
Darb looked at Zann. "Wyssa said you're descended from King Zanta.
Since the Mask got its power from him, maybe you have some sort of connection to it."
Perda gasped. "That would be just like Wyssa's ring!"
Darb nodded. "Wyssa said her ring had been in her family for generations.
She used it to make her spells stronger.
Maybe you could control the Mask, Zann."
Zann didn't like being related to such a terrible tyrant.
But what if his friends were right? He had to try.
Zann stepped closer to the shield.
Morb was now carrying the Mask to the contraption.
Zann rubbed his hands together and focused on the Mask.
"Come to me," he murmured. The relic jumped in Morb's hand!
"What's going on?" Morb grumbled.
Zann focused all of his energy on the Mask. "Come to me."
This time the relic wiggled free of Morb's grip and flew halfway back toward the hut!
"Stop!" Morb roared. He sent a blast of magic after it.
The Mask hung in midair for a second and then flew back to him.
Morb glared at Zann. "Give up, boy! My powers are much greater than yours."
With a snap of his fingers, Morb shackled himself to the Mask.
Zann concentrated hard on the Mask.
"Wow!" Perda cried.
Morb's entire body slid backward toward the hut.
"How are you—oh, never mind!"
He rubbed his fingers together. Sparks flew.
Zann groaned as he felt Morb's magic fight back against his own.
"I can't drag him anymore," Zann grunted.
"His magic is too strong!"
A moan rose nearby. The pile of insects shifted slightly.
"Wyssa's still alive!" Perda exclaimed.
She tried to shove some of the blank bugs away, but more kept swarming in.
Zing woke up from the Immobilization spell.
He flew over, shooting flames at the blank bugs.
But they hardly seemed to notice their own bodies smoking.
"Stop, Zing! You'll burn Wyssa."
Darb glanced thoughtfully from the dragon to the blank bugs.
"But I have an idea. Morb said these insects are related to dragons, right?
Perda, can you try one of your fancy new spells to summon Teplo's sniffer goose?"
"Sure," Perda said. "Why?"
"That goose is a natural enemy of dragons," Darb said.
"Maybe she'll recognize these bugs as dragons too!"
"Do it quickly!" Zann cried. A magic blast hit him, knocking him down.
He sat up and saw Morb bent over, breathing heavily.
"I've tired him out," Zann thought.
Perda rubbed her hands together and murmured under her breath.
Suddenly the sniffer goose burst in through an opening in the hut.
When she saw the bugs, she honked and flapped toward them.
The blank bugs clicked with alarm and scurried out of the hut.
Slowly Wyssa sat up, moaning.
"Morb is walking toward the contraption again!" Gliss cried.
That seemed to bring Wyssa back to her senses.
She staggered to her feet and sent out a blast of magic energy.
The green wall blocking the hut’s entrance vanished.
"We have to stop Morb," she croaked.
Zann was already at the hut’s entrance, racing toward Morb.
"Get back, boy!" Morb snarled. "You can't—"
Zann leaped forward and shackled himself to the Mask and Morb.
When he touched the relic, a jolt ran through his body, almost knocking him over.
He braced himself, remembering how another relic had taken over his mind and almost driven him crazy.
But that didn't happen this time.
Zann was flooded with a power that felt perfectly natural.
He glanced toward his friends.
The trolls were blocking them from helping him.
"Zap!" he cried. He was hoping to zap himself, the Mask, and Morb away from the contraption.
He felt a tug, but he was unable to zap away.
Morb smirked. "Give up, Zann. You can't beat me—not this time."
Gritting his teeth, Zann tried to drag Morb away from the contraption with both his muscles and his magic.
Despite the extra energy surging into him from the Mask, he was tiring fast.
Morb was too powerful!
Morb sneered. "See what I mean? But perhaps my triumph can wait a few moments.
It will be a pleasure to watch all the energy drain out of you first.
Soon all of Magica will know how that feels!" He cackled with delight.
Darb finally managed to dodge around the trolls.
He edged closer. Morb spotted him and smiled.
"Ah, the little Void," he said.
"I like you, boy. You don't babble incessantly like your friends.
Why don't you come with me when I leave Magica?
I could use a servant." He winked.
"If you prove loyal enough, perhaps I'll even teach you a few of the tricks Wyssa taught me."
"Really?" Darb said.
Zann's jaw dropped. Could Darb actually be considering Morb's offer?
"Darb, no!" Gliss cried.
Morb chuckled. "Ignore them, boy," he said, reaching out toward Darb.
"Join me. You won't regret it."
"No, I won't," Darb said. He stepped closer.
"But you might regret some things soon!"
He yanked something out of his pocket and tossed it to Zann, who caught it automatically with his free hand.
Only then did he see what it was: the infusinator!
Suddenly more energy flowed into Zann. This could be his chance!
"Zap!" he shouted with every bit of energy he could muster.
Splash!
As Zann had hoped, he landed in the middle of the river near the palace, with Morb and the Mask still shackled to him.
"No!" Morb cried. "I can't—" A wave washed over his head.
Zann yanked him up. "What's the matter?" he said. "Can't swim?"
Morb glared. Then panic filled his eyes as he began to sink again. "Save me!"
Zann pulled the villain up out of the water.
"I'll rescue you, but only if you unshackle yourself from the Mask."
Anger burned in Morb's eyes.
But as more water splashed over his face, he looked nervous.
"How do I know I can trust you?"
"You don't know that," Zann said.
"But what choice do you have?
I'll let us both drown before I let you steal all the magic from Magica."
Morb glared at him again.
But when another wave washed over him, he whimpered and then snapped his fingers.
The magic shackles fell away.
Zann hesitated for a second, letting one last ripple of strong, wonderful energy run through him.
Then he unshackled himself from the Mask too.
The relic drifted away with the current.
Zann winced as the Mask smashed against a rock and broke into a dozen pieces.
The current swept them away.
"Help me!" Morb gurgled. "You promised!"
Zann dragged Morb out of the current to the shallows.
Then he rubbed the fingers of his free hand together to create energy for a Swelling spell, to make his voice louder.
"Help!" he called to the people in the palace square nearby.
"I need the palace guards over here!"
"Why don't we zap to the university instead of walking?" Gliss said.
Zann grinned at her. "I want to walk," he said.
"I never really got a chance to show you guys around First City before everything happened."
"True." Perda laughed. "This has been the craziest visit ever!"
Zann had to agree.
It was hard to believe that life was nearly back to normal less than two days after Morb's defeat.
Just hours after Morb's capture, the king and queen had reappeared and explained why they'd quit so abruptly.
Laddno had kidnapped one of the queen's young nephews and threatened to toss him into the vortex if the king and queen didn't step down.
Still, Zann couldn't help feeling sad.
Gliss' uncle Gar was planning to zap Gliss, Perda, and Darb back to Swamp Bottom the next day.
When would he see his friends again?
"It was fun watching Queen Venna's inauguration yesterday," Gliss said.
Perda nodded. "I'm glad they figured out that Laddno tampered with the vote toads."
"He never could have done it without Morb's help," Darb said.
Even though the king and queen had returned to the palace, they'd decided to retire.
They promised to do everything they could to support Queen Venna.
Gliss took Darb's hand.
"I think Venna will make a good queen.
For one thing, she's promising to meet with the leaders of the Void Rights groups."
"Not Laddno," Perda said. "The real leaders."
"We're here," Zann said as they reached the entrance to the university campus.
"Are you sure you want to see this?"
Perda nodded. "I want to see for myself that he can't get free."
Gliss and Darb nodded too.
At one end of the campus, there was an enormous, clear cube.
A small island sat in the middle of it, surrounded by deep water.
The island contained a chair, a table, a cot—and Morb.
He sat slumped in the chair, looking miserable.
The prison cube had been Teplo's idea.
It was laced with spells—some that provided Morb with food and other basic necessities,
and some that ensured that he couldn't break out or communicate with anyone.
"If he tries anything evil, we'll know right away," Zann said.
"Let's go. My parents are expecting us at the lab."
"Why do they want us to come to the lab, anyway?" Gliss said as they walked.
"Maybe they need our help cataloging the relics, now that Mari isn't around anymore," Perda said.
Zann felt sorry for Mari, who'd gone into hiding along with most of her family.
Queen Venna had sentenced Laddno to a year of hard labor on the slopes of Mount Mystery.
"I'm glad all the relics were recovered," Perda said.
"Boz says they even managed to fish all the pieces of the Mask of Zanta out of the river."
"I wonder what they'll do with the relics now," Gliss said.
When they stepped into the lab, there was a burst of lights and music.
"Surprise!" many voices cried.
Zann grinned. The place was packed.
His parents and Boz were there, along with Teplo, Fala, Gliss' uncle, and many other people.
Even Maff was there.
"We wanted to throw your friends a going-away party," Nax explained.
"And also a thank-you party for saving Magica."
"Again!" Fala added.
"Thanks," Zann said. "You didn't have to do this."
"Sure we did. And there's more. These are for you."
His mother handed each of the kids a silver twig with a crystal on the end.
"Are these from Atmo?" Zann asked.
His father grinned. "It's our latest invention."
"Wyssa helped us before she left Magica," Asta said.
"They're called zap accelerators," Boz said.
"They'll allow you to travel between First City and Swamp Bottom with a single zap.
Now you kids can visit each other whenever you like!"
Zann was so stunned that he couldn't speak for a second.
The past couple of weeks had been strange and often scary.
But this was the best happy ending—and surprise extra birthday gift—that he could ever have hoped for!
"Wow, thanks!" he exclaimed at last.
His heart swelled with good feelings. "Now let's party!"
